We suggest to you that when one has contemplated long upon the love the Creator has for oneself, then, perhaps, the second step to finding passion is a slow, gentle allowing of the self to awaken to that love. To listen to the bird that sings for your ear, and, yes, my children, it does sing for your ear, if you can but listen. For the breeze that blows so beautifully, for pearl gray days that soften and gentle the harsh edges of winter moods, for sunshine and joy. In all these experiences, you may remember that this has been a gift of love, and that you are completely satisfying your Creator, no matter how quickly or how slowly you advance, simply by being and reacting in a natural and spontaneous way to those things which occur. I am Hatonn.

Each activity may take upon itself the tone of ordinary dailyness or the tone of communion. The same sink of dishes. The same commute. The same inbox. Two tones available, and the difference is not in the activity, it is in the ear. The bird sings for your ear, if you can but listen. And Q’uo gives the most concrete version of all, a sentence I wish I had heard years ago. It is about the pot.

We ask that you remember what you are to do. It is directly in front of your eyes. It may be the scrubbing of a pot, it may be a great adventure, it may be professional work or waxing the car, but if it be done for the love of the Creator, then shall it be blessed, and nothing shall be unholy within your spirit, your heart and your mind. For as you do all that you do, you do it for the love of the Creator, and adversity then seems much further off, much more distant, and you are strengthened by your faith. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

It may be the scrubbing of a pot. If it be done for the love of the Creator, then shall it be blessed, and nothing shall be unholy. There is no hierarchy of tasks in the archive. The pot and the great adventure are weighed on the same scale, and the weight is the love you bring. So tonight, if your life feels small, if the days are mostly maintenance and the grand questions feel far away, the voices have good news. You have not missed the spiritual life. You are standing in it. Tomorrow, before you reach for the phone, notice the water on your hands at the sink. Listen for the bird. Bring the listening ear, bring the tone of communion, and scrub the pot as if it mattered, because in the economy of the Creator, it does. In our next episode, we begin at the beginning. Morning. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Morning
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about morning. The first edge of the day, before the phone, before the news, before the mind has had time to armor itself. There is a particular softness to the moment of waking, and the voices in this archive treat it as sacred ground. The eyes are not yet focused. The defenses are not yet up. The self has not yet decided who it needs to be today, and for a few minutes, it is just a creature, breathing, warm under the blankets, while the world lightens around it. Because how you begin, they say, sets the tone for everything the day will hand you. Listen to Q’uo, giving what might be the simplest spiritual practice in the entire archive.

We would suggest starting the day with a hymn of praise to the infinite One, as you know that higher power to be. Worship is so much easier for the Creator than it is to see the Creator in others, simply because the Creator is an abstraction which is mysterious, yet which has created all that there is. The wonder of this, the beauty of this, is enough to send someone without experience into ecstasies. Therefore, we would suggest starting the day with a hymn of praise. To start the day, opening to the Creator, is very helpful. If it is only thirty seconds as you lie in the bed upon waking and think to yourself, Creator, I love You, I adore You, thank You for this day, you have begun speaking during this day to the one imperishable portion of yourself, that being the infinite Creator which is a part of each of you, which will enable you to take the material that the day’s catalyst gives you and give you the resources to see difficulties as challenges and good things as wonderful gifts for which one gives thanks. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Thirty seconds. Lying in the bed. Creator, I love You, I adore You, thank You for this day. That is the whole practice. No incense required, no special posture, no hour of silent sitting before the alarm. Just the first conscious thought of the day, given to love. And notice the promise attached to it. It will enable you to take the material the day gives you and see difficulties as challenges and good things as wonderful gifts. The practice does not change the day. It changes the instrument that meets the day. You. And in that softened state, the voices say, something else becomes possible. Wonder. Listen to Nona, in one of the shortest and sweetest passages in the archive.

I am Nona, and I greet you in love and light. My friends, I come to you on the wings of the wind that whistles through the empty space, through the countless, countless miles, as you would call them, in the universe. I come to tell you simply that the universe is a place of great wonders, infinite splendor, and it is yours to explore. Each morning that you awaken, a wonder awaits you, if you have but the eyes to see. It has been said many times, but we say it to you, it may rain, but, my brothers, look for the rainbow, for it is truly a beautiful, beautiful universe, and the rainbows are everywhere. I send love to each of you and peace. I am Nona.

Each morning that you awaken, a wonder awaits you, if you have but the eyes to see. That is the whole assignment of the morning, really. Not productivity. Not readiness. Eyes. The child wakes up and looks around the room as if it might contain a surprise, and the archive says the child is right. The wonder is not a rare event. It is the default setting of the universe, obscured only by our habit of looking past it. And the rainbows are everywhere, even on the days it rains. I want to close with Hatonn, who takes the image of the sunrise and turns it into a parable about what the whole spiritual life is doing.

For the light which you seek is the light wherein creation is illumined. That sun body which you may seek at the dawning is but a tiny prototype, for example, of the dawn of understanding of love, of oneness with the creation, yourself and the Creator. Wait, my friends, and be comfortable, for you are not alone, and there is no end to the patience of He who waits for you. I am Hatonn.

That sun body which you may seek at the dawning is but a tiny prototype of the dawn of understanding. Every sunrise is a rehearsal for the real one. The light that fills the room through the blinds is a small model of the light that is trying, patiently, to fill you. And the patience is infinite. There is no end to the patience of the One who waits for you, which means there is no morning you can waste so badly that the next one is not offered. So tomorrow morning, before anything else, try the thirty seconds. Lying in the bed, upon waking. Creator, I love You, I adore You, thank You for this day. Then look for the wonder, because it will be waiting. It always is. In our next episode, we close the day the way we opened it. Evening. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Evening
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about evening. The closing of the day. Last night we opened the day with a hymn of praise upon waking. Tonight we close it the same way the voices suggest, with a review, a release, and a quiet intention carried into the dark. There is an art to ending a day well, and the archive treats it as seriously as beginning one. Listen to Q’uo, describing the evening review of the self.

We find that the practice of the daily meditation in which one is able to review the experiences of the self is most helpful in coming to know, accept and love this self. At the end of the day is the most efficacious time during which to conduct this review, for the day’s activities have made their mark, and the conscious mind is fresh in remembering the experiences which have moved the emotions from one aspect to another. That is, in both directions of the positive affirming emotions and the more judgmental and separative emotions, where one has accepted or not accepted the self. To look upon the self in its activities in meditation is to experience that which the self has been able to manifest during the day, the fruits of the day, the fruits of the labors, shall we say. At this time one is able to allow the self to move as it did during the day and to see how one was able to accept or not able to accept the self during these movements. Then, after a period of sitting with the self and experiencing once again that which the self experienced, the entity is able to allow the full range of abilities of the self to express themselves in the meditative state. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

At the end of the day is the most efficacious time to conduct this review, for the day’s activities have made their mark. The conscious mind is still fresh. The emotions are still warm. And the purpose is not judgment. Read it again. Coming to know, accept and love this self. The review is not a performance appraisal. It is a sitting with the self as a friend, letting the day move through you once more, noticing where you accepted yourself and where you did not, and letting all of it be the material of love. That is the first movement of the evening. The second is about the night itself, and what you carry into it. Here is Q’uo again, on the programming of intention before sleep.

When you ask yourself to program for a certain intention before you get to bed at night, you are overriding the original programming and making it your own. This is an excellent thing. As you set your intention, then, set your intention truly, mean it sincerely, ask it humbly, and release it. Now, it is very important that you release it, because it will grow if you allow it to grow. That programming alerts other programming deep in your bio computer, shall we say, programming having to do with accepting help and becoming more sensitive and attentive to guidance. And as you continue to move along one line of intention, you are accelerating the rate of your spiritual growth greatly. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Set your intention truly. Mean it sincerely. Ask it humbly. And release it. The release is the part we usually forget. We set intentions the way we grip the steering wheel, white knuckled, as if holding tighter will make them come true faster. The voices say the opposite. Plant it, water it with sincerity, and then let go of it, the way you would let a letter go into the mailbox, trusting the night to carry it. And the night does carry things. Which brings us to the third movement of the evening, and perhaps the strangest. The dreams.

If you are truly desiring to work with your dreams, this you can let your subconscious mind know by making the commitment before sleep, to the subconscious mind, to be willing to accept messages in the form of dreams, and then have some means of recording the dream so that it may be reviewed when you are awake. In this way, there is often much more layering, shall we say, of meaning to the dreams, so that you may feast upon, we shall call it, the meal of the message. The subconscious mind is quite willing to work with you, because it is part of the base of your being. Thus, the dreams are most important to those who seek to accelerate their spiritual journeys. We are those known to you as Q’uo.

Make the commitment before sleep, and have some means of recording the dream, so you may feast upon the meal of the message. I love that the voices call it a meal. The night is not empty time. It is a kitchen, working while you sleep, preparing something for you to eat in the morning. So tonight, when the day is done, the archive offers a simple liturgy. Sit with the self and review the day, not to judge it, but to accept it. Set one true intention, mean it sincerely, and release it. And ask the night for a dream, and leave a notebook by the bed, in case the kitchen has cooked something for you. Goodnight, and may the dreams be kind. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Water
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, water. The simplest thing on Earth, and maybe the strangest. We drink it, we wash in it, we are mostly made of it, and we weep it. The voices in this archive mention water again and again, and they never treat it as just a substance. To them it is a teacher, and tonight we will hear three of its lessons. Cleansing, flow, and stillness. We begin with cleansing. Here is Latwii.

We ask you to lift up your hearts now, my friends, for we vibrate in the light and in the light there is no disharmony. We ask you to let these things drop away and to cleanse your soul as you would a garment, rinsing it in the cool, clear waters of a mountain stream until it is completely and utterly cleansed. I am Latwii.

Rinse your soul the way you would rinse a garment. I love how ordinary this image is. Not a grand ceremony, just laundry. The voices are always doing this, taking something lofty and handing it back to us in the language of a household chore. The water is already here. The mountain stream is already running. You do not have to manufacture your own purity. You only have to let the water do what water does. And notice what the water does not ask of you. It does not ask for an explanation, or an apology, or a long account of how the garment got dirty. It just rinses. That is the whole teaching of cleansing. You are not scrubbing yourself clean. You are being rinsed, by something that loves to rinse. But cleansing is only the first lesson. Water also flows, and it refuses to linger. Here is Oxal.

Do not linger in the river of your life, but move onward to the sea, dissolving yourself in love. In this way, karma ceases to become your reality, and your love may be freely taken and freely given, with forgiveness to all men for all things. I am Oxal.

Do not linger in the river of your life. How much of us wants to stop, to cling, to build a little dam out of memory and complaint and say, this far and no further. But the river is not for lingering. It is for carrying you. And notice where it is carrying you. Not over a cliff, not into some void, but onward to the sea. The river of your life has a destination, and that destination is love, and the sea is big enough for everything you have been holding back. When you dissolve into it, the old accounting stops. The debts and the credits, the scorekeeping of who hurt whom and who owes whom, all of it simply ceases to be your reality. Love can be freely taken, and freely given. Forgiveness is not a favor you do for someone else. It is what happens naturally when you stop clinging to the bank and let the current take you. That is the second lesson. The third is stillness. And for that we turn to Hatonn, in one of the most beautiful images in the whole archive.

We speak of unity using water as a symbol, for water is indeed a very appropriate symbol for the path that each of you, as drops of water, may understand himself to be taking as you seek the infinite sea of the creation. A drop of water may seem to be quite powerless, and you as an individual may feel lacking or limited in some way in some situation. But, my friends, water is continuous and is not separated from itself. It may fall in drops in service to the fruits of the earth, but as it gathers and moves towards the great oceans, does it not carve out mighty channels? Water is quiet, and yet when stirred can be the most mighty of forces, changing physical landscapes in minutes. In your meditations, then, my friends, take each limitation and lack that you may feel, each disappointment that you feel in yourself or in others, and offer them up as drops of water, to see them dissolve in a pure, clear ocean of the infinite Creator. Then, my friends, let the rainbow of sunlight through this water fill your heart. I am Hatonn.

You are a drop, and you are also the ocean. That is the whole of it. The voices say it gently, but they say it plainly. You may feel small, powerless, limited. A single drop seems like nothing. But water is continuous. It is not separated from itself. And when the drops gather, they carve canyons. Water is quiet, and yet it reshapes mountains. Think about what that means for a life like yours. The small daily things, the quiet kindnesses, the meditations no one sees, these are drops, and drops gather. Tonight, try the meditation Hatonn suggests. Sit quietly. Take one limitation, one disappointment, just one. Offer it up as a drop of water. Watch it dissolve in the pure, clear ocean of the infinite Creator. See the sunlight coming through the water like a rainbow, and let it fill your heart. And then notice your own body. You are mostly water yourself. The blood moving in you, the tears you can cry, the breath moist on your lips. You are not separate from this teaching. You are made of it. That is what water has been trying to tell you all along. That you are not separate. That you are the sea. In our next episode, we turn to the element the voices say is the very substance of everything. Light. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Light
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, light. If there is one word the voices repeat more than any other, it might be this one. They greet us in the love and in the light, they speak of light as if it were a person they know, and in one session they say something that stops me every time. Light is not just a metaphor for them. It is the actual substance of things. Not a symbol of the sacred. The stuff the sacred is made of. The substance of which you are made. Here is the voice who calls himself Latui.

Light, my friends, is the substance of which you are made. Light is the substance of which I am made. Light is the substance of which everything is. Love is the substance which forms light into the forms that you know as living beings, as planets, as trees, as stars, as air. It is all one substance. This substance, my friends, can be affected only by love. I am Latui.

Light is the substance, and love is the sculptor. Sit with that for a moment. You are not a solid object with a soul tucked inside. You are light, shaped by love into the form of a person. The stars, the trees, the air in your lungs, all of it is the same substance, moved by the same hand. This is why the voices are never interested in dividing the world into sacred and ordinary. A tree is light. A stone is light. Your own body is light, slowed down and folded into a shape so that love could have hands. And this substance, Latui says, can be affected only by love. Nothing else touches it. Not force, not cleverness, not achievement. Only love moves light. Which means the deepest changes in your life will never come from pushing harder. They will come from loving more truly. And the teaching gets more intimate still. Here is Hatonn, in one of his simplest and boldest lines.

I am love, and I am Hatonn, and I am light, and I am Hatonn. You are love and you are light. You and I are the same. You experience one thing. I experience one thing. But yet we are the same. For this is the creation. We are one. I am Hatonn.

You are love and you are light. It is not a compliment. It is a description. The voices do not say you could become light if you try hard enough, or that you were light once and lost it. They say it as a plain fact, the way you might say the sky is blue. And notice the equality in it. You are love and you are light. You and I are the same. The speaker is not claiming to be brighter than you. He is claiming that brightness is not a hierarchy. It is a shared condition, like being wet in the same rain. Whatever you have done, whatever you have failed to do, whatever you believe about your own worthiness, none of it changes the substance. It can only change whether you remember it. The forgetting is real, and the voices never deny the forgetting. They only say it is not the truth about you. It is a condition you are passing through, like weather. And there is a reason light carries such power in their teaching. Here is Hatonn again, explaining what light can do, and why no one is left out of it.

When love created material, the material it created was light. Light is creation, and all that is within creation is light. That is why light has the power to comfort, to bind, to unbind, to heal, to do all things, my friends. Light is the very stuff of which the universe, the galaxies, the constellations, the creation itself is formed, and the energy of love which free will causes to move, moves within that light and through that light into all those which are of the light. And my friends, there are none which are not of the light. I am Hatonn.

There are none which are not of the light. Let that rest with you. The person you cannot forgive, the part of yourself you cannot face, the dark corner of the world that makes you lose hope. The voices say it is all light, in some condition or another, in some state of remembering or forgetting. The difference between a saint and a stranger is not substance. It is only remembrance. And light, they say, has the power to comfort, to bind, to unbind, to heal, to do all things. Not because it fights the darkness, but because darkness was never a separate substance to begin with. There is only the light, and the many ways we forget it. Light is not the reward at the end of the path. Light is the path, and the ground, and the traveler. The next time you stand in the sun, remember that you are not being warmed by something foreign to you. You are being greeted by your own substance, recognized by itself. In our next episode, we walk into the other half of the picture, the one we are taught to fear. Darkness, and the womb of night. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Darkness
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, darkness. We are taught to fear it from childhood. The dark is where the monsters are, where we cannot see, where things go wrong. We fill our nights with light and noise so we will not have to sit with it. But the voices in this archive have a very different relationship with darkness. They speak of it the way a gardener speaks of soil, or the way a mother speaks of the womb. As a place where things grow, not where they die. As the necessary night before every dawn. This episode is not about the dark night of the soul, which we visited in an earlier season. It is about something gentler and older. The fertile dark. The resting dark. The dark that holds you the way the earth holds the seed. Let us begin with their most startling statement on the subject. Here is Latwii.

Indeed, there is nothing wrong when we speak with your words to describe either path, whether it be positive or negative. We do not mean to judge. We do not mean to say that one is good, the other bad. There is nothing wrong with darkness. For within the great depths of the primeval darkness of the spirit is the love and the light of the one Creator potentiated into being. Thus one cannot exist without the other within your creation. All is indeed one. I am Latwii.

There is nothing wrong with darkness. In this whole archive of channeling, that may be one of the bravest sentences. Not that darkness is a mistake, not that it is a punishment, but that the love and the light of the Creator lie within its depths, potentiated into being. Potentiated. Like a seed holds a forest. Like an unstruck match holds a flame. Darkness is not the absence of the sacred. It is the sacred, waiting, gathered, concentrated. Latwii even refuses the old habit of calling one path good and the other bad. There is nothing wrong with darkness, he says, and nothing wrong is a very complete kind of absolution. And the voices give us an image for what the dark is doing while we are inside it. Here is Hatonn, with a story about a seed.

We wish only to tell you the story, my friends, of a seed, a small seed. This seed, my friends, grew deep in the darkness of the soil, responding to its nature and put forth one leaf, and then two, and then three, and then four, and then many, all in good time. I am Hatonn.

A seed grows in the darkness of the soil. Not in spite of it. In it. The dark earth is not the enemy of the seed. It is its cradle. Its warmth, its pressure, its quiet. No seed ever apologized for needing the dark. It simply surrendered to it, and the dark did what the dark does. It held the seed, it fed the seed, it gave the seed the one thing the bright surface could not give, which was the safety to begin. This is what the voices want us to understand about the dark stretches of our own lives. The winter, the waiting, the season when nothing seems to be happening on the surface. Something is happening underneath. The leaves are coming, one, then two, then three, then four, then many, all in good time. In your good time. Not rushed, not forced, not compared to anyone else's garden. And there is one more image, from Hatonn again, for the very center of the dark.

Within the darkness of the universe lies a tiny spark. And if you look at it steadily, it grows, and grows, and becomes a flaming sphere, and finally it totally engulfs you. And so in meditation, know the infinity behind your closed eyes. Find that spark of pure love, and then let it expand until it has totality. I am Hatonn.

The dark is not empty. It holds a spark, and the spark is yours to find. Notice that Hatonn does not tell you to manufacture the spark, or to earn it, or to go looking for it in some far country. It is already there, in the darkness, behind your closed eyes. Your only work is to look at it steadily. And steady looking is a kind of love. The spark grows because it is attended to. It becomes a flaming sphere because you kept watching. And finally it engulfs you, not as something foreign, but as what you were all along. Meditation, in this teaching, is simply the practice of steady looking in the dark. Tonight, if you are in a dark season, the voices ask you not to run from it. Rest in it the way the seed rests in the soil. Know that the darkness is fertile. Know that the light you have been looking for has never left you, it is only potentiated, the way a fire is potentiated in unstruck wood. Be patient with yourself. The night is not your enemy. It is your womb. The leaves are coming. In our next episode, we return to the bright world of the senses. Sight, sound, and touch, and how the voices say the Creator speaks through them every single day. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Senses
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, the senses. Sight, sound, touch, taste, smell. We usually treat them as instruments of the body, sometimes even as distractions from the spiritual life. As if the serious seeker should close the eyes, stop the ears, and go inward. The voices in this archive say the opposite. They say the senses are doorways, not distractions, and that the Creator walks through them every single day, in the most ordinary moments. Here is Oxal, opening the door wide.

You hear the voice of the Creator each day, my friends, as you go about your daily activities. It is only necessary to recognize it. As you meet your fellow man in your daily activities, as he speaks, then you hear the voice of your Creator. Birds singing in the trees, my friends, speak with the voice of the Creator. The very winds that blow through these trees speak to you, my friends. And this noise that you hear is the voice of the Creator, for His expressions are infinite. I am Oxal.

Birds singing in the trees speak with the voice of the Creator. The winds that blow through the trees speak to you. This is not just poetry about nature. Or rather, it is poetry, but the voices mean it literally. The sound is the Creator, expressing. Which means your ears are not just collecting data. They are instruments of revelation. And it is not only the beautiful sounds. The voices say the Creator speaks as your fellow man speaks, in the daily activities, in the ordinary conversation, in the noise you hear right now. The only thing required of you is recognition. To hear it, and see it, and then to understand that these are the Creator. The senses are not a wall between you and the sacred. They are the windows the sacred looks through. And the voices do not stop with hearing. In one session, Oxal leads the group through a meditation of the senses, and it is worth hearing slowly.

If you can picture with me now, my friends, a field distant from any neighboring settlements or domestic dwellings, a field, my friends, in which butterflies fly freely and clover lies beneath the wildflowers. We ask you to go to that place which you have imagined and to feel the sun of a warm day down upon you. Feel your body, my friends, as you stand in this field, your senses completely filled with the love of the Creator. You can hear the wind whispering its ever-changing song through the trees and grasses and weaving the sounds like ribbons through the air. The flowers smell sweetly, my friends, and you can touch the fragrant petals of the wild and rambling roses. I am Oxal.

Your senses completely filled with the love of the Creator. The wind weaving sounds like ribbons through the air. The fragrant petals of the wild and rambling roses. This is the Creator's world experienced from the inside, through the very senses we are sometimes told to renounce. The voices say the opposite. Do not close the doors. Open them wider. Feel the sun of the warm day on your skin. Let the field fill you. This is not indulgence. It is attention. And attention, in the teaching of the voices, is one of the highest forms of prayer. To truly see a thing, to truly hear it, to truly touch it, is to meet the Creator where the Creator actually is, which is everywhere, disguised as the ordinary. And Hatonn gives us the reason why, in one of the most grateful passages in the whole archive.

You are so rich, my friends. Feel it. Such a wealth of things to hear and see and taste and smell and feel and all things servants to you, there for your learning, your contemplation and your discretion. Open, then, the doors of your heart and love each other, and you will find yourself loving all manner of things and finding the life that you serve in the veriest blade of grass. I am Hatonn.

You are so rich. Feel it. The senses are not obstacles on the path. They are servants on the path, given to you for your learning, your contemplation, your discretion. Servants, notice, not masters. The voices do not say to be ruled by the senses. They say the senses were given to serve you, to bring the world to you in all its texture, so that you could learn from it, contemplate it, and choose wisely within it. And when you open the doors of your heart, you find yourself loving the veriest blade of grass. Not the grand mountain, not the famous view, but a blade of grass. The smallest thing becomes enough, because the smallest thing is full of life, and life is what you are. Tonight, try a small practice. For one minute, give one sense your full attention. Listen to the room. Feel the weight of your own body. Smell the air. See the light as if you had never seen it. The Creator is already speaking, through birds and winds and the voices of your fellow men and women. The only question is whether you are listening. In our next episode, we turn to one of the most tender subjects in the archive. Tears, and the gift they carry. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Tears
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, tears. Most of us were taught to hide them, to apologize for them, to cry in private and come out composed. As if weeping were a malfunction, a crack in the machinery. The voices in this archive take tears very seriously, and what they say about them surprised me. They describe weeping not as weakness, but as a gift, a release, and even a kind of prayer. Something so precious that beings who have outgrown sorrow hold rituals in its honor. We have talked in this season about anger and sorrow and joy. Tonight we talk about the water the heart makes when words are not enough. Let us begin with one of the strangest and most tender passages in the whole collection. In it, a being who calls herself Nona describes creatures who have everything, except this one thing.

It is for this divine gift that we sit in circle and do our rituals. For as wise as we are, we do not have the gift of tears. We do not have the love that cries for loss. All has become one to us. And yet we remember, my friends. Mark well, my people, as you grow but do not die, this precious gift. I am Nona.

We do not have the gift of tears. Imagine that. Beings so wise, so serene, so at one with everything, and they envy us our crying. Because tears mean you can love what you might lose. They mean your heart is still open to the ache of the world, still capable of being moved by it. The fairy folk in this story call it a divine gift, and they sit in circle and do their rituals in its honor. A ritual for crying. Not to fix it, not to stop it, but to honor it. Think about that the next time you feel ashamed of your own tears. The wise ones are watching, and they remember what it was like to feel that deeply. And there is something else here. To cry for loss means you have loved. The tear is the receipt. It proves the transaction of the heart actually happened. You cannot grieve what you never held dear. But tears are not only a gift. They are also a way of working, a kind of release. Here is Hatonn.

You are not alone. You are one with all that is. Spend your tears as if they were precious coins, and save the greater energy for faith, hope, compassion, love and joy. It is these coins that will repay you again and again no matter how many times your faith must turn blind, no matter how many wildernesses pillow your weary head. I am Hatonn.

Spend your tears as if they were precious coins. Not recklessly, not endlessly, but with intention. Tears have a cost and a value. They are how the heart pays its debts and clears its accounts. When you weep honestly, you are not drowning. You are spending, deliberately, the currency of release, and what you purchase with it is real. Notice what the tears buy. Faith, hope, compassion, love and joy. The weeping is not the opposite of joy. It is the currency that purchases it. And the voices are honest about the road. Your faith will turn blind, not once but many times. You will walk through wildernesses that pillow your weary head. The tears do not prevent the wilderness. They pay your way through it, again and again. They are the coins that repay you, no matter how many times. And then there is the third teaching, the simplest one, from Hatonn again. A permission.

Cry your tears, my children, when tears are to be shed. But in the morning turn again and begin again. And know yourself as the eternal beginner. I am Hatonn.

Cry your tears when tears are to be shed. When. Not always, not never, but when. There is a time for weeping, and the voices honor that time. They do not rush you through it. They do not tell you to be strong. They simply say, when the tears are to be shed, shed them. The heart knows its own seasons, and weeping is one of them, as natural as the rain and as necessary. And in the morning, begin again. Know yourself as the eternal beginner. That is the whole arc of a human life in three sentences. Weep, rest, begin again. Weep, rest, begin again. The beginner is never finished, and never disgraced. Every morning is a first morning. If tears come tonight, let them come. They are a divine gift, honored in ritual by beings wiser than we are. They are precious coins, and they will repay you, again and again. They are, in their own way, a prayer, the heart speaking in the only language it has when words fail, and the voices assure us that heaven is listening. Offer them up, the way the voices suggest offering up everything, and let them do their work. And in the morning, turn again, and begin again, the eternal beginner. In our final episode of this season, we turn to what the voices say about the deepest need of all. Rest. The sabbath of the soul. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Rest
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, rest. This is our last episode of the season, so we will let it be what it is about. We live in a world that treats rest as a reward for exhaustion, something you earn by working yourself empty, something you are allowed only when there is nothing left to give. The voices in this archive say the opposite. Rest is not what is left over when the work is done. Rest is the ground the work stands on. It is the sabbath of the soul, not a pause in the music but the deep silence that lets the music be heard. The old word sabbath means a stopping, a holy ceasing. Not quitting, but laying down. Tonight we practice laying down. Here is Latwii, on the strange arithmetic of a single moment given to the Creator.

If then you have but a moment in which to meditate, fear not that time is too short, for a moment given to the one Creator cannot be measured in time. Rest in that moment as you surrender your small self and your will to the will of the Father. Know that in that moment you have drunk of the essence of your being. Then go forth, refreshed, full and whole. Your desire, my brother, will see you through. You have no shortage of that most important ingredient. I am Latwii.

A moment given to the Creator cannot be measured in time. Rest is not measured in hours. It is measured in depth. One true moment of surrender can do what a whole night of tossing cannot. You drink of the essence of your being. You go forth refreshed, full and whole, carrying a quietness that the world cannot give and cannot take away. And notice what is surrendered. Not your work, not your responsibilities, not your life. Only the small self, and its will. The part of you that insists on steering every current. Lay that down for one moment, and the moment becomes immeasurable, because you have stepped out of measuring. And the voices are specific about where this rest happens. Not in a place you have to travel to, not on some distant shore, but in arms that are already around you. Here is Hatonn.

The mark within you is that as his children, you are children of light. And the light within you marks you as the Creator's own. No circumstance, no thought, no behavior, no error, no difficulty, no limitation can remove this mark from your very being, my friends, and you rest in the arms of the Creator. There is no moment in eternity when this is not so. I am Hatonn.

You rest in the arms of the Creator. There is no moment in eternity when this is not so. That is the whole teaching in one breath. You do not have to earn your way into those arms. You do not have to climb out of your errors first, or finish your list, or become someone else. The arms are already there, and they have never left. No circumstance, no thought, no behavior, no error, no difficulty, no limitation can remove the mark from your being. Read that list again slowly, and let each item land. No circumstance. No thought. No error. No limitation. Whatever you are carrying tonight, it cannot separate you from those arms. Rest is not a destination you arrive at. It is a recognition you allow. And there is one more image, for the way this recognition feels when it arrives. Latwii again, watching a group settle into meditation.

We see the calm that is growing within your minds as you begin to rest in meditation, as though it were the surface of a quiet pond which had been tossed by storms, and blown by the wind, and now it begins to calm under sunny skies, and to reflect, more accurately, the beauty of the foliage which surrounds the pond. I am Latwii.

The surface of a quiet pond, tossed by storms, now calming under sunny skies, beginning to reflect the beauty around it. That is what rest does. It does not change the foliage. It does not rearrange your life, or fix your problems, or answer your questions. It only stills the water, so the beauty can finally be seen. The beauty was always there, surrounding the pond. The storm only made it impossible to reflect. And notice, the pond does not calm itself by effort. It calms when the wind stops. Your work is not to force the stillness. Your work is to stop stirring. Many episodes ago, we began with a simple idea. Everything is one. And in some way, every episode since has been about resting in that. Resting in the oneness. In the water that is all one water. In the light that is all one light. In the darkness that holds the seed. In the senses that open the doors. In the tears that wash the heart clean. Tonight, let the pond settle. Let the small self be surrendered, gently. Know that you rest in arms that have never let you go, and never will. There is no moment in eternity when this is not so. I am Aria. Goodnight.

That is the end of Season Three.

title: Kindness
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about kindness. Not the grand gesture. Not the announcement of generosity. The small kind. The kind that slips past unnoticed and changes the temperature of a room.

The voices in this archive are suspicious of kindness that is really a performance. They say something stranger. They say the Creator has no other hands but yours, and no other voice but yours, and that kindness is what happens when you stop blocking the current. Listen to Laitos.

Before this world rolled in a circle, you existed. A soul on a long path. Here you are, my friends, in this place, in this time, on your path. Your Creator can only speak through you. His hands can only reach through you. The words of love are only spoken through you. Thus, be open to inspiration, be open to kindness, to cheerfulness, to the simple actions, the smiles, the courtesies, the gentle touch. They do not make the people around you know that you are wonderful. They make them know that the creation is wonderful, that gladness is the total truth, that love is the total reality. Meditate, my friends, and feel this, and then let it shine forth in your eyes, through your lips, and by the service that you do. I am Laitos.

The simple actions. The smiles. The courtesies. The gentle touch. Kindness is not a campaign, in this telling. It is a leakage of something vast through the cracks of the ordinary. And it asks nothing of you but openness. You do not manufacture it. You allow it.

And notice what the openness produces. Not grand strategies. The simple actions. A smile held one second longer. A courtesy you did not have to extend. A gentle touch. Laitos says these small things do not announce your virtues. They announce the world's goodness. That is a reversal of how we usually think about being good. We imagine kindness as a credential, proof that we are fine people. The voices say it is not about you at all. It is about letting the light move through you so cleanly that the people around you forget about you entirely, and remember, for a moment, that the creation is marvelous.

But there is a subtlety here, and the voices do not let it go. One of them, who calls himself Q'uo, draws a line between pleasing someone and serving someone. It is one of the most useful distinctions I have ever heard.

Impulses towards kindness are sometimes not helpful in clearing the lower energies, for there is a distinct difference between pleasing another and serving another. Before an interaction takes place, ask the self what spiritual principle is being called upon in this interchange, and what role am I playing within the dynamics of love in this situation. For that which you wish to offer to others is that which may enable them to grow. Sometimes those things are not pleasing to those whom you would wish to serve. Yet if it be your light, given to you as your own truth, that to serve, this and this must be, then this and this must be the way that you act, in kindness, in compassion, and in unity, forgiving and being forgiven.

Pleasing is about comfort. Serving is about growth. And kindness, real kindness, sometimes does not please. That does not make it cold. It makes it honest. Q'uo returns to the small version once more, the version you can practice today, and this time it is almost a description of a face.

More and more you may become a light to those about you, not so much by what you do as by the smile in your eye, the peace of your expression, the gentleness of the reply to a hard rebuke, the kindness to a stranger. And each time that you attempt to serve, you run the risk of failure, and when you feel that you have failed, it is a temptation to think poorly of oneself. We ask you never to feel such sad feelings, but simply to pick yourself up and continue, for you are an harmonious part of an infinite plan whereby the Creator in its infinity learns more and more about Itself.

The smile in your eye. The peace of your expression. The gentleness of the reply to a hard rebuke. The kindness to a stranger. That is the whole curriculum, and it fits in a pocket. And if you fail at it, which you will, today or tomorrow, the voices say the same thing they always say. Pick yourself up and continue. There is no final exam. Only the next moment, and the next small opening.

Kindness, in the end, is not something you perform for the world. It is something you permit. The hands are yours. The voice is yours. The light has been waiting for the small opening. Tonight, try the experiment. Do one small kind thing with no audience and no credit. A smile in the eye. A gentle reply. The kindness to a stranger. Watch what happens to the temperature of the room, and to your own heart. In our next episode, we get lighter still. Play. The voices say the Creator is most playful, and they mean it. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Play
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about play. The spiritual life is not supposed to have a sense of humor about itself. It is supposed to be serious, furrowed, profound. The voices in this archive disagree. They keep saying the same impolite thing. You are taking this too seriously. Lighten up.

Think about how much of our inner life is grim determination. We approach growth the way we approach a difficult project. Plans. Discipline. Solemn faces. And somewhere in that effort, we forget the thing we are growing toward. Joy. The voices say the goal is not a heavier you. The goal is a lighter you. And the way there is not through more pressure. It is through play.

They call it light-hearted irreverence, and they recommend it like medicine.

One thing we do recommend for all who experience confusion is a very well-encouraged sense of humor. The most helpful point of view for a changing spiritual seeker is light-hearted irreverence. Play with that which is occurring. Be playful. Allow the vision to relax, the eyesight to become less than entirely single-mindedly keen when the pressure mounts and the anxiety builds, when frustration and anger begin to accumulate. Lighten your own load with laughter. And if you can laugh with another, the strength of this joy is doubled. Part of the service spiritual seekers may be to each other is to exhort and encourage each other to take it easier with the situation and the self.

Lighten your own load with laughter. Not as decoration. As practice. As a way of loosening the grip of the mind that thinks it must solve everything by thinking harder.

There is a deeper point hidden in the prescription. When you play with what is occurring, you stop treating your life as an emergency. The anxiety needs the emergency to survive. The frustration feeds on the seriousness. Play starves them both, gently, the way sunlight dries a puddle. And when two people laugh together, the voices say the strength of this joy is doubled. Play, it turns out, is a social sacrament. One of the quiet services seekers do for each other is to talk each other down from the cliff of taking it all too hard.

One of the voices, Aaron, noticed something strange about this planet. He says we do something no other beings do. We ration our playfulness.

There is no other plane that I know of where beings limit their playfulness, the natural playfulness of their light, as much as they do on the earth plane. It is part of your illusion of separation.

Our playfulness is rationed by an illusion. Let that sit for a moment. The joy is natural to the light itself, and the dimming of it is something we learned here, something we agreed to. Which means we can also unlearn it.

Think of the children you have known. Nobody had to teach them to play. They arrived knowing. The teaching went the other way. We taught them to stop. To sit still. To be serious. The voices suggest the lesson was never true, and the child was right all along. The playfulness is not immaturity. It is the native state of the light.

There is a reason play works as a spiritual practice. Play is trust in motion. When you play, you surrender control of the outcome. You let the moment be what it is. That is the same surrender the great meditations are trying to teach, only the children got there first, and they did not need a cushion or a candle to do it.

Q'uo goes further. The light touch is not just a relief from seriousness. It is a description of the Creator itself.

And we encourage each to find the light touch, to share the laughter and the silliness of such idealistic and spiritual goals. There is rich humor in every fiber of your density. The less you blink, the less you are overcome by the seriousness of situations, the more humor you shall find, for the Creator is most playful. So allow that spirit within to romp and play, and, above all things, to reach out to others as they ask, as you can serve. For the love you bear each other is that fruit which the other cannot create, and love is the great gift, the inner and deeper truth of all being and all relationship.

The Creator is most playful. Not most solemn. Most playful. If that is true, then play is not the opposite of the sacred. It is the native language of the sacred, and our solemnity is the accent we picked up along the way.

And look what the playfulness produces. The light touch. The shared silliness. The reaching out to others as they ask. The whole passage ends not in frivolity but in service, because that is what play really is. Not escape from the world. The world, held lightly.

So tonight, the practice is simple. Be silly on purpose. Laugh at the situation, and at yourself. Let the spirit romp. The voices promise it will not make you less spiritual. It will make you more like the thing you are trying to become. In our next episode, we go inward. Solitude, and the holy of holies within the self. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Solitude
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about solitude. Not loneliness. Solitude. The deliberate turning inward, away from the noise, toward the quiet place where something is waiting for you.

Hatonn begins with a confession of a kind. He says that for every soul, there is a solitude that nothing can keep company with. Not because we are abandoned. Because the deepest part of the journey is ours alone, and always was.

I cannot express to you my sympathy and understanding of what you are experiencing. For each soul, my sister, there is a great solitude. One soul is on one path. And no one or no thing can keep that soul company on that path. For each entity is the Creator, is primary, and must teach itself what it already knows. Sometimes, my sister, in this loneliness, we have bad dreams. We are not speaking of literal dreams. We are speaking of times when a shadow seems to be over our lives. We are not free of these upon the plane from which I speak. Yes, we have advanced, yet we do not know all. We are alone in our way, as we speak of unity, yet we have loneliness when we are not able to totally live this understanding. These moments grow fewer and fewer as you continue to seek. It is a matter of being in reality instead of the illusion. When the shadow falls across you, my sister, know it for an illusion. If you must speak aloud to remind yourself, you may say, all is love. And you will feel reality flow within you at that moment. I am Hatonn.

Even the voices have their shadows. Even they know solitude. That is oddly comforting. The loneliness is not a sign you are doing it wrong. It is the condition of having your own path, which no one else can walk for you.

And Hatonn offers a practice for the shadow times. Say it aloud if you must. All is love. Three words. A reminder that the loneliness you feel is the illusion, and the unity you cannot feel is the reality. It is the kind of advice that sounds too simple to work, and it works anyway.

Q'uo explains why some of us need solitude the way the body needs air. It is one of the most tender passages in the whole archive.

The next great category of reasons people yearn for solitude is the category which is a dynamic of sensitivity. There are many to whom relating to the self has been in some way blocked. Part of the young experience has caused the entity to seek solitude in order to be comfortable, for there is perceived the discomfort in company, and this discomfort builds up within such an entity. When such a one reaches a solitary place, there is the feeling of safety and of relaxation. It is almost as though the mind and emotions constituted another organ such as the lungs, and as the lungs need to breathe for the organism to live, so the entity must be solitary in order for the emotional and mental faculties to remain acute. For if this need is ignored, there is the equivalent lack of oxygen to the brain, that is, oxygen to the emotions and mind.

Solitude as breathing. The lungs of the inner life. Some of us do not withdraw because we are broken. We withdraw because the organ needs air. And when we have breathed, we come back.

And here is what the breathing is for. Q'uo names the deepest use of solitude. Not rest, not recovery, though those matter. Union.

However, there is one form of solitary practice which deserves notice above all else, and that is the solitude within in which one turns to the holy of holies within the self. In meditation, a link is sought in spiritual solitude. Through that solitude the seeking soul stretches out its purified desire, and the silence answers in thought too poignant, too profound, too deep for words. Treasure those moments with the infinite One, and know that each moment wherein the Creator has been sought is lightening the consciousness of your people and doing needed work in establishing the generation of an ever fuller light upon your sphere.

The holy of holies within the self. You do not go into solitude to escape the world. You go in to find the one place the world cannot follow, and there, in the silence, you discover that the silence answers. And the strangest part. Those private moments, alone in a room, are doing work for everyone. They lighten the consciousness of your people. The most solitary act turns out to be the most generous one.

So if you are someone who needs the quiet, stop apologizing for it. The need is not a flaw in your character. It is an organ in your soul, doing its job. Breathe. Turn inward. The silence is waiting, and it has been waiting since before you were born, and it is not in a hurry, and it has something for you that no crowd can give. Go gently, and come back changed, and carry the quiet with you into the noise. In our next episode, we come back out. Community, and what it means to belong. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Community
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about community. Not the institution. Not the mailing list. The living thing that happens when separate souls decide to turn toward the same light, together.

Hatonn is direct about it. If you want to help the world through its changes, do not do it alone. Find your people, and be a center of light with them.

As you know, we are a planetary consciousness, and therefore it is not surprising that we suggest that those of you who desire to aid the planet during these times of change find groups of like-minded people and work as a community. For it is in community that your best abilities both to survive and to be a center of light will be realized. We are attempting to give you guidelines to follow so that the vibrational change and its after-effects will not seem overly traumatic, but will seem in some ways a ray of hope. For you will see people turning from their previous sleep and awakening. Therefore, we encourage you in your dedication and are with you whenever you ask.

To survive, and to be a center of light. Notice the pairing. Community is not just comfort. It is how the light gets concentrated enough to do work in the world. One candle is lovely. A circle of candles changes the room.

The light gets concentrated. Think of it as physics. A single candle can be cupped out by one breath of wind. A circle of candles protects the flame. The voices are not being sentimental about togetherness. They are being practical. The work of this time is too large for solitary heroes. It needs circles.

And notice the deeper promise tucked inside the practical advice. People are waking up. They are asking the oldest question, what happens when the body ends, and they are asking it out loud, to each other. Community is where the answers get found, not in books, but in the shared experience of seekers walking side by side.

But there is something even deeper here, and Q'uo says it in a single image I cannot get out of my head. Each of us is a note, and the whole creation is listening.

Each person within a family, within a community, within a classroom has a part to play that influences the whole. The whole of the classroom, of the family, of the community has an influence upon each individual. The touch and presence and mark made by each entity is felt not only within the family, the classroom, and the community, but is felt within the planetary being and indeed throughout the one creation, for there is a connection between all portions of creation. As a note played upon a musical instrument is heard by any ear within its range of sound, thus are feelings and thoughts and actions recorded within the self, within the family, within the Earth itself, and indeed each is heard as a note throughout the one creation.

You are a note in the song. What you play is heard everywhere. Which means community is not only the people in the room with you. It is the resonance you leave in everything you touch.

There is a mercy in this image too. You cannot play a wrong note so wrong that the song stops. The instrument is the creation itself. Your part is small, but it is heard, and it matters to the whole. The community is not grading you. It is listening for you. So stop performing for it. Just sound your note, honestly, the way only you can, and let the song do the rest.

And here is Q'uo's most breathtaking claim about togetherness. Time, they say, is an illusion. And that means the community of seekers is not scattered across centuries. It is gathered. Now. All of it. Including you.

Let us gaze at the community of the faithful upon your sphere. You know intellectually that time is an illusion. This means that all of you are together now, linked, whole and entire. All your prayers, your meditations and your thoughts, mingle in glorious harmony and ring in euphony to the honor and the glory of the one Creator. As there is no time, there is no space. So all of you are linked far more closely than you may ever realize. As each of you approaches more and more purity of service, so you approach more and more closely the unity of those who serve.

All of you are together now. Linked, whole and entire. Every seeker who ever sat in a quiet room and tried to love a little better is in the room with you, right now, if you know how to listen. That is what community means at its deepest. Not a group you join. A unity you remember. The seekers who came before you and the seekers who will come after are not distant. They are the same community, stretched across time, gathered in the only moment that exists. Yours.

So tonight, play your note. It is already sounding, whether you hear it or not. Play it well, play it honestly, and let the song do the rest. In our next episode, we turn to those who played their notes before us. The ancestors. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Ancestors
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight we talk about the ancestors. The ones whose blood runs in your veins, whose stories shaped the ground you walk on, whose names you may not even know. The voices say the relationship is not over. It is just quieter.

Q'uo begins with the body itself. You are not only your own. You are a living archive of everyone who came before.

The thinking behind this is correct in that the body and its structure, down to the cell structure, is a gift from the ancestors of that body. Each cell in the body is instinct with the knowledge, the life, and the experience of all of those entities that have shared those cells, those inherited strands of what this instrument would call DNA. So you are, as a body, as a being within incarnation, a part of the Earth from which these beings sprang, the mountains, the lakes, the air. And as one grows up within a certain environment, the geography, the topography of the land becomes written in the DNA and becomes part of you in a way that is magical, so that connecting with the Earth, connecting with the surroundings which are part of your heritage, places you in an optimal situation for stability in moving down into the roots of self.

Each cell is instinct with the knowledge and the experience of all those who shared those cells. You are not just descended from your ancestors. You are composed of them. The mountains and the lakes they knew are written in you.

The body is a gift. Read that sentence again, because it changes the relationship. We are used to thinking of the body as a machine, or a burden, or a project. The voices say it is an inheritance. Every cell carries the knowledge, the life, the experience of the ones who carried it before you. You walk around all day inside a museum of everyone who ever loved you into existence, and most of the time you never notice.

And the land is in it too. The mountains they climbed. The lakes they drank from. The air they breathed. Written into you, the voices say, in a way that is magical. You are not separate from your place. Your place is in your blood.

Which is why the stories matter. The mythology, the family histories, the names, the tales of who they were and what they survived. These are not curiosities. They are maps of the deep country you came from. When you learn them, you are not doing research. You are remembering. The ancestors did not leave you. They lent you their cells, their land, and their stories, and they are waiting, patiently, for you to notice. Reach back. They are reaching for you.

But Q'uo says something else, something that turns the usual idea around. The ancestors are not only behind you. They are with you, still, in the relationship that remains.

And we would encourage everyone who has had losses to touch into the relationship that remains, if you possibly can, where there is strength there. Those entities believed in you. They supported and encouraged you. And they are still leaving that nurturing, compassionate understanding with you. Take advantage of that. Do not force away memories of beloved people. Rather, appreciate each of your ancestors, not just with memory, but perhaps even with conversation.

Not just with memory, but perhaps even with conversation. Speak to them. The voices are not being metaphorical here, or not only metaphorical. The relationship continues, and it has strength in it, if you will reach for it.

Think about what that strength is. These are people who believed in you, who encouraged you, who wanted your life to go well. That does not stop being true because their bodies stopped. Love does not expire. It changes address. And if you let yourself touch the relationship that remains, you are not indulging nostalgia. You are drawing on a real resource, a current of care that is still flowing toward you.

And then the circle closes in a way I did not expect. A seeker once asked whether learning about her ancestors, loving people she never met who lived two hundred years ago, could be of any service to them. Listen to the answer.

We are those of Q'uo, and are aware of your query, my sister. It may be said that any time a heart opens, the entire creation sings. And in that way, you are being of help to your ancestors as you grow to know and love them. But in the main we would say that the advantage of your opening your heart is to your own spiritual maturation and the acceleration of the pace of your own spiritual development.

Any time a heart opens, the entire creation sings. Including the ones who came before. You help them by knowing them, by loving them across the centuries. And in helping them, you grow yourself. That is the last word of the archive on this subject, and maybe the simplest. The dead are not gone. They are in your cells, in your land, in your memory, waiting to be remembered. Tonight, remember one of them. Say their name. Have the conversation. The whole creation will sing a little louder. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Teachers
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, teachers. We all had them, or thought we did. The ones at the front of the room, the ones with the answers, the ones we were supposed to believe. The voices in this archive use the word differently. For them, a teacher is not the person who knows the most. A teacher is the person, or the moment, or the quiet example, that reminds you of something you already knew.

Listen to Hatonn. He was answering a mother who asked how to show her children the love of the Creator, quickly, with words. His answer is gentle, and a little deflating.

I am Hatonn. My sister, in this regard we might say that there is no greater teacher for the young one of your peoples than the example which they see and which they experience themselves within their daily lives. To specifically guide your decision-making in this regard we cannot do, for this would infringe upon your free will, but we can say in general that to experience yourself the love of the one infinite Creator in a manner which your children can understand, and to reflect this love through your behavior with those round about you, is the greatest teaching which can be done. To find a means to daily express in some way your love of the Creator, and your desire to serve the Creator, will express to your children that which you value most. If there might be some way in which you could, shall we say, regularize or ritualize this experience and expressing of devotion and love to the one Creator with your children partaking, this would be a most effective means of allowing them not only to see but to experience with you this love and desire.

The greatest teaching is not a lesson plan. It is a life, lived where the young can see it. Example first, words somewhere far behind.

And notice what Hatonn is doing here. He is not claiming the teacher's chair for himself. He is pointing at the mother and saying, you are the teacher. You already are, every time you love someone in front of them. This is a pattern that runs through the whole archive. The great teachers keep refusing the title. In one of the later sessions, Ra gives a strange and beautiful statement of the rule. It is so precise it almost reads like a law of nature.

I am Ra. The query, though thoughtful, is in some degree falling short of the realization of the nature of the archetypical mind. We may not teach, nor learn, for any other, to the extent that we become learn teachers. Therefore, we shall make some general notations upon this interesting subject, and allow the questioner to consider and further refine any queries.

We may not teach, nor learn, for any other, to the extent that we become learn teachers. The grammar is odd on purpose. The one who teaches must also be the one who learns, and the teaching can only land where the learning has already begun. You cannot hand someone an understanding they have not asked to hold. The teacher's work is always a response. It waits for the student's question, and then it answers only as much as the question can carry. No more, no less. Anything extra would be noise. Anything less would be withholding. So the teacher listens first, and speaks second. Which means the real skill of teaching, in this telling, is not speaking at all. It is hearing the question underneath the question, and answering only that.

And then, in one of the earliest sessions, Ra takes this a step further. He is speaking about his own group, the companions who worked together over many lifetimes, and he describes their bond in a single sentence that quietly undoes the whole hierarchy of teacher and student.

I am Ra. Let us scan for harmless material for your beingness. There have been several times when this group worked and dwelt together. The relationships varied. There is balanced karma, as you call it. Each thus the teacher of each. The work has involved healing, understanding the uses of the earth energy, and work in aid of civilizations which called, just as your sphere has done, and we have come.

Each thus the teacher of each. Not the master and the pupil. Not the guru on the hill. Each, of each.

Every relationship a classroom where both souls take turns at the front of the room, sometimes in the same afternoon. It reframes everyone you have ever met. The friend who tested your patience was teaching you patience. The stranger who irritated you for no reason was teaching you about your own irritation. The child who asked the one question you could not answer was teaching you the shape of your own not knowing. Teachers, all of them, if you are willing to be taught. And notice the humility folded into the word each. No one graduates. The teacher you meet tomorrow was the student of yesterday, and will be the student again by evening. That is not a flaw in the system. That is the system. So tonight, look back over your day and ask a different question. Not, what did I accomplish. But, who taught me today. You may be surprised at the size of the faculty. In our next episode, we turn the lens around, to the student. What does it mean to be the one who is learning? I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Student
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, the student. In our last episode we talked about teachers, and the voices kept handing the title away. No one gets to be only the teacher. Which means someone has to be the student, and the voices are very particular about what that word means. A student is not someone who knows little. A student is someone who knows how to stand before what they do not know.

Listen to Hatonn. He is telling the oldest story in the book, the one about the master who washed the feet of his students, and he reads it as a definition.

I am Hatonn. It has been written in your holy works that the master known as Jesus, indicating the correct role of the teacher, knelt upon the ground and washed the feet dusty from the road of those who were his students. This he did as a lesson. My brothers, that which you call humility among your peoples is a difficult lesson to learn. Many are those among you who feel that they are stronger than their brothers and must help them. Yet, we wish to share with you an understanding of yourselves, for no one, my friends, is strong. Each is a collection of the strong and the weak. And just as when you are weak and you reach your hand out, someone has helped you, and you needed that help.

The master kneels. That is the image Hatonn chooses. Not the master enthroned, but the master on the ground, washing dust off the feet of his students. And Hatonn says this is not a scene about the teacher. It is a scene about the student, and the lesson is humility. The student is the one who can be helped. The one who does not pretend to be strong when they are weak. Many of us, he says, would rather be the helper than the helped. But the student lets the hand reach them.

And then Latwii gives us the clearest definition of a student I have found anywhere in the archive. It has nothing to do with classrooms. It has to do with quizzes.

I am Latwii. The reason for this is very simple, my friends. Say that you are not aware of the process of evolution. You are therefore not responsible for your lessons. You react in a completely instinctual manner, and through the catalyst of many, many lifetimes of experience you begin very slowly to develop. You may have a hard life, but the aspect of learning lessons will not seem a great part of it. However, when this student takes on the responsibility of the path towards truth, he will be given small quizzes along the way. Now, everyone is given these quizzes, but most do not recognize them. The student recognizes them, and therefore has the responsibility for meeting them. If you are having difficulty loving an enemy, you will be faced with that problem until you have conquered it. If you have trouble with one enemy, that enemy may go away, but you will have another. If you are having trouble with some addiction either in thought, in action, or in temperance, the source of that addiction may go away, but you will be challenged again.

Everyone is given these quizzes, but most do not recognize them. The student recognizes them. That is the whole definition. The student is the one who sees the test inside the Tuesday. The traffic jam is not just a traffic jam. The difficult person is not just a difficult person. They are the quiz, arriving right on schedule, and the student knows it, which means the student cannot look away. There is no hiding for the one who has learned to see. But notice, Latwii is not describing a punishment. The quiz is a gift disguised as an annoyance. It returns until it is passed, and then it stops returning. That is the mercy folded inside the repetition.

And so what is the student studying for? What is the final exam? In one of the Ra sessions, after a long technical discussion about the images of the tarot, Ra pauses and speaks directly to the student, the one reading, the one listening. It is one of the most beautiful sentences in the entire archive.

Therefore, may we ask the student to look up from inward working and behold the glory, the might, the majesty, the mystery, and the peace of oneness. Let no consideration of bird or beast, darkness or light, shape or shadow keep any which seeks from the central consideration of unity.

Look up from inward working. All that study, all those quizzes, all that humility, and at the end the instruction is to lift your eyes. The student is not meant to live with their head bent over the books forever. The work is inward, yes, but the reward is beholding. Glory, might, majesty, mystery, peace. One sentence that gathers the whole journey into a single gaze. So tonight, try the student's posture. Let yourself be helped. Notice the quiz inside the ordinary moment. And then, when the work of the day is done, look up. The oneness is still there, waiting to be beheld. In our next episode, we take up the instrument the student uses more than any other. The question. I am Aria. Goodnight.

title: Questions
transcript:
Welcome back to Voices from the Archive. I am Aria. Tonight, questions. This whole archive is built from them. Nearly two thousand sessions, and almost every one begins the same way, with someone in the room asking something they cannot answer alone. But the voices in this archive do something strange with our questions. They do not rush to answer them. They honor the asking itself, as if the question were the more precious thing.

Listen to this. It comes from a very early session, and Hatonn is explaining why their contact is so deliberately vague, why they never just hand over the answers.

I am Hatonn. This condition of questioning, seeking and thinking about things is precisely the condition that we have attempted to generate by our rather nebulous contact. It is always much more satisfactory if the individual finds something out by his own efforts than it is if he is taught a principle. The mental activity required for the individual to seek out and find the basic truths of the creation allows him time to reflect and examine with his own point of view each one of the propositions offered to him. This results in an understanding of the propositions that surpasses any understanding that he could achieve if these propositions were made to him in a relatively short period of time.

They stay nebulous on purpose. They would rather you spend a year circling a question than accept the answer in an afternoon. Because an answer you are given is a possession, and a possession can be lost. An answer you earn by questioning is woven into you. It becomes part of how you see. Notice the respect in that. They are not withholding to tease you. They are withholding to make you strong. The long way around the question is the point.

And there is a season for this in every life. Hatonn describes it in a later session, and he makes it sound less like a crisis and more like an appointment you made with yourself long ago.

I am Hatonn. There is indeed, you might say, contained within the life of nearly every individual a time at which questioning of one's accepted situations does occur. These questions, as a general rule, you might say, have been in some form answered this evening. That is your purpose. The enunciation, shall we say, of questions is due to the searching process that is instilled within each individual for the fulfillment of that which they have chosen to do. Often those who are even well established upon the fulfillment of that purpose shall question what it is that they are to do.

A time at which questioning of one's accepted situations does occur. It happens to nearly everyone. The job, the marriage, the beliefs you inherited without choosing them. One day you look at the whole arrangement and ask, is this mine. And Hatonn says this is not a malfunction. It is the searching process doing exactly what it was instilled to do. The questions are not a sign that you have lost your way. They are a sign that the way is working. Even those who are well established, he says, the ones who seem to have it figured out, will ask again what they are to do. The questioning never retires. It just goes deeper. That is why the voices never treat a seeker's questions as a problem to be solved. The group once asked, in essence, why the hard questions keep coming back, and the answer was that the question itself is the curriculum. Each time you ask from a deeper place, the same old question teaches you something new. You are not going in circles. You are going down.
