And as they wandered farther, they became more and more immersed in an illusion of their own making. This illusion is at present so very strong that many of the children of the Creator find themselves confused, and unable to easily find the pathway back to the infinite light.

It is necessary that they realize for themselves how to do this, for the principle is still totally in effect. It allows them to do precisely what they desire. So they must realize what they desire, and then seek it. This is our purpose at the present time. To help those who are presently seeking the pathway that will return them to the love and the light that they now desire.

He is honest about the limits of his own foreknowledge. We are acquainted with certain aspects of what you would call the future, because we can move in time as well as space. But free will alters the stream. As events change in what you know as the present, so do they change in what you know as the future. It is not possible to travel through time in exactly the same sense that you travel in space, for time has properties dependent on the action of free will.

In the past, he says, many of your people have traveled in the dimension of time. Many are experiencing this dimension now, in what you know as dreams.

Then the closing charge, and it is the simplest thing he has said all evening. Realize that you are a part of the creation, and that the creation is one single thing, and that in so being, you and all your brothers and sisters throughout all space are one being. This realization will result in an ability to demonstrate only one reaction to anything. That reaction will be love.

Do these simple things. Do not sway from this understanding and this love. Do this, and only this, and you will reach a state of ecstasy enjoyed by all of the Creator's children living in His light. Join us, he says, in the kingdom of heaven. For this was what was meant for you. This is what is your destiny. It is what you desire.

The stream flows. You are already in it. And every point along it, past and future both, is here, now, waiting for you to arrive.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Only Place
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the only place.

It is a strange session to begin with, and the best ones often are. The group gathers on a Sunday evening in January of nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn opens with something that sounds like a riddle. He and his brothers, he says, are in space, and they are also here. Both at once. To them, all places are the same place.

From our point of view, this is nonsense. A place is a place. You are in your kitchen or you are not. But Hatonn insists that being in two places, or many places, at one time is entirely possible, and that the reason we cannot do it is not physics. It is thinking. Our location, he says, is simply a consequence of our thinking. We are where we think we are, and we stay there because we keep thinking it.

The idea is not entirely new to this planet, he admits. A few have understood it. But understanding it takes more than a clever argument. It requires the reality of the unity of the creation, because only from unity does the riddle dissolve.

I like the way he draws the line here. There are many ways to state this idea intellectually, he says, but it is more revealing to experience it. This experience is available to all of the Creator's children. It was how they were originally created. Only through your own desires, he says, have you cut yourself off from the ability to experience the reality that is all about you.

Listen to that. Not through sin. Not through failure. Through desire. We wanted the limitation. It was not intended that we be so limited, he says. It is only our desire that we be so. And that means, he is explicit about this, that it is a simple process to free ourselves from the thinking that limits us to our present locations. Simple. He never says easy. He says simple.

The dimensions of the creation, as we experience them, seem of such magnitude that traveling any great distance looks impossible. The Confederation voices do not have these limitations, and the reason, Hatonn says, is only their understanding of the truth of total oneness. This oneness is the original Thought that was provided to all of the children of the Creator.

And so he gives the instruction, and it is one sentence long. Return to this Thought. Have no other thought but this Thought: a Thought of total and complete love. This, he says, will enable you to know all of the fruits of our infinite Creator.

One Thought. Held in place of all the others. The smallest possible doorway, and he says everything is on the other side of it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Creation Is Thought
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the creation is thought.

On a Friday evening in February of nineteen seventy-four, Hatonn gives the group the operating manual for the universe, and it is shorter than you would expect. Everything that you experience, he says, has been created by mind. Everything.

The creation was designed, he says, to reflect the impressions given to it by man. It was so designed as to express his desires in any way that he chose. The conditions you experience in your daily activities are a result of your thinking, and the thinking of those about you, and others on your surface. Read that again slowly. Your days are made of thought.

He makes the creation larger than our science suspects. There are various levels or densities in this creation, he says, levels and densities not yet suspected by your physical scientists. Each of these levels is expressing the desires of the Creator's children who are acting within it. Each is moldable, able to be acted upon by the thoughts of the individuals within it, to a greater or in some cases a lesser extent than those on the surface of your planet appreciate. It is only necessary to desire an effect to create it.

He makes it concrete. Consider the creations of man, he says: his cities, his homes, his factories, his vehicles for conveyance. All of them are expressions of his thought, brought into existence through a physical manipulation of his physical body, but no less a direct manifestation of thought. And since man is himself an expression and a creation of the Creator, his creations are simply an extension of the original Thought. All creations, everywhere, are the works, directly or indirectly, of the Creator of us all.

I love how plain he makes it. It is only necessary to desire an effect to create it. That is what the Creator provided. And the abilities that made it possible were never removed. They are within all of the children of the Creator, and they will always remain. He wished for all of His children to have and to use the abilities to govern and mold their environments at will.

The people of this planet have forgotten the principle. That is the whole tragedy, stated in one sentence. The teacher known as Jesus, Hatonn says, was no different from any of you. He simply was able to remember certain principles. These principles are not at all complex. They are very simple.

Then comes the turn that explains so much of the archive. These principles, Hatonn says, are not necessarily of an intellectual nature. The people of this planet have been mentally conditioned by erroneous thinking for so long that they cannot easily become intellectually aware of what is simple and true. So the intellectual mind must be circumnavigated, and the principles communicated directly to the soul, to the spiritual mind, through telepathic impression in a non-intellectual, conceptual sense.

This is why he keeps asking for daily meditation. Not as a ritual, not as a discipline to impress anyone with, but as the mechanism. The impressions arrive in meditation. They are analyzed at a deeper level. And a true and complete understanding is arrived at.

If this process of daily meditation is continued, he says, each of those who avail themselves to it will begin to become aware of things about them in a new sense, and will begin to appreciate the true creation in a greater and more beautiful way.

He is honest about the resistance. There is what he calls interference: erroneous thoughts manifested in most of the areas of your planet, of a nature to cause a problem in the realization of truth. These erroneous thoughts, he says, must be totally obliterated from the thinking of an individual if he is to return to the original thinking with which he was created. Strong words. But then he softens the method. You do not fight the interference with arguments. You go around it, in silence, every day.

This is the road to the future, he says. This is where you are going to be. It is only necessary that you go.

Thank you for listening.

title: Two Kinds of Service
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: two kinds of service.

This is the evening Hatonn teaches the group how to tell whether their helping is actually helping. A Saturday in February, nineteen seventy-four, and he begins by saying something the Confederation does not say lightly: service is an extremely difficult task to perform effectively.

There are two classifications, he says, under which all services may be divided. The first includes services of a transient or unlasting nature. These are the things you do in your daily activities for your fellow man, and they are truly services. But then he gives the test, and the test is everything.

The test is to determine whether or not the service is of such a nature to cause spiritual growth for the one served. That is the second classification: services of a permanent nature. And this, he says, whether it is known to the individual or whether he has forgotten, is in truth his only real objective.

Think about what that means. The people of your planet are, for the most part, in a state of ignorance with respect to their real objective, which is the evolvement of their spiritual awareness. So the true service is whatever serves that evolution. Everything else, however kind, is transient.

This is why the Confederation holds back. It is necessary, Hatonn says, that if an individual is to make progress in a spiritual sense, it be a result of his own inner-directed seeking, rather than an outer-directed commandment given to him by an organization of a religious or other nature. If they landed their craft on every lawn and proved themselves beyond question, the inner direction of seeking would be lost. The seeking is the point. The conditions of this planet, difficult as they are, were selected to produce exactly that: an inner-directed seeking for truth.

I find this part quietly devastating. Many of the people of this planet, he says, are so involved in activities of an extremely transient and unimportant nature that they do not have opportunities for experiencing the growth of awareness that is necessary to accomplish the seeking that they actually desire. Busy with nothing. Starved of the one thing.

So the Confederation balances. Too much exposure and the seeking dies. Too little and the seekers are left alone. They must approach those who are ready without distressing those who are not. The evidence of their visits must be of such a nature that it can be rejected or accepted by anyone exposed to it.

He admits this visit is happening earlier than the plan called for. Our craft and our people have visited this planet many, many times in the past, he says, but only after a civilization was ready to receive us, only after it was displaying the principles of love and brotherhood that are the product of inner seeking. This time, he says, they are forced by conditions over which they have no control to visit even though the civilization has not reached a satisfactory level of spiritual awareness. Some are ready. Most are not. And the problem is how to approach the one part without distressing the other.

That is why the contact looks the way it does: deniable, quiet, arriving through meditation and through channels like this one. Not a landing on the White House lawn. A whisper that the ready will recognize and the unready can ignore.

And here is the line I keep returning to. It will not be necessary to prove to these people that what we are giving them is truth, he says, for if an individual has reached an understanding of truth through inner-directed seeking, then he will recognize this truth when it is given to him.

Recognition, not proof. That is their whole method. A helping hand up the ladder of spiritual evolution, extended in daily meditation, to whoever reaches back.

He closes the evening the way he always does, but this time the farewell carries the whole teaching in it. I am always with each of you, he says, and I am always at your service in your seeking of the love and the light that is the true creation.

Always with you. Always at your service. The help is not coming later. It is already here, waiting for the inner direction to turn toward it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Serving as It Comes
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: serving as it comes.

On a Sunday evening in February of nineteen seventy-four, Hatonn is asked a question about the self, about appreciation of the self, and his answer is one of the cleanest statements of unity in the whole archive. There is no necessity, he says, to establish within one's thinking an appreciation of self. For this presupposes that it is possible to separate self from the entire creation.

If one appreciates any part of the creation, then one appreciates self, for they are one and the same thing. The elimination of the concept of self, he says, is an important one in your spiritual seeking. It is necessary only to appreciate the Creator and His product, the creation. In appreciating any part of the creation, one must appreciate all parts, for they are inseparable.

Then he draws the practical line. It is important to act in unison with the creation rather than out of harmony due to a lack of confidence in a state of oneness. And the way to arrive at that oneness is the way he always names: daily meditation.

The Confederation's own example follows. It is not necessary, he says, that we appreciate ourselves in our attempts to serve. It is only necessary that we serve.

He opens the evening by saying where the answers come from. The group has asked him a question, and he tells them the answer is found the same place they could find it themselves: within. It is possible for you, like us, to directly find these answers, he says, for they are within you as they are within everyone. We only hope to remind you that you have these within you. We only hope to help guide you to a remembrance of what you seek. The channel is not a source. It is a reminder service. This will be appreciated by the Creator, for the Creator is all that there is. It is as impossible to separate the Creator from the creation as it is impossible to separate yourself from the creation.

I love the next instruction, because it removes so much striving. It is not necessary that you seek out opportunities to serve. It is only necessary that you serve as best you can as the opportunities present themselves. Do not hunt for chances to be good. Live your life, and when the moment arrives, serve in it. That is all.

But there is a condition, and he states it plainly. It is impossible to serve if one is not knowledgeable as to how to serve, and it is not possible in your particular state of awareness to know how to serve unless this knowledge is sought through daily meditation. So the process is simple. Become aware of how to serve through meditation. Then serve as the opportunities present themselves. If these simple tasks are performed, he says, you are fulfilling all of the requirements that were specified by our Creator.

Later in the same evening, Hatonn returns with a smaller teaching that belongs beside the larger one. In the fields of your planet, he says, grow many things that are edible. They are given to you by your Creator to sustain life in your present physical form. But the food you select is up to you. The Creator provided for the fulfillment of desire, and it was His plan that each individual should have exactly what he would desire.

Desire again. The same mechanism that runs the universe also runs the dinner table. And the understanding of desire, he says, like the understanding of everything else, comes through one door. With an understanding achieved through daily meditation, it is possible to fully understand desire.

There is much wisdom in this arrangement, he says of the food growing in the fields. It is necessary, if you are to exist in physical form, to sustain the body. But what you select is up to you, and the selection reveals the desire, and the desire reveals the understanding. Even appetite is a teacher, if you sit still long enough to hear it.

Meditate. Then serve what comes. That is the whole evening.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Death, Only Experience
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no death, only experience.

This is one of the shortest sessions in the archive, a Monday meditation in February of nineteen seventy-four, and it begins with two hard questions from the group. Why do animals have to kill each other? Why do earthquakes have to kill people?

The answer comes back in four words. There is no death. There is experience.

Each entity, the voice says, experiences what he desires. The concept of dominion is unclear, but the concept of awareness is clear. The people of this planet experience a higher degree of awareness, and in that respect they enjoy a kind of dominion over the other forms of life. But all the forms of life are one form: the Creator. They all express His love.

Listen to how they handle rank. The concept of dominion, in the sense that there should be a separation by rank or privilege, was never a portion of the original Thought of our Creator. There are many experiences allowed the children of the Creator. There are many experiments which they may perform. However, there is only one truth, and it is the truth of unity and love.

Then the voice turns to vibration, and gently corrects the group's mental picture. You speak of vibration, and in your mind you think of various grades. We do not think in this manner. There are simply different experiences for an entity to choose. Different experiences, but the same creation.

The closing passage is the one to sit with. An infinite creation, experiencing an infinite number of experiences, separate but the same, graded but ungraded. Separated by vast distances, but all in the same place. Expressing many thoughts and desires, but being only one: the Thought and desire of the Creator.

Separate but the same. That is the whole session in four words. The earthquake, the animal, the questioner, the voice answering: one Thought, having infinite experiences, none of them final.

The tape ends there. No farewell, no blessing, just the sentence hanging in the room. It is enough. If there is no death but only experience, then nothing is lost, and nothing was ever separate to begin with.

Thank you for listening.

title: Many Mansions
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: many mansions.

A Monday meditation in February of nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn begins with something practical: how a person actually becomes a channel. The thoughts of the Confederation, he says, are available to all who would receive them. But they are not necessarily received by all who desire them. The problem is to produce the condition in which all who desire the concepts receive them.

The first step is seeking. An individual must first initiate a spiritual seeking himself, and sometimes a catalyst is needed: some verbal concepts of a more spiritual nature, to generate an attitude of seeking. That, he says, is the reason for communicating through channels such as this one. The spoken words are only the spark. Once the spark catches, the individual begins to seek on his own, and the seeking builds on itself.

Then comes the part the group found strange: conditioning. When seeking reaches a certain intensity, the individual becomes aware of what Hatonn calls a blanket conditioning wave. It is automatic, like tuning a radio receiver, except the tuning is unique. The wave acts on the channel physically, producing a muscular reaction, an attempt to speak the first portion of a communication that matches it in spiritual quality.

The process builds upon itself, he says. As an individual becomes aware, intellectually, of certain spiritual truths, and since these truths are in actuality within him but to some degree forgotten, he will then begin to seek on his own. The spoken concepts are only the catalyst. The real work starts when the listener stops listening to the channel and starts listening inward, and finds the same truths waiting there, half-remembered, like a song from childhood.

I love his honesty about how messy this is for beginners. A new channel cannot easily tell which thoughts are meant for communication and which are not. So a long period of conditioning is needed, so the channel learns to recognize the muscular signal that arrives when the spiritual quality is sufficient. If the thought is of little value, there is no attempt to initiate the communication. The body itself becomes the filter.

Then the session turns, and Hatonn speaks the line this episode is named for. There are many vibrations within this creation. It has been written in your holy works that in my Father's house, there are many mansions. The mansion, or vibration, in which an entity finds himself is a result of his desire. If there is a separation to be made, it is up to each entity to select, according to his desire.

No mansion is good or bad, he says. Each is simply a different place. And suffering exists only in the mind of the individual experiencing it, and if he experiences it, it is because he desires it. Strange, he admits. But this is how the creation is designed.

There is a detail in the conditioning I do not want to skip. The wave, Hatonn says, operates at a sufficiently high spiritual level that when a thought of that level enters the channel's consciousness, the conditioning matches it, and the body attempts to speak. If the thought is of little value, nothing happens. No effort, no forcing. The silence itself is the answer. A new channel needs a long period of this, he says, simply to learn the difference between a thought worth speaking and one worth letting pass. Most of us could use the same training without the muscular part.

The session closes with one of the most quoted passages in the early archive, and it needs no commentary from me. I am love, and I am Hatonn, and I am light, and I am Hatonn. You are love and you are light. You and I are the same. You experience one thing. I experience one thing. But yet we are the same. For this is the creation. We are one.

And then the final instruction, the whole method in one sentence. To separate, classify and measure is not of the Creator's design. To unify, embrace, and love is all that is necessary. Three verbs offered in place of three others, and the entire spiritual path is contained in the exchange.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Key of Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the key of desire.

A Saturday evening in February of nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn states the master principle of the archive more bluntly than anywhere else. Your desire, my friends, is the key to your existence. The Creator planned that all of His children, throughout all of the universe, would get exactly what they desire. That is how the universe works. That is how the Creator planned it.

Every condition on this planet, he says, from those you would call enjoyable to those you despise, is a result of desire. Man on Earth does not realize that he creates everything that he experiences through the mechanism of desire.

And then the turn that makes this more than a slogan. Man on Earth is desiring things that he does not want. He does not understand his desires, and since he does not understand them, he does not understand the gifts of the Creator. He interprets them quite erroneously. The Creator never planned for His children to be the recipients of that which they did not desire. But they keep desiring it anyway, blindly, and receiving it faithfully.

Listen to how he describes the mechanism. Ask, and you shall receive. Knock, and the door shall be opened. Seek, and ye shall find. These are not promises of reward. They are descriptions of physics. Your desire sparks cause and effect. The universe is a mirror that never looks away.

The objective underneath it all, he says, is the same for every person in the creation, whether they know it or not. The objective is the Creator. A return to Him. A return to the true creation. Many of His children have wandered far, led by desires that led to other desires that led them farther still, until they no longer remember the original Truth.

Why, then, do they sleep? Hatonn gives an answer I have never heard anywhere else. Sleep, my friends, is not a normal condition. It is something that the people of your planet do out of necessity. During sleep they come into contact with their innermost thoughts, and if they did not, they would long since have ceased to exist, for a being cannot long exist in a condition of total lack of the Creator's truth.

But sleep is not enough. It does not satisfy the requirements for the truth to be revealed in its totality. So meditation is necessary: the waking return to what sleep only hints at.

The session ends with the shortest sermon in the archive. Seek, my friends. Seek. This is the word that opens the door to everything that exists throughout all of space and all of time. Seek. Seek.

And what will you find? You will find love, he says, for that is all that there is to find. For that is all that there is.

Before that closing, there is a passage I cannot leave out, because it shows why the Confederation is here at all. The people of your planet are living an illusion, Hatonn says, and this illusion includes the concept of the possibility of separation. As you look at your fellow man, see him for what he is: the Creator. For there is no part of this creation that is any more or less than any other part. Each part is a portion of the creation. Each holds equal rank.

This is not so with the Confederation, he says, and here his tone changes. We feel your pain, and this brings us to you at this time: to serve you. For in doing so, we serve ourselves, since you and we are one. Your pain is felt throughout all of the creation, and for this reason there are many, many here to serve you at this time.

The desires of this planet, he warns, are a contagion. They affect not only the ones generating the desire, but others who live on the surface. It requires an extreme degree of understanding to live upon your surface and not experience this contagion. It can be done, he says. It is only necessary that you know and demonstrate the Creator's truth in every thought and deed. And then you will be free from the effect of the desires of your brothers who live about you.

He adds one more thing, almost as an aside, and it reframes the whole evening. This message, he says, is not meant so much for this group as it is for those who will read it at a later time, for this group is seeking. He was speaking past the room. He was speaking to us.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Force That Creates
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the force that creates.

On the first of two meditations held February eleventh, nineteen seventy-four, Hatonn takes up the two words the Confederation uses in every greeting, and shows what they actually mean. Love and light. All of the creation, he says, is composed of love and light. But the words in your language are extremely lacking in depth of definition. Tonight he will clarify them.

Love is the force that creates. Light is what it creates. That is the whole teaching in two sentences, and everything after is commentary.

The Creator is love. You are love. You are a part of the Creator, therefore you are love, but your love is expressed through the manifestation of light. Light is the substance out of which the creation is formed. The Creator's love causes vibrations. This is what is meant by the term vibration: it is a condition of love.

I want to slow down here, because the physics he describes is beautiful. These vibrations are the building energies that compose all of the creation. They produce the basic particle that you understand as a particle of light, and the particle manifests as a function of the rate of vibration. The intensities of vibration are a function of the intensities of love that generate them. Then these particles are arranged by this expression of love to produce everything: your physical world and its inhabitants, and all other worlds and their inhabitants, physical or non-physical.

From this it follows, he says, that any individual who understands the principles could express this love to create for himself that which he desired. This is done all the time. The Creator considered it normal. Each of you has the ability to create through love anything that you desire. It is only necessary that you express the love that is yourself.

He points to the teacher known as Jesus as the demonstration. By the simple expression of the love that was himself and all of the creation, he created this vibration, and then, through desire, there was formed of this vibration the light as was originally conceived by the Creator. This light was formed to the wishes and desires of this man. All of your material is composed of this single basic particle.

And healing. If desire is to be intelligently employed, he says, it is necessary to employ it through the principle of love, for this is the generative force which produces the vibration condensing, you might say, out of space, the particle known to you as light. It is possible to return things considered to be lacking in perfection to their original perfection through this principle. This is how the healing evidenced by the man known as Jesus was accomplished. This is how all healing of a spiritual nature is accomplished. This is, in fact, how all healing is accomplished, although your science is not at this time aware of this.

Do not believe that this man was unique in his ability, Hatonn says. He was demonstrating that each of the Father's children could do the same thing. It is only necessary that you meditate to realize this, and then demonstrate your knowledge of it through your thoughts and your actions.

He is realistic about the difficulty. It is quite possible, he says, to insulate one's consciousness from the infringements of thought all around you and realize the truth of your origin. But it is a difficult thing to do when surrounded by vibrations created by desire of a nature never intended by the Creator. The one known as Jesus was able to do it. The insulation is possible. The noise is real. Both things are true at once, and meditation is the insulation.

We use these two words, love and light, he says, because they are the closest in your language to what we wish to communicate. But they are extremely lacking in depth of definition. Every greeting the Confederation gives, every farewell, is an attempt to say in two thin words what the whole creation is made of. Tonight he tried to give the words their weight back.

He closes with a sentence that lands like a bell. This is the word, my friends: love. But it is not understood. Love: it means all that you think it means. But it means much more. Learn what it means, and you shall truly be free.

Thank you for listening.

title: Anxious to Meet You
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: anxious to meet you.

The second meditation of February eleventh, nineteen seventy-four, is unlike any other session in the archive. It is the night Hatonn tries to land.

It begins with difficulty. The instrument known as R cannot hold the contact, and another channel takes up the thread. Hatonn announces that he is speaking from a craft, a small craft, approximately thirty feet in diameter, capable of landing at any point upon the surface. He is aware, he says, that the instrument relaying this is skeptical. He has always been skeptical of communications of this nature. Hatonn asks him, gently and repeatedly, to relax, to clear his mind, to stop analyzing, and simply let the words come.

I am aware that you are extremely anxious to meet us, he says, and we, my friends, are extremely anxious to meet you. Nothing would give us greater pleasure than to walk upon your surface and meet you directly. They are in the atmosphere, he says, and around the planet outside the atmosphere, constantly keeping watch, constantly ready to serve in any way that they can.

Then the question comes. Is it possible for us to meet now? And Hatonn answers with an instruction. Put on your coats and go into the back yard. I will reveal myself to both of you.

The transcript notes what happened next, plainly, the way these old records do. Both went to the back yard. One saw nothing. One saw a white star-like object which moved very rapidly across the sky, with no trail, and then disappeared.

When the contact resumes, the group is wondering why they could not see the craft. Hatonn's answer is brief and a little wry. Because you were not looking as we told you to look.

I love this session, not because it proves anything, but because of what it reveals about the voices. The skepticism of the instrument is not hidden or edited out. It is part of the record. Hatonn addresses it directly, patiently, the way you would speak to a friend who does not quite trust his own ears. He does not scold the doubt. He works around it.

And underneath the strangeness there is the same teaching as every other night. They want to meet. They are anxious to meet. But the meeting can only happen in the way the creation allows: through desire, through readiness, through the slow work of becoming able to receive.

There is a small mercy in how Hatonn handles the instrument's doubt through all of this. He never asks for belief. He asks for relaxation. Clear the mind, stop analyzing, let the words come, and judge later. It is the same instruction he gives for meditation, for receiving conditioning, for knowing your desire. The whole archive, in the end, is one instruction repeated in different keys: get quiet, and let what is true arrive. One saw a light cross the sky. The other saw nothing. Both, in a sense, received exactly what they were ready to receive.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Desire to Serve
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the desire to serve.

On a Wednesday evening in February of nineteen seventy-four, Hatonn gives the most complete teaching on service in the early archive. It begins with a correction to the way the people of this planet chase their desires. They seek the result of their desires almost exclusively within the physical illusion, he says, and having fulfilled one desire, they immediately generate another, and then wonder why they are not happy.

But there is one desire that is different, because it is not manufactured by the illusion. The Creator had an original desire, which continues throughout all of time and all of space: to provide an experience for all of His parts that would fulfill in totality the desire of all of His parts. And since all of His parts share this same desire, it should be evident, Hatonn says, that this desire is to serve the other parts.

This dwells within each individual throughout all of the creation. The planet you stand on serves you. The growth that comes from the planet serves you. Its atmosphere serves you. Its water serves you. The entire creation serves you. You feel the energy from your sun. It serves you.

I find that passage quietly overwhelming. Everything, serving, all the time, without being asked. And the law underneath it is stated with total simplicity. You will achieve what you actually desire only if you are to serve the rest of the creation. This is a law that is natural. This law is the creation.

The Confederation calls itself by this law. We are in His service, Hatonn says, but we are in our service, and we are in your service, and we are in the creation's service, for we have recognized that it is only possible to fulfill desire through service. This is why we are here now: to give you our service. This fulfills our desire. This fulfills the Creator's desire. The entire process is simplicity itself.

Then comes the warning about blind service. Many people on this planet are serving, but only a small percentage are actually fulfilling their desire to serve, for blind service is not as effective as service performed as a result of the knowledge gained in meditation. It is important to learn how to serve, and whom should be served. Meditate, he says, for this knowledge is within all people throughout the creation.

Later in the evening, after a silently asked question, Hatonn returns to speak on love, and gives the sentence this episode turns on. A service is only a service if it is desired. Man has free will. He is free to choose anything that he desires. It is necessary, if you are to serve, that you understand the desire of those served, not in an intellectual sense, but in a sense that you gain through meditation. A knowledge that transcends the intellect. A knowledge that results in effective service.

Listen to how practical that is. The love you give in return for your service will be reflected back to you only if the service was actually wanted.

He explains why. With each service effectively performed, love will be reflected. This will generate within you more love, and the process will be repeated, or recycled. The process is self-generating and will continue to build. This is what occurred with the teacher known as Jesus. Why was he so much more effective in generating this love than others? Because he fulfilled his desire for service intelligently, seeking the answers to how through meditation, rather than learning service intellectually from others or from readings.

So many who seek to serve today, Hatonn says, learn their methods from books and teachers, and then find difficulties, and the love they expect in return is not reflected, for the service they attempted was not desired, and is therefore not a service. The loop only runs when the service is real: serve what is desired, love returns, love grows, service deepens. Begin it anywhere and it feeds itself.

Serve what is desired, not what you have decided should be desired. And the way to know the difference is not to think harder. It is to sit still.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gift of Frustration
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gift of frustration.

A short session, a Friday in February of nineteen seventy-four, spoken through a new and unpracticed instrument. Hatonn knows the contact is rough. He says so himself. But what he manages to say through it is one of the kindest teachings in the archive, and it is for anyone who has ever felt stuck.

Perhaps it is hard for you to realize how your spiritual development is progressing, he says. This is because this development cannot be measured, as you would say, on a day-to-day basis. It is possible to realize it more readily over a period of months.

I love the gentleness of that. No daily scorecard. No proof required by morning. Growth is happening on a timescale longer than your patience, and your inability to see it is not evidence that it has stopped.

Then the turn. He speaks of the frustration encountered by those who would seek a higher spiritual life, and the doubt that comes with it. Look upon your frustrations and doubt as spiritual tests, he says. Look upon these as things to be overcome. It is a most interesting paradox that these great hardships can bring such great reward.

It has been said, he adds, that one makes one's greatest spiritual strides during these times. During the frustration. During the doubt. Not after they pass, but inside them.

He closes with a sentence that reframes the whole difficult business of being a seeker on this planet. It is hard, he says, for people to realize how great a gift these frustrations and doubts are, as it is difficult to realize how great a gift it is to be able to experience the vibrational change upon your planet. How great a gift it is to be able to serve your fellow man.

The hardship is the gift. The doubt is the gift. The slow, unmeasurable progress is the gift. If tonight you feel that you are getting nowhere, Hatonn would tell you that this feeling, too, belongs to the path, and that the path is working on you even now.

Thank you for listening.

title: A Great Graduation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a great graduation.

On a Sunday evening in February of nineteen seventy-four, Hatonn states the Confederation's mission in its simplest possible form. We are attempting to bring to you one thing, he says. We have attempted to do this in many ways, but still we have but one thing to bring to you at this time. We are bringing to you love.

This is all that is necessary, he says, for when you are able to receive this love, with it will come the understanding that many of you now seek. There is only one thing to understand, and that is the actual interpretation of the word love.

The word is misunderstood among your peoples, he says. It does not mean what most of them believe it means. The man known as Jesus demonstrated it. His miracles were not miracles in the true sense. They were simply expressions of this man's love, for in expressing this love in its true and total sense he was able to use the single force of the creation given to each of the Creator's children as their birthright.

Each of you here tonight has the same birthright, Hatonn says, for each of you is equal in all respects to all of the Creator's children. Nothing else is of any real importance, for once this is understood, all is understood. And this concept, my friends, is simplicity itself.

Then the contact passes to another instrument, and the evening takes its famous turn. Be aware, my friends, that a great opportunity is presented to all of your peoples at this time. Those among your peoples who can raise their consciousness rapidly enough can take part in what you might call a great graduation.

Your planet, he says, moves to a higher vibratory area, and is even now at the entrance to this higher vibratory area. Only those individuals whose vibration can be raised along with that of the planet will continue into the Golden Age which will soon dawn upon your surface: a spiritual age of beauty, grandeur and true love.

I want to note the practicality tucked inside the prophecy. As an individual, each of you have everything to gain by following our simple suggestions, which will raise you in consciousness. You have nothing to lose but a small particle of what you call your time. And then the question he puts to the listener, which still lands: do you not find the time for those things which are important to you? It may simply be a matter of readjusting in your own thinking that which is important to you.

Many upon your planet, he says, have been deeply immersed in a hypnotic state. It is desirable to awaken from this state. The method is the one he always gives: daily meditation, constant self-analysis, and love.

A graduation is coming, he says. The entrance is already here. The tuition is a little of your time, and the willingness to wake up.

He is candid about the record itself. There have been misunderstandings about their contacts, he says. There have been misrepresentations, through no fault of the contactee, of what they would bring. So he states it once more, without decoration. What they bring is an education. For many of the people of this planet have lost direction and have become involved in a complex illusion. With this awareness, he says, comes all awareness. This is the first step, and it is also the last step, in knowing all that there is to know.

May you put forth the necessary effort, he says in farewell. May each of you grow rapidly in love, which will bring about understanding and a new awareness to you. Not effort toward achievement. Effort toward love, which does the rest on its own.

Underneath the prophecy there is the quietest claim in the session, and it is the one everything depends on. It is only necessary, he says, that you become aware of this birthright through meditation, for this knowledge is within you. For you, like ourselves, and like every being within this infinite creation, is a part of this creation. We are all one thing. We are the creation of the Father, and in so being we have within us His love, for this is what created us: a great force, a force that permeates everything that exists. You cannot be separated from it. You can only forget it for a while.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Meaning of Christ
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the meaning of Christ.

The first meditation of February eighteenth, nineteen seventy-four, is the longest session yet in this part of the archive, and it goes somewhere the voices rarely go. A questioner asks about the antichrist. Hatonn answers by dissolving the question.

The source of confusion, he says, is the concept of Christ. Once this concept is understood, then the concept of antichrist is understood. So he speaks of the man known as Jesus.

This man was born into the physical upon your planet, Hatonn says. He was able to realize the truth of the creation, and then he was able to demonstrate this truth to those about him. He came, as many teachers have come, for the purpose of serving the people of this planet. Each of them did it in his own way.

These teachers were limited, he says, limited by the same conditions that each of you experience. And the people of this planet have misinterpreted the meaning of these men. They are at this time misinterpreting the meaning of the man known as Jesus. His purpose was to demonstrate that it is possible, through an awareness of the Creator's truth, to experience what the Creator planned for each of us. What were called miracles were simply the result of thinking in the original way as planned by our Creator. He was demonstrating that it is possible for anyone, at any time, to demonstrate this type of thinking, and therefore the abilities that accompany it.

Then the answer to the question. What is the antichrist? It is simply the ignorance of the knowledge of this truth. This ignorance is widespread upon this planet. If there exists an individual who would be called the antichrist, then there exists an extremely ignorant individual. Should this be a threat to any of the Creator's children? I think not.

The questioner presses further. Are there people working against you? Hatonn's answer is absolute. There is no possibility of working against us. We are in the service of the creation. We extend our love to all of the creation. There is no possibility existing for a portion of this creation to work against us, for it is part of us.

But what of the dark groups, the destroyers of Atlantis and Lemuria, the one called Satan? Hatonn yields the instrument to another source for this, and the answer reframes evil itself. The one known as Satan, the voice says, was interested in experiencing the result of a desire: a desire of individualization. A desire for isolation.

In our understanding, this is not possible. The creation is full of the expressions of the Creator. Isolation is only possible through the creation of illusion. In creating the illusion of isolation and intense individuality, the one known as Satan has experienced his desire. He has attempted to serve others in giving to them the experience of isolation. And many have sought this experience.

I sit with that for a long time. Evil, in this telling, is not a force opposed to the creation. It is a desire for separateness, granted by a creation that grants every desire, experienced inside an illusion of isolation that was never real.

There are groups, Hatonn says, who express themselves in ways that were never considered by the original Thought. The original Thought, however, provided for no limits on expression. We consider some expressions evil. They consider them expressions. And still he says: we would freely serve them in any way that we could. However, they do not desire this. Therefore, we do not serve.

Even the darkness is met with an open hand. It simply does not reach back.

There is one more thread in this long evening worth holding. Hatonn tells the group that each of them will become a channel of communication between the Confederation and the multitudes on the surface. But the service has a hard limit, and he states it plainly: we can only do as much in this area as you desire. For this is the limitation of all of our service: to do only as much as is desired. They will not force the truth on anyone. There will be many who do not desire this information, and they will not have it proved to them. Each of the Creator's children has what they desire, regardless of the consequences. That is the plan, and even the Confederation does not override it.

Thank you for listening.

title: How to Meditate
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: how to meditate.

The second meditation of February eighteenth, nineteen seventy-four, is brief, and it is entirely practical. The group has asked Hatonn to speak on meditation itself, and he gives them the instructions the way you would give someone directions to your house: plainly, in order, nothing extra.

The first and most important thing, he says, is that you allow the conscious mind to relax. Relieve it of thoughts that are of a transient nature. And most of the thoughts concerning daily activities, he notes, are of a transient nature.

Sit in a quiet place, he says, with the spine erect. This is the most important of the techniques of meditation. A silent place is very beneficial, but it is not necessary. It helps a beginner more than it helps someone experienced.

To remove the intellectual concepts that keep the mind circling through transitory thoughts, he suggests that something to fascinate the intellect can at times be of use: music, or what you have called a mantra. This, however, is not necessary.

What is necessary is that thoughts of an intellectual nature be allowed to leave the consciousness. That is the whole technique. Not forced out. Allowed to leave.

I love how little there is to it. No posture beyond an erect spine. No silence required. No mantra required. Only the relaxation of the conscious mind and the release of the day's transient thinking, so the mind becomes receptive to things of other than a transient nature.

It is worth remembering who is giving this advice. This is the same voice that has spent weeks telling the group that meditation is the single mechanism by which the truth of the creation is recovered: the way around the intellect, the way into the soul, the way desire is understood, the way service is learned. And when asked how to do the one thing he never stops recommending, his answer fits in a few sentences.

Sit down. Straighten the spine. Let the day go. Let the thoughts go. That is the doorway he has been pointing at all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: What You Take With You
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: what you take with you.

On a Thursday evening in February of nineteen seventy-four, Hatonn returns to the subject of desire, and this time he follows it all the way to the end of a life. Desire, he says, dwells within each of the Creator's children. But what the desire is depends on the vibratory level of the individual. The lower the vibration, the more basic the desire. The higher the vibration, the higher the desire.

As you increase your vibration through meditation and seeking and service, your desire will change. The things desired by those tightly locked within the physical illusion are not those desired by those on the verge of freedom. And the verge of freedom is itself a product of desire, going hand in hand with increased awareness.

The technique for refining desire is the one he always gives. Avail yourself to the reality and truth of the creation through meditation, and then act upon the desires generated by the availing.

He states the aim of the whole practice in a single question. How is it possible to achieve what you actually desire, and that is to remove from your thinking desires of any nature except those of unity with the creation and those of service for your fellow man? That is the refinement: not the killing of desire, but its narrowing, until only two desires remain. Unity. Service. Everything else falls away on its own, the way leaves fall when the season changes, not because they are torn off. These desires will be somewhat different from the ones you experienced before. The desire to seek will be generated from seeking. It is a self-perpetuating phenomenon.

Why do we continue to tell you to meditate? he asks, as if hearing the group's unspoken impatience. To understand your desires. To understand yourself. To become aware of seeking, and of what it is you actually do. Why do we spend so much time on these subjects that so many on your planet would consider trivial? Because, he says, these are the only subjects that are not trivial.

It is of no value at all to seek within the illusion that you now know as your physical world. What you seek there, and what you find, is not lasting. It is stated in your world that you cannot take it with you. This is fact.

And then the line this episode is named for. What you take with you past the boundaries of the physical illusion is one thing. That is your mind. This mind that you take with you is, in reality, all that there is.

You dwell now, he says, in an illusion designed for the schooling of this mind. The teachers provided for this schooling are seldom heard. But the schooling takes place anyway. Every desire refined, every act of service, every sitting in silence: these are not preparations for some later examination. They are the shaping of the one thing you keep.

So the question is not what you will accumulate. It is what your mind will have become, when everything else is set down.

Why does he return to this subject again and again, week after week, when so many on the planet would call it trivial? Because these are the only subjects that are not trivial, he says. The markets, the achievements, the carefully arranged illusion of a life: none of it crosses the boundary. Only the mind crosses, carrying whatever shape your desires have given it. The time to shape it is not later. The time is the present sitting, the present act of service, the present choice of what to want.

He knows the group hears the difficulty in all of this. The contact begins, in fact, with the instrument failing: R cannot receive the thoughts, and Hatonn moves to another channel, then uses the moment to teach. A new instrument must clear the mind completely, he says, and attempt not to analyze what he is saying, but simply to say it. It is better to make errors in communication, which we later correct, than to fight the concepts we impress upon you. Even the channeling itself is a practice in desire: relax, receive, and let the mind become what it will carry with it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Fertile Field
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the fertile field.

A Friday evening in February of nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn gives the group an image for how the mind actually works. When you are meditating, he says, when you are in a receptive state, your mind is being programmed. The things that you program your mind with are things that will manifest, for you program your mind with the things that you desire.

Whatever you sow in the fertile fields of the mind, you also reap in the physical manifestation. That is his sentence, and it is worth hearing twice. The mind is soil. Meditation is the sowing. What grows in your life was planted while you were quiet.

The people of your planet, he says, are constantly programming themselves into undesirable experiences. This is completely unnecessary. It is ignorance. It is difficult to fully comprehend the power that a man has at his use through his desire.

The session then turns to the work ahead. The Confederation is here, he says, to help those of this planet who would help themselves and, by doing this, would help others. Each of you will be a channel of communication for the understanding of the truth of the creation. It will require effort. It is not a simple task to raise the understanding of a large number of those who will shortly be seeking. But with effort and diligence, it will be accomplished.

I love the practical note that follows, because it answers the most common objection to everything the voices teach. We realize, he says, that it is difficult to find time for sufficient meditation. But it is possible to avail yourself in meditation at various times during the day, when formal meditation is not possible. Clear the mind of the thoughts generated by the illusion at odd moments. Become at one with the creative consciousness that is in all of us. He suggests this in addition to the formal sitting, not instead of it.

Then the boundary, stated with unusual firmness. We are here to bring truth to those that seek it. But it is necessary that an individual seek truth, if he is to find it. It would be a direct violation of the principles of creation to attempt to serve those of your planet who do not seek our service. Concern yourselves, therefore, with those who seek. For they are the ones we are here to serve.

And the closing promise, which is really the law of desire stated one more time. The degree of your service will depend upon the degree of your seeking. This is always the way. If you seek to be of service to your fellow man, this you shall surely accomplish. For it has been provided by the Creator that if an individual seeks anything, this is what he shall find.

Sow carefully. The field is listening.

He returns once more to the strangeness of the central claim, because he knows how it sounds. We cannot overemphasize, he says, the need to realize the truth that one only experiences what one desires. We realize this is a completely different way of thinking on your planet, but it is necessary that you realize this. Not as a consolation. As a mechanics.

And he gives the group their dignity back. Your service, he tells them, in many ways is much greater than ours.

There will be many questions asked of you in the future, he says, and in order to answer them it is necessary that each of you be prepared. This will require effort. It is not a simple task to raise the understanding of a large number of those who will shortly be seeking understanding. But with effort and diligence, it will be accomplished. The preparation is not study. It is the daily clearing of the mind, so that when the questions come, the answers are already there, sown in the fertile field, ready to be reaped. For you must work within conditions that are much more difficult than those within which we now work. The ones inside the illusion, doing the slow work of waking inside it, are doing the harder job. However, each of you will be successful in your efforts to serve your fellow man. For this is what you seek. And it has been provided that if an individual seeks anything, this is what he shall find.

Thank you for listening.

title: No Destruction, Only Change
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: no destruction, only change.

The first meditation of February twenty-third, nineteen seventy-four, is the most dramatic session in this part of the archive. Hatonn speaks, under a heavy control of the instrument, of conditions soon to manifest upon the planet: physical changes of great magnitude, obvious to many, feared by many. And the group, quite reasonably, wants to know exactly what is coming.

What he gives them first is not a prediction but a principle. There will be events of a physical nature, he says, which from the point of view of those living within the illusion will be of a very destructive nature. However, there is no such thing as destruction. There is only change. This you must understand.

I want to stay with that sentence, because everything else in the session hangs from it. No destruction. Only change. The end of a form is not the end of anything real. It is the rearrangement of what was always there.

The cause, as Hatonn describes it, is a mismatch of vibrations. The planet is passing through the last portion of what you know as the third-density vibration, moving into the fourth. The thought generated upon and within the planet for thousands of years is out of harmony with the new vibration, and the disharmony will release energy of a physical nature: earthquakes, storms, volcanic eruptions, a shift of the poles. This is looked upon by those of us who understand it, he says, as an extremely beneficial change. It will not be considered good by those within the illusion.

Labeling this change good or bad, he says, is dependent upon the individual observing the change and his orientation. In a normal transition there would be no energy released at all. Your planet is an aberration, because its people generated a thought so out of harmony that the passage cannot be smooth.

And yet, inside the warning, there is mercy. This change will alert many who are lightly slumbering, and many who are slumbering relatively deep. Many will, at this time, be what is known in many of your religions as saved. It will save them, because they will get the violent awakening necessary to raise their vibrations that last amount, to get them off the fence, so to speak.

The task of the group, then, is preparation. Those who wish to serve will have at their door many who have been awakened and are afraid. There will be much misunderstanding. But there is one thing that is always understood, Hatonn says, and that is love. Your demonstration of this principle will be the greatest benefit you can offer to those that seek to learn.

He gives them the old words to carry: yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me. These are not false words, he says. Those words are meant for you.

And underneath it all, the teaching that never changes. Each individual in the creation possesses all of the information in the creation, for each individual is a portion of the creation. The only reason for a lack of availability of this information is that the individual has desired to limit himself, for the sake of his own experience. There is one single simple Thought behind all of it. In your language, this thought is expressed as love.

No destruction. Only change. And love underneath the change, holding it all.

The group asks, naturally, about meeting the Confederation directly, about landing on the land they have bought. Hatonn's answer is dry and absolute. It is impossible to own a piece of the creation, he says. The rights and privileges the group worries about are the gifts of the Creator, and the illusion that says otherwise will very rapidly cease to exist as the change manifests. There will be aid given to groups, he says. These groups will number in the tens of thousands. It will not be necessary to convince the illusion of anything.

And when they ask whether wanting to meet is the same as desiring to meet, he draws the distinction the whole archive turns on. Many receive things they believe they do not desire, he says, but in truth they desire precisely what they are receiving. True desire is not the wanting of the surface mind. It is known only through meditation. What you truly desire, he tells them, is that you grow in a spiritual sense, so that you may better serve your fellow man, fulfilling your desire, his desire, and the desire of the Creator.

Thank you for listening.

title: True Wealth
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: true wealth.

The second meditation of February twenty-third, nineteen seventy-four, opens with a story. Hatonn says he would like to tell them one, because it has several aspects. There once was a man who dwelled upon this planet who had such wealth he thought he had great security, for with his wealth he was able to do or have done whatever he wished.

But the wealth this man had, Hatonn says, was not wealth as you would interpret it today. The wealth that this man had was a wealth of knowledge, and in this wealth of knowledge he saw great security, for the knowledge that he had was the knowledge of truth. And in this truth, there was knowledge of security. For in the knowledge of truth, he says, there is the only security.

Today, upon your planet, security is sought by your peoples. They seek wealth as security, and yet they do not have it, for they do not know what wealth is. Wealth is thought of today in its material sense by most of the people of your planet. Only a very few understand true wealth.

We are attempting to give you true wealth and true security, he says. The wealth that we are attempting to give you cannot be taken from you. Even though you may leave your physical body in death, it is a wealth that can be carried with you. It is a security that encompasses all of the creation, for in this knowledge you are once more in total harmony with all that exists, and therefore you are in possession of all that exists. And this is the ultimate wealth.

I love the economics of that. True wealth is not having everything. It is knowing you are everything, so there is nothing left to acquire. It cannot be stolen, taxed, inflated away, or buried with you. It travels.

Then the teaching on provision, which belongs beside the story. It has been said that you should take no thought of what is to come tomorrow, but exist for service in the present. This is truth, he says, for everything has been provided for you. It is impossible to create a security by acting so as to accumulate material wealth. This security does not exist. It exists only within the illusion.

Consider the birds and the animals in the wild, he says. The Creator has provided for them that which they need. The food you eat was designed by the Creator. The sun that brings you light and warmth was designed by the Creator. Everything was provided for you. Man on Earth has strayed into darkness and built an illusion that causes him to think it necessary to struggle against problems that he considers a natural part of the creation.

And here is the image I keep returning to. These problems that he creates in his struggling: as one entangled in a mesh of brambles becomes more entangled in struggling, so does man on Earth become entangled in his own manifestations. The harder he fights the illusion, the deeper it holds him.

Who is created to suffer? he asks. He has created it himself in his lack of understanding, and this is not necessary, my friends. All of the supply for the sustenance of physical life is provided by one source. That source is the Creator. If all of these things are provided for you, how is it possible to doubt the objective of the Provider?

Live in the present, he says, and serve the Creator in any way you find opportune. This is your reason for existence: to serve. For this is the Creator's reason for existence: to serve.

The man in the story had it right. The only vault that cannot be broken into is the knowledge of truth. Everything else is a bramble.

He is gentle about the ones still caught. Why should you learn lessons from those who know nothing, he asks, who have built a complex illusion not even remotely related to truth? And then he softens it at once: their ignorance is no more their fault than it is your fault. It is simply an ignorance due to a lack of education. No blame. Only an unmet need. And that, he says, is why the Confederation is here at all: to remedy this lack of education, speaking on subject after subject until the service is accomplished. A service that must be desired by those who receive it. If it is not desired, then they cannot serve. That is their understanding of truth.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Great Trance
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the great trance.

We are going back to the very beginning. February of nineteen seventy-four. The first meeting of the archive, the first time Hatonn speaks through this instrument to a small room of people. And he does not waste the opening. He tells them, in the plainest language he can find, what matters most. Seeking, my friends, he says, is the most important thing that you do.

Think about that for a moment. Not serving. Not meditating. Not believing. Seeking. All of us in this creation seek, he says. The question is never whether you are seeking. The question is what you are seeking. And here he gets honest about the people of this planet. Many of them seek, he says, but they do not seek things that are of value. Every day they are handed suggestions about what they should chase, and if they stopped to examine them, they would find that most of them are worth very little.

There is a strange detail buried in this opening session, and I keep coming back to it. Hatonn says the people of Earth chose their incarnation for the purpose of seeking truth, and then forgot. They came here on purpose, and then fell asleep on arrival. He does not scold them for it. But he does name the machinery of the sleep. The religions of the world, he says, have for the most part eliminated the responsibility for individual seeking. Somebody else does the seeking for you. Somebody else tells you what was found. It is, in his words, an extremely erroneous point of view.

And then he gives the sleep its name. They are, he says, truly in a state of trance. They have been hypnotized by suggestions of social systems which have been built up by erroneous thinking through many centuries. I love how direct that is. Not confused. Not misled. Hypnotized. Centuries of bad suggestions, stacked on top of each other, until the suggestion feels like reality.

So why do the voices not simply wake everyone up? This is the part of the session that explains the whole archive, really. It comes down to asking. If the population of a planet asks for our services, Hatonn says, then we may give them freely. If only a portion asks, we must limit our services. If none asks, we can give none. That is why, he says, you find us in a state of hiding. It is not a mystery. It is courtesy. The Creator's law is that nothing real is forced on anyone.

Then what do you do, if you are one of the few who are awake in the trance? His answer is beautifully small. Be an example. Not a preacher. An example. Those who are in great need of truth will notice that you are different, he says. They will notice that you will have an inner peace and tranquility. They will come to you and ask. And then you can serve them, the way the voices serve you.

And there is one more instruction, and it is the one I want to leave you with. When you share what you know, present it so that it may be rejected. Do not force it on anyone who did not ask. The goal, Hatonn says, is to create within the individual an intense seeking that is his own. Borrowed conviction does nothing. The hunger has to be yours.

He is also honest about the scale of the work. Shortly, he says, many of your people will be seeking much information, and more of them are seeking it already. But they are difficult to reach, mixed in as they are with those who want nothing to do with it. So the work must grow. More channels. More information, by more means. And the instruction for the ones already awake is wonderfully undramatic. Act as you are directed through your daily meditations, he says. And we will, with you, succeed.

So tonight, a question to carry into the quiet. What have you been seeking lately? And is it yours?

Thank you for listening.

title: There Is No Death
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: there is no death.

Same night, second meeting. Hatonn is still working with the new channels in the room, teaching them how to receive. And then the questions start coming. Real questions, the kind people actually lie awake with. What happens to the body? What is death? Listen to how patiently he handles them, and how far he goes.

But first, the teaching on the channeling itself, because it sets up everything else. The instrument, Hatonn says, has learned to make his mind a blank. It is only when you clog your mind with your own thoughts that it is very difficult for us to get through. Thinking about nothing, he says, is not at all complex. It is like learning to ride a bicycle. Once you learn it, you do not forget it. But you must practice to keep the skill.

I love that line about the bicycle, because it punctures something. We imagine receiving the infinite as a great mystical achievement. Hatonn describes it as a practiced emptiness. The conditioning they do, the strange physical sensations the new instruments feel, is simply a means of helping the individual think of nothing. That is all. Nothing.

Then his brother Laitos speaks, and gives the sentence I want you to hold. There is no separation, he says. It is an illusion, but it is very strong for you at this time. Everything in this episode, and honestly everything in the archive, is commentary on that one sentence.

Hatonn leads the room into a short meditation first. Concentrate, he says, on that which is all. Let your thoughts become one. For all is one. Become aware that you are one and that one is all. Do not separate yourselves from anything. You are not separate from anything. There is only one thing. That one thing is truth.

And then someone asks about the physical body, about the changes coming to the planet, and whether bodies will be destroyed. Hatonn does not flinch. Your physical body will be destroyed, he says. There is not a single physical body upon the surface of this planet that will not be destroyed. You already know this. It is what you call death. It is a natural cycle.

But listen to the turn. What is death, he asks them back. What is the physical body? The reason you have the concept of death, he says, is that you are unable to communicate with those whom you consider dead. There will come a change in the density of this planet, and after it, there will be no inability to communicate between levels of awareness. Therefore, he says, there will be no awareness of the concept of death. The word will simply stop meaning anything.

Someone asks the obvious follow-up. Should we practice dying in meditation, to make the transition easier? Should we rehearse leaving the body? And Hatonn's answer is four words long, and it is the whole teaching. There is only one thing to practice. That is meditation.

There is one more exchange I want you to hear, because it shows his dryness. Asked whether some will be taken up bodily in craft during the coming changes, Hatonn answers with a question of his own. There will be a change of density, he says. The physical body as you know it will not be in evidence in the fourth density. You would have no need for this dense a body. Do you wish to retain it, and remain in the third density? I think not. The whole anxious apparatus of escape fantasies, punctured in two sentences.

He will not be drawn into timelines or predictions, either. Asked when the great change will come, the instrument balks, and Hatonn respects the boundary. He gives concepts, he says, not the kind of specific information that feeds the hunger for dates. The hunger for dates is the illusion talking.

So the episode ends where the archive always ends. The body goes. That was never in question. What you are does not. There is no death because there was never a separation to die out of. Only the illusion was ever separate, and illusions do not die. They dissolve.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Self-Inflicted Wound
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the self-inflicted wound.

Third meeting, same night, and a new voice enters the archive. Not Hatonn this time. Philip, of the Brotherhood of the Seven Rays. He speaks for only a few minutes. And in those few minutes he says one thing, over and over, from every angle he can find, until it cannot be misunderstood.

Here it is. You and the Father are one. He and you are one and I and you are one and we are all one. There is nothing else but the Father and I.

He knows how hard this is to hear from inside a human life. It is very difficult loving in the society that you now enjoy, he says, and that might be the most compassionate sentence in the early archive. He is not pretending it is easy. Your days are beset by difficulties. You are constantly confused and drawn into unimportant problems. And into that noise he drops a single stone: in everything you do and in everything you see and in everything you touch there is nothing but the Father. For He is and you are.

Then he widens the lens until it hurts. Throughout your planet there are many peoples of many races, and each thinks many things. But you must see them and know them as one. Not as a metaphor. As a fact. Each of them is a part of the Father as a part of you. And not only the people. All of the trees and flowers and rocks, all of the planets and stars, are part of that one great Being.

And what has man done with this simplicity? He has divided and subdivided. He has killed his fellow creatures in great profusion. He has generated hatred for his fellow creatures, and in doing so has generated this hatred for himself. Listen to how Philip puts it, because this is the line the whole episode turns on. To hate your fellow men, my friends, is to hate yourself. Every act of hatred is a self-inflicted wound.

Sit with the logic of it for a second. If there is only one being, then there is no one else to wound. The millions of planets he describes, full of peoples who do not hate, do not fear, do not envy, do not judge, are not morally superior. They have simply understood the arithmetic. How is it possible to do any of these things if there is only one being? You cannot strike your enemy without striking yourself, because your enemy is yourself, wearing a different face.

He borrows the old words at the end. I and my Father are one. These are true, these spoken words. And then the instruction, which is not an instruction to believe. Know this and this alone and you will know enough. But know it, my friends. Do not think it. Do not speak it. Do not accept it. Know it. For when you know it, you will then know love.

I keep returning to that sequence. Do not think it. Thinking is the mind handling the idea like an object. Do not speak it. Speaking is performance. Do not accept it. Accepting is borrowing someone else's knowing. Know it. The kind of knowing that changes how you reach for a glass of water.

And notice what Philip says about the alternative to this knowing. Man on Earth attempts to separate and divide and subdivide, and this is not truth. Truth is simplicity itself, he says, and yet man has complicated this truth to such an extent as to kill his fellow creatures in great profusion. The complications are not sophisticated. They are expensive. Every subdivision has a body count.
