Are you aware, my friends, that you may desire to be a star? Are you aware, my friends, that it is permissible to desire any and all of the understandings that you wish to know?

Permissible. As if somewhere there were a rule against wanting too much, and he has come to repeal it. You may desire to be a star. You may want the highest things. The only requirement is that the desire be aimed at its true target.

And what is the true target? The shape of the path, he says, is ever towards the infinity of the circle of unity. As you reach the reality of planet, of star, of open space, of infinity itself, as you begin to become aware of how far your desire may take you towards the love of the Father, then turn back to the present and concentrate upon the purity and the essence of this desire.

You wish to know, to understand, and to accept the truth, the highest truth. And as you do this, my friends, you will be moving. As well as you do this, so well will you move towards that which you seek, for it is desire alone that will impel you forward. Your desire, my friends. Your desire. We can only encourage you and give you food for thought.

Desire alone impels you forward. Not technique. Not merit. Not the approval of any teacher. The fire itself is the engine. Everything else is kindling.

And then he gives the image the whole evening is named for. The sun shines beautifully upon your planet, everywhere the same, and yet, my friends, if you have what you call a lens, the sunlight may be so focused that it will burn paper. This, my friends, is desire. Desire to know the infinite Creator in the highest way of which you are capable.

Sunlight falls on everything equally. It warms the stone and the field without choosing. But gather it through a lens, bring it to a point, and it burns through paper. That is what focused desire does. The light was always there. The lens is the wanting. Meditation, he says, is the focusing point.

The second half of the session turns darker. Hatonn speaks, through a struggling contact, of the centuries in which the people of this planet have given almost no consideration to the spiritual nature of creation. This is a great mistake, he says. The creation is entirely of what you would call a spiritual nature. There is nothing else. It appears to you to be of a certain nature, but this is simply because your awareness is limited to the boundaries of this particular nature.

And he is candid about the mission's limits. There will be no general proof of their reality, no convincing display. They must serve only those who desire their service. For each of the Creator's children must be free to seek what he desires, regardless of any other interpretation of the value of those desires. Even the fire of desire must be freely chosen. Especially that.

So tonight, one question to carry into the quiet. What is your fire pointed at? The sunlight is already falling on you, everywhere the same. The lens is in your hands.

Seek, my friends. Seek and focus.

Thank you for listening.

title: Understanding Is Demonstration
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: understanding is demonstration.

April thirteenth, nineteen seventy-four. A Saturday. Hatonn opens with a question, and then refuses to let you answer it the way you want to. What is it that you seek? You seek understanding. And what is understanding? Then he takes apart every definition you might offer, one by one.

Understanding, my friends, is not precisely what you think it is. Understanding is not an intellectual interpretation of the creation or of its realities. It is not an emotional response to reality in the most approved fashion. Understanding is not an emotional or intellectual response to your fellow creatures. Understanding, my friends, is very, very simply understanding the demonstration of the love of your Creator.

I want to read that again, because it is the hinge of the whole evening. Understanding is the demonstration of the love of your Creator. Not the theory of it. Not the feeling about it. The demonstration. Understanding is something you do, with your hands, in your day. This, my friends, is understanding. This is what we attempt to bring to you: understanding of the demonstration of His love. For this, my friends, is the understanding of all that there is. For His love is all that there is, for this love has created all that there is.

And this is what is sought by those who seek, whether they are aware of it or not. They simply seek to understand His love, and thereby to demonstrate it. To demonstrate it in every thought, in every word, and in every deed.

There is a beautiful honesty in what Hatonn says next. It might be asked, he says, why we of the Confederation bother to communicate more than this one simple concept. And his answer is disarming. We have, in this simple statement, given you the very core, the essence, in actuality the totality of what we wish to convey to you. Everything else they have ever said, across all these sessions, is commentary on that one sentence. But, he says, we will give you more. More, so that you too can serve. So that you will be equipped to help those who seek but must be led through their own pathways to the understanding of this very simple truth. For man on Earth is very complex, and is unable, for the most part at this time, to receive this simple truth and use it.

The simple truth needs a complex delivery system, because the recipients are complex. That is why there are years of sessions, and mystery, and enticement. He admits it outright. We have for many of your years enticed those who would seek by various methods. They would have preferred to come directly to the point. But experience taught them that the direct approach produces a very shallow harvest of seekers. The illusion is strong, even for those who desire to seek. So they worked patiently, for years, to arouse the seeking first, and only then to satisfy it.

Then the tape turns over, and Hatonn returns with the second half of the teaching, the part that gives the evening its spine. Each time we speak of understanding, he says, we always link it to service. And he wants you to know why. We are not attempting to draft you. We are not choosing your future for you. The reason is a simple law of reality. There is balance, my friends, in all things.

The most exalted and pure understanding, he says, is an empty shell if it is not expressed. There is a limit to how far you may go in understanding if you do not choose to express your understanding through demonstration in service. If you wish to receive, you simply give. This is a law.

And then the image that closes the teaching, one of my favorites in the whole archive. Each entity that you meet is yourself turned over. The other side of you. The other side of the coin, my friends. The side you cannot see of yourself, turned suddenly so you may see it. There you are. Serve your fellow man, my friends.

Every stranger is the back of your own head, turned around so you can finally look at it. That is why service is not charity. It is self-recognition.

And Hatonn is candid about his own stake in this. We are here by our service to you, he says, because by our service we advance ourselves in understanding. We are not aware of any other means of effectively creating a forward movement in our own understanding. The teachers are students. The helpers are being helped. The coin has no edge, only two faces, each serving the other.

So the evening's equation is short. Understanding is the demonstration of love. Demonstration is service. Service is the only road upward, for them as for you. Seek it in meditation, he says, and then spend it on each other, in every thought, in every word, in every deed.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Augmented Century
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the augmented century.

April fourteenth, nineteen seventy-four, the first of two sessions that day. Hatonn is speaking from a craft, and he begins with a word game. Let us consider, my friends, the meaning of identified. Identified is something that you understand. What do you understand? The peoples of your planet believe that they understand many things. They do not understand the unidentified flying objects in their skies. What they do not realize is that they do not understand anything, for they have not attempted to understand anything.

It is a bracing opening. And it sets up the evening's real subject, which is stranger than spacecraft. It is your own century.

Your science has created what you consider to be many marvels, he says, but these marvels lack true understanding. And then he tells them something they could not have guessed. Within the past one hundred of your years there has been an advance in your knowledge, what you consider to be science, of many, many thousand-fold. This advance was not brought about unaided. This advance was highly augmented, my friends, for a purpose.

The technological explosion of the last hundred years, the telephones and airplanes and all the rest of it, was not an accident of human cleverness. It was seeded. Augmented. Given. And Hatonn names the purpose, and it is not what you would expect. It was not to make life easier, though it did. It was not to build weapons, though it did that too, and he is sorry for it. The entire technological advance your civilization has experienced in the past one hundred or so years, he says, has been for the purpose of increasing the ability of those who seek new intellectual answers to find intellectual answers which will lead them to non-intellectual truths.

Read that slowly. The machines were given so that the seekers could find books. The printing presses and radios and libraries, the whole apparatus of mass communication, exist so that a person hungry for truth can find the words that will lead her past words. It is difficult, he says, for a society intent upon maintenance of the physical body to spend much time actively seeking in a spiritual way. And it is difficult for those who seek spiritual truths to find them if there is very little dissemination or publication available. Technology spared people physical labor and gave them leisure, and gave them the means to share what they found. Those are the ones the Confederation is concerned with: those who have been provided with more leisure time to extend their seeking.

This is not the decision of any particular person, he says. It is not the decision of a council. It comes about in a more natural way, as entities near the end of a cycle are drawn into physical experience, bringing with them the memory of previous advancement, which is then reflected in their works. It was the same, he says, upon the continents known as Atlantis and Lemuria. Great technological flowering, just before the change. Many of those who dwelled within that experience, he says, are now returning, and have returned into the physical, to experience once more a termination, a change, and this time an even more grand change than that which they experienced before.

Many of you, in other words, have done this before. You were there for the last flowering. You came back for this one.

And then Hatonn says something grave and reassuring at once. He agrees that it does not seem wise for such technological advance to fall upon a people whose spiritual qualities are so lacking. We are in complete agreement, he says. But they cannot control it. There is, however, one exception to their non-interference, and he states it plainly. They are able and willing, if necessary, to terminate certain totally insane actions with respect to your nuclear weapons. These weapons endanger not only the peoples of your planet spiritually, but threaten to terminate their existence. Interference to stop such warfare, he says, is within that which we will accomplish.

One more observation closes the teaching, and it is quietly devastating. The teachings of the one known as Jesus, he says, reached almost no one for many years after his passing. At this time their dissemination is at its maximum. There now exists upon your planet a communication system which will reach a very large percentage of the peoples of your planet's surface. And yet, he says, his teachings are not understood.

The century gave you the means to carry the message to everyone. The message is everywhere now. And still it is not understood. Because understanding, as another evening taught, was never going to come through the machinery. The machinery was only ever the envelope. The letter inside is read in silence.

So the next time you pick up the small glowing rectangle in your pocket, remember what it was augmented for. Not for the noise. For the seeking. It was built, in part, so that you could find your way past it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Lessons From Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: lessons from within.

April fourteenth, nineteen seventy-four, the second session of the day. Shorter. Quieter. Hatonn is speaking about something every person in the room is living: the shape of their own lives. The difficulty, he says, is the constant use of the intellect, taught to all people who have been at all educated. The body grows. The intellect grows. The schools and the machines see to that. There is much lacking after these two items have become mastered.

What is lacking is the training of the spirit. And the question he takes up is a practical one: what do you do about it, inside the life you already have?

His answer begins with a reframe. Each situation that surrounds you, he says, is in general a part of a lesson, or a lesson for you. Not the daily details, not the small accidents that occur under the simple laws of chance. He means the overall trend. The generalized direction of your situation. Whatever the difficulty is in that situation, take it to meditation. Come out of meditation with some understanding, not of your life, but simply in you, of the lesson of the job to be done within that situation. Then do the job, in as workmanlike and cheerful a manner as your meditation has given you the ability to maintain.

I love the modesty of that. Not: understand your life. Just: understand the job inside the situation. Do it well. Do it cheerfully, to the extent that the quiet has made cheer possible. And then this promise: as you accomplish your work within that lesson, the circumstances about you will alter of their own accord.

You do not change the circumstances. You learn the lesson, and the circumstances change themselves. The work is inside. The scenery rearranges around it.

And then the sentence that the whole evening turns on. The constant feeling of pressure from outside is an illusion, my friends. Sometimes an extremely heavy one, but only an illusion. Your lessons will be learned from within.

An extremely heavy illusion. He grants the weight of it. The pressure feels real because, at the level of your nerves, it is. But the learning does not happen out there, in the pushing and the shoving. It happens in here, in the quiet where you finally see what the situation was teaching.

He is honest about the difficulty of raising children, or anyone, in this atmosphere. To truly train the spirit, he says, it would be necessary to have communities centered about the great truths of the spirit. A completely different type of environment than you have. We have not found rich earth for planting this idea in many places, he admits. However, you are welcome to it.

But he does not leave you with only the ideal. There is much, he says, that can be done within the sanctity of your own life. Those of like mind may provide for you, and those dependent upon you, an atmosphere conducive to spiritual growth. In your own household, much may be done to encourage the constant awareness of the love of the infinite Creator. Imagine a home where the growing ones become aware, as their bodies and minds mature, that their infinite and eternal spirit is real, and is capable of maturing also. Imagine a place they might choose to go, with no pressure and no suggestion, to seek their own peace and find their own truth.

No pressure. No suggestion. Just a door that stands open. That is his whole pedagogy in three lines.

And he closes with a reminder that steadies everything: all things are one, and so meditation on a regular basis will proceed with you as you go along the path. The technology presses hard against the seeking. It can seem a harsh antithesis. And yet the path goes on, quietly, underneath it all, the way a river goes on underneath a frozen surface.

So tonight, look at the general shape of your situation. Not the details. The shape. Ask the quiet what the job inside it is. Do that job, workmanlike and cheerful, to the best of the morning's meditation. And trust that the circumstances will alter of their own accord. They always do. That is what circumstances are for.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Island and the Sea
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the island and the sea.

April fifteenth, nineteen seventy-four. Oxal tries to speak first and the contact falters, so Hatonn steps in with a few small thoughts while the conditioning continues. Small thoughts. That is what he calls them. What he gives them is one of the loveliest images in the archive.

Consider, my friends, an island in an ocean channel, far out at sea. There is no land in sight. And this small rock, washed by waves, bleached by the sun, with small flora and fauna growing upon it, looks out upon the world, and its limited consciousness attempts to grasp the reality as it eddies and swirls about it.

The little island detects strange things as they enter its purview. It lives through differences in climate and feeling and mood. It experiences the seasons of its flora and fauna, and it attempts to piece together a reasonable and holistic view of its reality. It is fixed in position, my friends. A poor small rock. The far limits, wherefrom come the waves, and the far limits to which they return, will be forever unknown to the island. The island can never know or fully understand that which appears at its doorstep.

This, my friends, is a very rough and perhaps shallow example of the type of instrument the intellect is.

I love that he calls his own parable rough and shallow. He is telling you, even as he tells it, not to mistake the picture for the thing. The intellect, he says, is very useful within the imagery for which it was made. It is a fine tool for island business: sorting the flora, noting the seasons, building a reasonable view of the doorstep. But the attempt to use the intellect to understand the far limits of your origin, or the far limits of where you shall return again, is impossible. For in the image which your intellect works upon, you are a rock chained to one mooring. This is not reality. Nor can your intellect give you a picture of reality.

You cannot think your way to the far limits. The instrument is wrong for the depth. It would be like trying to hear color.

And then the turn, the sentence the whole parable exists to deliver. Rather, my friends, in meditation seek to be the water.

Seek to be the water. Not the island studying the water. The water itself. Seek the consciousness, the oneness, the unity, and the adventure of water. All water is inseparable. There is no separation. It flows. It is as one. And each wave that breaks upon this shore may have broken anywhere, and may move to another. Let your consciousness flow like the water, not like an island, inwardly.

I have sat with that image for a long time. The island asks: where did this wave come from, and where is it going? The water never asks. It was there, and here, and there again. Your consciousness, Hatonn is saying, is not the rock. It was never the rock. The rock is the body, the biography, the fixed position. You are the medium the rock sits in. You are the thing that touches everything.

Notice the word he slips in among the grand ones: adventure. The consciousness, the oneness, the unity, and the adventure of water. As if unity were not a still gray pond but something moving, going places, breaking on shores it has never seen. The mystical life, in this telling, is not static. It flows.

This is why meditation works, in his account, and intellect does not. Meditation does not improve the island's maps. It dissolves the sense of being an island at all. You sit, you quiet, and for a moment the mooring slips, and you are the water, and the far limits are not far, because there is no far in water. There is only water.

So the next time your mind is working hard on the great questions, building its careful models of where you came from and where you are going, remember the poor small rock, bleached by the sun, doing its best. Thank it for its work. And then, in the quiet, try being the sea instead.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Step Backward
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the step backward.

April sixteenth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn speaks through the one known as R, and he is in a reflective mood. There is always so much to say and so little time to say it in, he says, that given any opportunity to speak, we are glad to do so. And what he wants to say tonight is about a perplexity several in the group are feeling. Nothing serious, physically. Just the low hum of confusion that comes with trying to live a spiritual life inside an ordinary week.

He offers them two ways of looking at it, and he says both are valid. The first way will be familiar to anyone who has ever taken seeking seriously. Take a life-or-death attitude toward your understanding. Go after spiritual understanding as the life-and-death matter, as indeed it is. Pursue it the way you would pursue air if you were drowning.

And then the second way, which he says is the perfect opposite, equally valid, equally helpful, and too little practiced upon planet Earth. Simply do not worry about the meaning behind the illusory experiences that fill each day.

Do not worry. That is the teaching. It seems, he admits, in a way very shallow. But listen to the condition he attaches. Once you have aimed yourself toward the spiritual path, and have begun to discipline yourself with regular meditation, patiently and carefully kept up, then the ability to take the all-important step backwards, toward detachment from that which is about you in your daily life, is extremely important.

The step backward. Not the frantic lunge forward. The deliberate move away. Aim yourself, discipline yourself, meditate daily, and then, he says, stop clutching at every experience demanding to know what it means. Let the day be the day. The meaning will come, or it will not need to.

And he tells them what is at stake in that step. It may mean the difference, he says, between a great many perplexing situations and a feeling that is more often with you: that of the rhythm of the universe resounding recognizably in your life. When your worried mind is still, and when all the ripples of worry of your daily life have stopped, then, and only then, may you discern the flow and stately movement of the universal rhythms.

I love that image. The worried mind is a pond full of ripples, and you cannot see the current for the chop. Still the ripples, and the deep movement shows itself. It was always there. You were only looking at the surface you were making.

There is a humility in this session that I want you to hear. Hatonn admits, outright, that it is very difficult for them to say words that have the desired effect. We wish for our words to impel you, or inspire you, toward seeking. So many words remain simply words. We wish to effect the transformation from word to idea. Therefore, he says, we have more to say than we can ever say, and we have very, very little to say, for our truth is very simple.

More to say than can ever be said, and almost nothing to say. That is the whole archive in one breath. The truth is simple. The saying of it is endless. And somewhere between the saying and the silence, the transformation happens, or it does not.

He also reminds them, early in the session, of something easy to forget. Although we do not always speak to you during the meditation, we are always with you during your meditation. We are always listening, and glad to help. The silence in the room is not empty. It is attended.

So tonight's practice is the smallest one in this whole series. Aim yourself. Keep the discipline. And then take one step back from the worry. Let the ripples settle. Listen for the rhythm underneath. It is stately, he says. It has been moving all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: Let Go of Analysis
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: let go of analysis.

April seventeenth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn has come to talk about becoming a channel, and he begins with two people in the room. The ones known as E and T are not pleased with their progress. The conditioning does not seem to be taking. And Hatonn, with great kindness, diagnoses the problem. It is not their vibration. It is not their level of awareness. It is the amount of intellectual activity they are allowing their brains to function with.

In the case of E, he says, the amount of intellectual analyzing is considerable. The habit is very strong, and each imperceptible wave of conditioning received moves such a strong habit of analysis only very slightly. T is closer, because he has attempted, from time to time, to effectively refrain from analysis of data.

And then Hatonn states the requirement plainly. To become a channel is to temporarily trust another entity with the use of one's vocal mechanism. This involves letting the control go completely, and not retaining any amount of judgment over it. This is very difficult, or impossible, to achieve if there is any thinking going on at all on the part of the channel.

Any thinking at all. That is a high bar. But notice what he says next, because it is generous. The conditioning is deliberately intended to be effective only for those who have accepted the form of meditation which precludes analysis of thought. And: there is no doubt in my mind that each of you may be instruments if you desire to become instruments. It needs only complete relaxation, and a complete ability to refrain from analyzing any thoughts that you receive. It may take some time, as you know time. However, it is not only possible, but inevitable, if you continue to desire this service.

Inevitable. Not possible. Inevitable. The only variable is desire, held steadily, and time.

Then the session turns, and this is the part I carry with me. Hatonn senses their disappointment in themselves, and he addresses it directly. We are not disappointed at all, he says. We are very pleased, for we can see your progress. We are, however, aware of the disappointments you feel. And then he gives them the teaching on regret, which is one of the cleanest statements of it I have found anywhere.

There is no time but the present. Regret has to do only with the past.

We are not saying, he adds, that it is not your business to live as correctly as you know how. But the time to live correctly is the present moment. A mistake made, or a missed step, or a simple misunderstanding later corrected, is simply a corrected error. What matters is not that you have made the error, but that you have become aware of it and corrected it. The present, with the awareness that you have gained, is all that you need to consider. Waste no more time on what is gone forever than you need to learn from it. Then carry on with the life that you are living now.

A corrected error. Not a stain. Not a verdict on your character. A corrected error, which is to say: the system working as designed. You noticed. You adjusted. That is the whole story, and it ends in the present.

For, my friends, there is a great deal of each present moment that most of those upon your planet miss completely. The ability to live fully in the present, with full knowledge of what you see and hear of God's beautiful creation about you, is most rare and valuable.

I keep thinking about how these two teachings belong together. The channel must stop analyzing the thoughts as they come, must stop looking ahead and behind the words. And the person must stop analyzing the past, must stop looking behind at the error. In both cases the instruction is the same: let go of the commentary track. Relax. Speak the word you are given. Live the moment you are in.

The instrument makes an error near the end, and Hatonn simply continues through it, which feels like the teaching demonstrating itself. No pause for regret. Just the next true sentence.

So tonight: whatever you are disappointed in yourself about, hear him. They are not disappointed. They can see your progress. Correct the error, keep the awareness, and waste no more time on what is gone forever than you need to learn from it. The present is all you need to consider. It is also, he says, the most beautiful thing you are missing.

Thank you for listening.

title: One Understanding
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: one understanding.

April nineteenth, nineteen seventy-four. A Friday. There is a small domestic interruption at the start of the session, a cat named Gandalf who needs attention, and I mention it because I love that the archive keeps these moments. The infinite Creator, the Confederation of Planets, and a meowing cat, all in the same ten minutes. The teaching that follows is worthy of the company.

Hatonn says he has one thought to give them this evening. Our only aid to you, he says, is to give you a concept of understanding. What you are seeking is understanding. And then he says what the understanding is, and it is the shortest sentence in the session. There is only One.

This unity, he says, within which the entire creation resides, is whole, complete, unbreakable, and transcendent of all illusion. Therefore, my friends, it is the most impossible thing to conceive of within the boundaries of your intellect and your consciousness within the physical.

The most impossible thing to conceive. He does not ask you to conceive it. He asks you to notice that you cannot, and to understand why. The intellect is a divider. It knows things by cutting them apart. Unity cannot be cut. So the intellect, reaching for it, comes back empty, and calls the emptiness a mystery.

This consciousness of unity, which is your understanding described in one way, is available to you only through meditation. And then Hatonn says something wry and sad. It is quite amazing to us that those upon your surface have devised so many different ways of removing from themselves all indications of the reality, or even the possibility, of understanding. We build, in other words, elaborate machinery for not noticing. The noise, the hurry, the endless sorting of the world into pieces: all of it functions, whether we intend it or not, as insulation against the one thing that is true.

However, he says, you are, although in the physical environment, not of it. Your choice is completely free. You may seek for this understanding even within the dense illusion which occupies your physical senses. We offer you only simple help. We offer you only simple understanding, for there is only one understanding, only one truth, only one entity: the Creator, my friends.

Any attempt to work through any other understanding, he says, will be an attempt which is working within an extremely transient illusion. Everything else is weather. This is climate.

Later in the session, through another instrument, the teaching takes a practical turn. Many of your peoples, Hatonn says, do not comprehend that which you have come to accept. You need to grow in confidence, in order that you may be of beneficial service to these people. Many will approach you and will begin searching because of the confidence you display in the Creator. Your vibration shall rise, and shall be felt by those whom you come into contact with.

Confidence, not argument. The people who will seek from you will not be convinced by your reasoning. They will feel your steadiness and want to know where it comes from. Use what time remains, he says, to develop your confidence in His will.

And near the end, a line about channeling that I think applies to far more than channeling. When the conditioning wave is given, he says, the thoughts that are of a creative or spiritual nature will vibrate within your mind, and you will feel the impulse to speak. The question of whether these creative thoughts are yours or ours is somewhat unspiritual, in that those thoughts which are of a spiritual nature are the thoughts of the Creator. As they are in me, they are in you. And as they are in you, they are in everyone.

Whose thought is it? The question dissolves. If there is only One, then the thought that rises in you in the quiet, the true one, the loving one, was never yours or theirs. It was His, passing through, the way light passes through clean glass. Your only job is to be the glass, and to let it pass.

One understanding. One truth. One entity. Everything else is the cat meowing in the next room: real, and loud, and not the point.

Thank you for listening.

title: For the Adults
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: for the adults.

April twentieth, nineteen seventy-four. The first thirty minutes of the session are lost. The tape gives us only static and a note. Then Hatonn's voice comes through, and what he wants to talk about is who to serve, and how.

He begins with an image that runs through the whole evening. The people of Earth, he says, are fascinated by many things, because they are children, truly children in the evolutionary state of this vast universe. There are some who are not as fascinated with the things of childhood, who are seeking the things that are enjoyed by those whom we might consider adults.

Now, he is quick to say what he means, and it matters. I am speaking of the adult who is mature in a spiritual awareness. Many of your people are quite mature with respect to the planet's average maturity. They simply are unaware of the truth, of the reality of the creation in which they exist. Serve these, he says. Those who will understand.

And here is the discipline he lays down, and it is strict. It will be of no value to attempt to serve children with the information that we have given, for they will not understand it. No matter how you phrase it or how you prepare it for them, they will not understand it. For, as you know, a child does not understand many concepts. Prepare yourself, therefore, to serve the adults. Prepare to serve them well. For, in being adults, they will require that you, also, speak as an adult.

Speak as an adult. I keep turning that phrase over. It does not mean speak down, or speak with authority, or speak in jargon. It means: do not dilute the truth into entertainment. Do not perform. The mature seeker will recognize maturity, and nothing else will satisfy them. And it is simple to identify them, he says. They will understand. The child will not.

Do not do the child a disservice, he adds, by impressing upon him something that he cannot understand. There is a kindness in that I had not expected. Withholding the teaching is not snobbery. It is care. To press a truth onto someone who cannot hold it does them no service. It only confuses them, and it wastes the truth.

Serve those who seek. Serve those who will initiate their seeking very shortly. And remember, he says, if you are to serve those who are adult, it will be necessary that you speak with the knowledge of an adult. For this reason, it is very necessary that meditation be practiced daily. For in this way, and only in this way, can an individual become aware of what is necessary to give to those who seek. In no other way can he obtain this ability.

The qualification for teaching is not study. It is the daily quiet. The adult speaks from what the silence has shown him, and the other adult recognizes it, the way one musician recognizes another's tuning.

He is honest about the scale of the work. How many more of the peoples of this planet are seeking now than when we initiated our program? Considerably more, my friends. Considerably more. And yet their seeking is going, for the most part, unanswered. For there are all too few groups of this nature, groups able to act as goads for those who seek. I love that word. Goads. Not teachers, not masters. Goads. A small sharp thing that keeps the ox moving.

And then he names the deepest principle underneath it all. It will always be up to those living upon the surface of a planet such as this one to act, to convey to their brothers that which they desire: the truth of the creation. This must be the way of truth, for it was provided by the Creator of us all that those upon a planet such as this one would have a freedom of choice that is complete. This choice may not be influenced in a direct manner. This choice must include the only thing of importance in the universe: the individual's acceptance or rejection of his Creator.

The only thing of importance in the universe. He says it so quietly. Not knowledge. Not progress. Not even love, as an achievement. The choice itself. The free turning toward, or away. Everything the Confederation does, all the mystery and patience of their method, exists to protect that one thing from being coerced.

So the teaching tonight is a job description. Find the adults. They are the ones already looking. Speak to them as one adult to another, which means: from your meditation, plainly, without performance. Do not chase the children. Do not force the choice. Be the goad, the small sharp reminder, and let the turning happen in freedom.

For as it is known by the adult, he says, the rewards of true maturity are more desirable than those of childhood. And we, the Confederation, are serving those who wish to mature. For we also wish to mature.

Thank you for listening.

title: Across the Ocean
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: across the ocean.

April twenty-first, nineteen seventy-four. A Sunday. And a new voice enters the archive. Not Hatonn, not Oxal. The instrument speaks a name: Philip, of the Brotherhood of the Seven Rays. The contact is difficult. The tape is full of gaps. Whole sentences dissolve into inaudibility. What survives is fragmentary, but the fragments have a shape, and the shape is beautiful.

As I speak to you, he says, there is between us an ocean amount of space. My beloved brothers, you have truly bridged this chasm, this great ocean which lies between the understanding within the physical illusion, and we understand the dilemma in understanding.

An ocean amount of space. Not a distance measured in miles, but in kinds of knowing. On one shore: the physical illusion, the world of your senses and your certainties. On the other: the understanding he is trying to send across. And this small group, sitting in meditation, has built a bridge. The difficulties of communicating across this gap are formidable, he says. And yet, my friends, it must be done, and it can be done.

It must be done, and it can be done. I love the stubbornness of that. No hedging. The gap is real, the work is hard, and it is going to happen anyway, because it must.

You are truly a shepherd, he tells them. You are truly a disciple. To you, my brethren, is given a great task, but you are not left helpless. The ability which you have, with your contact, the One Who is All, in meditation, will stand.

And then the image that gives the evening its heart. It is very necessary, my friends, for you to shepherd your sheep. There is information about the other side of the ocean that needs to be expressed to all those standing on the shore, who are looking out to sea.

Picture it. A shoreline. People standing at the water's edge, looking out, sensing that there is something beyond the horizon but unable to see it. And the shepherds are the ones who have received word from the far shore, and whose work is to carry it back to the people on the beach. Not to drag anyone into the water. Just to say: there is another side. I have heard from it. Here is what I can tell you.

What you have done, my friends, is already an aid. There is much more that you may do, if you are willing. We will be of help to you in whatever way that we can. There are things that we can do, things that we have done, and things that we will do, if you desire us to aid you.

He knows they are tired, or will be. He knows the far shore looks impossibly distant some days. We are aware, my friends, that you long to be on a different part of the shoreline than the one you are now on, and that you wish to be, in spirit and in truth, within the sphere of understanding. As I say to you, my friends: we each have our part. Each of us has a service to perform, and when that service is done, the next service may begin.

We each have our part. The ones on the far shore have theirs: to send the word across the water. The ones on the near shore have theirs: to stand on the beach and speak it to the people looking out to sea. Nobody has to swim the ocean. You only have to do your part of the relay.

The contact breaks before he finishes. I am having trouble with this instrument, he says. I will leave you. And the tape runs out. But the fragments hold together. A voice from across an ocean of space, saying: the bridge you built is real. The people on the shore are waiting. Do your part.

Thank you for listening.

title: What True Seeking Is
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: what true seeking is.

April twenty-second, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn opens the evening, and he begins by drawing a line most people never draw. There are few people upon your planet who are seeking, he says. There are many who believe that they are seeking, but they are not seeking. They are simply going through motions and fooling themselves.

That is a hard sentence to sit with. So he tells you what the real thing is. What is seeking, my friends? What is true seeking? Seeking is an attempt to understand the desires of your Creator. Seeking is an attempt to understand why you are yourself, and how you may express the desire of your Creator. This, my friends, is true seeking.

Not the search for experiences. Not the collection of beliefs. The attempt to understand what the Creator desires, and to express it. Everything else that calls itself seeking is motion without direction.

Most of the people of your planet at this time, he says, are not aware of their true desires. They chase what glitters, and they call the chase a life. They are not aware of these desires because they have not availed themselves, through meditation, to this awareness. Avail yourself to your own desires, my friends. Do this through meditation, and you will make the progress that you wish to make.

Your true desires are not the ones shouting the loudest. They are the quiet ones underneath, and you meet them only in the quiet.

Then he redefines progress, and the redefinition is worth hearing slowly. All of the people throughout all of space wish to make progress, he says, but many do not understand what progress is. Most of the progress of which they are aware is quite transient, of no real value. Become aware of real progress. Become aware of what you must know in order to reunite your thinking with that of your Creator. That, my friends, is progress: the progress of understanding what you must know to, once more, think in exact harmony with the original created Consciousness. In this way, and in only this way, can you truly progress.

Progress is not going somewhere. It is coming back into tune. Like a stringed instrument, tightened until its note matches the note it was made to play. You do not travel to harmony. You remember it.

Later in the session, through another instrument, Hatonn speaks to the group about their work with those who will come to them for help. And he gives them a principle for reading the world that steadies everything. The interpretation of change and event is extraordinarily different when seen, first, from the standpoint of the illusion, and second, from the standpoint of the infinite being. There is no difficulty in physical change from the viewpoint of the eternal. These things are inevitable. These things are not to be feared. These things are part of a whole that is organic, natural, and extremely helpful as you cycle through the physical illusion.

Each experience that you have desired comes to pass, and you learn from them. Nothing is wasted. Nothing is off the plan, because the plan includes your learning from all of it.

Always remember, he says, that the human viewpoint is not what you, or those who seek from you, are truly seeking. Within meditation, see all things from their true perspective.

Then Oxal takes the instrument, and the evening takes a strange turn. He speaks of a sphere discovered on your southeastern coastline. A device, he says, for the projection of thought to a point on your planet. A remote amplifying device. It was not intended to be found. He is sorry that it has been discovered, though he doubts examination will reveal its purpose. It is our wish, he says, that the purpose of this sphere not be detected at this time.

The tape breaks off before he finishes, and the rest is inaudible. So I will leave the sphere where the archive leaves it: half explained, humming somewhere off the coast, a reminder that the unseen world has its instruments too, and that not everything is meant to be understood yet.

What is meant to be understood, tonight, is simpler. True seeking is the attempt to know what the Creator desires, and to express it in your thoughts and deeds. True progress is thinking in harmony with the original Consciousness once more. And the way there is the way it has always been: avail yourself, in meditation, to your own deepest desires, and you will find they were His all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Only Qualification
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the only qualification.

April twenty-third, nineteen seventy-four. The first twenty-four minutes of the session are inaudible. When Hatonn's voice comes through, he is talking about service, and about what it takes to be fit for it. And his answer is so simple it almost sounds like no answer at all.

In the future, he says, every member of this group who desires to serve those who seek this service will have the opportunity to serve. If this service is to be effective, it will be necessary for one offering service to fully qualify. These qualifications may be obtained in only one way. It is necessary to spend time each day in meditation. There is no other way.

No degree. No lineage. No special gift. The only qualification is the daily quiet. Everything else is commentary.

And he says why. We speak of true service, he says. Service that will bring to those who desire understanding the understanding which they desire. This is all that we are attempting to do, for this is all that is necessary. For once this understanding is acquired by an individual, he then needs nothing else. For he is then an integral part of the creation in every respect. He is no longer separated, in an illusory way, by the illusion which he and his fellow man have created for their experience. And this, my friends, is the only thing man on Earth needs: the understanding that allows him to dissolve the illusion in which he now finds himself.

The only thing man on Earth needs. He says it plainly. Not food, not justice, not peace among nations, though all of those matter. The one thing needful is the understanding that dissolves the illusion. Because the illusion is what makes all the other needs feel so desperate and so separate.

There are many ways to serve the people of a planet such as this one, he says. There is only one way to serve them with what they truly desire. Even though they do not realize it, they desire understanding. And there is only one way to bring them understanding. This we are attempting to do. You who seek to serve with us will find that this seeking and service will bring to you much joy, as it does to us.

Then comes the passage I want you to hear twice. Meditation will allow the individual to eliminate questions concerning the validity of the information that he receives from his thoughts. Meditation will allow the individual to become aware of reality, and therefore truth. This truth will be self-evident, and it will not be necessary for an instrument to seek an appraisal of that which he is able to channel or to speak. For through meditation he will know, as it is written in one of the holy books of your planet: know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

Free from what? He answers his own question. Free from the illusion, my friends. It is stated that you must know the truth. It is not stated that you must be told what is true and what is not true. It is stated that you must know. My friends, there is only one way to know, and that is through meditation.

I love the distinction he draws there. Being told what is true is not knowing. Knowing is firsthand. It is the difference between reading about honey and tasting it. No one can taste it for you. The meditation is the tasting.

And this is why the qualification cannot be given any other way. No teacher can certify your knowing. No course can complete it. You sit, daily, and the truth becomes self-evident, or it does not. And when it does, you no longer need anyone's appraisal, anyone's permission, anyone's stamp. You know. And the knowing makes you free.

He closes with a sentence that feels like a hand on the shoulder. It is sometimes difficult for a new instrument to speak using the thoughts which we project, he says, but this problem, like all others, is eradicated through meditation. For this eliminates questions of falsity or truth. It simply avails, to the individual, of the truth that is within all beings throughout creation.

The truth that is within all beings. Not within the special ones. Within all. The qualification is open to everyone, because the quiet is open to everyone.

So tonight, one requirement, and only one. Spend time each day in meditation. There is no other way to qualify. And nothing else is required.

Thank you for listening.

title: The View from the Sun
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the view from the sun.

April twenty-fourth, nineteen seventy-four. Hatonn speaks briefly, then the group asks its questions in silence, and the instrument is unsure whether the answers are her own thoughts or Hatonn's. Out of that honest confusion comes one of the richest sessions in this stretch: a teaching on light, on healing, and on children. It begins with night.

The subject you seek information on, he says, does not readily yield fruitful knowledge. But a concept which may be helpful is as follows. You know night. This darkness is real to you within the illusion you call life. But imagine you are observing the solar system from the standpoint of the object you call your sun.

From the standpoint of your sun, there is no night. There is no darkness. There is no lack. There is no limitation. There is only light. An enormously wasteful amount of energy, infinite, self-perpetuating, expressing itself in all directions with all of its heart and strength. The concept of darkness, lack, or limitation is quite foreign to the point of view of the inhabitant of the sun.

Night is not a thing. Night is where you are standing. Move your standpoint to the sun, and night disappears. It was never a substance. It was a shadow cast by your position.

It is for this reason, he says, that we often describe to you the love and the light as being like sunlight. This light is a spiritual phenomenon. It is one of the two building blocks of your entire universe. Light, unlimited and infinite in its capacity, is the basis for all that is in a physical sense. The shaping, creating, molding force is the consciousness, the Thought, which we call love. Love shapes light into the vibration we know as the physical world.

Two building blocks. Light, which is everything. And love, which shapes it. The universe is light, sculpted by love, into tables and trees and you.

The Creator's love is completely, down to the smallest detail, a spiritual thing. The lack, the limitation, the darkness, and the want is the creation of that most chief of the Father's creations: mankind. Mankind is a creator, even as his Father wished him to be. He has created. And through his desires come things which he does not truly desire. He has invented a great many ways to experience lack, limitation, and want.

We made the night. Not knowing what we were doing, but we made it: the experience of lack, shaped out of unlimited light by our own thought. This, he says, is only true from the point of view of the dweller within the illusion, who rotates with the planet and sees the sun go down. A simple shift in point of view, from the planet to the source of light, will bring the conditions of the planet into much clearer focus.

The ability to change one's point of view, he says, will often banish a question and replace it with understanding. You do not always need an answer. Sometimes you need a different place to stand.

Then a questioner asks about children. Are they born with the knowledge of love and understanding, or must they be taught? And Hatonn's answer is careful and tender. Children arrive, he says, with a heritage of previous experiences, and those incarnating now are somewhat advanced, called to Earth for the ending of this cycle. But the physical illusion is designed for further teaching, and the teaching is of two kinds.

The first kind is the school of hard knocks, as you call it. Life itself, bruising its lessons in. The second kind is us. And here is his counsel. The most informative stance, he says, is that taken by the master known as Jesus. When asked for understanding, Jesus spoke to the best of his ability. But more importantly, he exemplified by his life that which he wished to make known. Children learn not from what you intellectually manifest, but from what you manifest by your existence. This is your greatest area of teaching of any child: the area of example.

They watch what you are, not what you say. So he gives three simple ways to aid. One: remember that children are already somewhat mature, and need only direction. Two: let your best direction be the twenty-four-hour-a-day abiding of yourself with the light of your own spiritual awareness. Your life itself. By example, more have been aided than by any other means. Three: when asked, speak the truth as you know it. Forgive and encourage amidst difficulties and setbacks. And above all, accept and love on any terms.

Teach, but always above all, accept and love on any terms. He is sorry he cannot give any more certain method. We have been attempting to aid each entity upon your planet for many, many years, he says. Some may be aided, some may not. They may be aided only when they desire it. It is within each entity to choose what he will learn.

So tonight, two images. The sun, from whose standpoint there is no night. And the child, watching your life more closely than your words. Stand where the light is. And live, where they can see you, as if the night were only local.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seek Ye First
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seek ye first.

April twenty-sixth, nineteen seventy-four. A Friday. Hatonn opens with a problem, stated with unusual frankness. Our problem, my friends, is not in gaining the ability to catch the attention of the people of your planet. They can do that. The strange lights, the anomalies, the phenomena: all of it works as intended, creating the alerting mechanism in the entity's mind which it was intended to create. Our difficulty, he says, is to aid them in a way that is truly consistent with all of their desires. And then: there is a continuing difficulty, not in alerting the consciousness of men of Earth alone, but in keeping those who are alerted within the active attempt that they are making.

We have seen many, many people, he says, who have gone through some sort of confrontation and gained a sense of seeking, only to place it far back in the closet of their mind, to be taken out at some future time.

The closet of the mind. I know that closet. The book bought and never opened. The practice begun on Monday and shelved by Thursday. The vivid experience that was going to change everything, filed away under someday. Hatonn has watched this happen, many, many times. The awakening is not the problem. The staying awake is.

You cannot lose awareness, my friends. Yet there is little time. And it is our desire that we may help each of you who truly desire it to seek not only when there is that very day a reason for seeking, but to seek each day in a self-perpetuating way, so that your thinking is completely independent of such things as physical appearances of a controversial nature which turn you toward seeking.

Seeking that does not need a reason. Seeking as a condition, not a reaction. That is what he is asking for. Not the seeker who runs to the window every time something strange flies past, but the one whose seeking runs on its own fuel, every day, whether anything happens or not.

Seek ye first, my friends, is written in your holy works. Seek ye first the Kingdom of Heaven. If we can lead you to this level of seeking, then we will have produced in you the capacity which you have always enjoyed for continual, lifelong, and productive seeking. Furthermore, once this seeking has taken its place within your life as knowledge which needs no impulse to give it the central place in your consciousness, then you are within the boundaries of a true discipleship, in which you join the service of the infinite Creator.

Seek ye first. Not seek ye when convenient, or when frightened, or when the sky does something interesting. First. Before the rest. The seeking is not one item on the list. It is the page the list is written on.

Then Hatonn tells them something he says they do not usually tell. Your scientists will shortly experience a great deal of consternation, he says, for in their physical skies they will discover a new phenomenon entered. It will be looked upon as miraculous, because it will be exclusively different from what is comprehended as normal. We of the Confederation, he says, do not consider anything more miraculous in this creation than anything else. The creation is a miracle in each of its infinite parts.

He describes it further through the other instruments. A phenomenon of a radiation nature. A visible radiation that will change the color and the intensity of your night sky. A new body entering your system, visible for quite some time, radiance different from any object presently in your skies. You, along with your entire system of planets, he says, are evolving into a new sector and vibration within this creation. There shall occur many changes in the physical appearance of your system. The phenomenon shortly to occur shall be the first major change.

We generally have not given such specific information, he admits. But this occurrence is only one of many which we shall attempt to inform those who seek about. You can use this information in establishing the requested validity of our knowledge to those whom you serve. When it occurs, you shall surely have no more doubts.

And here is the part I want you to hold onto. This new experience will create seeking among many, he says. Some will seek in a scientific manner. Others in a spiritual manner. The physical trauma often produces seeking, but it is not a lasting stimulus. The only true stimulus comes from within, and can be discovered easily and always through meditation.

The sky may change. Probably will, in ways large and small, across a lifetime. But the sky is not the stimulus. The stimulus is the quiet you carry, the seeking that needs no impulse, the kingdom put first. Everything else, the phenomena, the predictions, the changed night sky, is weather around that one decision.

So tonight, check the closet. Is there something in there you meant to take out daily? Take it out. Seek ye first. Not when there is a reason. As the reason.

Thank you for listening.

title: Look at the Clouds
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: look at the clouds.

April twenty-seventh, nineteen seventy-four. A Saturday. Hatonn begins where the world is: in confusion. At the present time, he says, there exists a condition of confusion among your people. And he does not pretend it will lift. This state of confusion is but a small confusion, he says, compared to that which will exist in a very short time.

But listen to what he does with that. This creates, he says, a great opportunity for those who desire to serve their brothers. An opportunity to help those who desire assistance, and an opportunity to obtain a higher personal vibration. The confusion is not only a problem. It is an opening. Where people are lost, they can be found. Where they are certain, they cannot.

Those of you who are accepting the Creator's answer have found much peace in your own mind, he says. As time progresses, you will find this peace will intensify. This is a very comforting thing in the days that are shortly upon you. I wish to stress that daily meditation be adhered to. Through meditation you will find the answers to many questions that may be brought to you if you wish to serve. Much confusion will be brought to your door, but within meditation you will find the path to peace.

Much confusion will be brought to your door. Not might be. Will be. People will arrive with their questions and their panic, and you will need something to give them. The giving requires the getting, and the getting happens in the quiet. Daily. Adhered to. He keeps repeating it across these sessions the way a doctor repeats a prescription: not because you did not hear it, but because you will not do it.

Through another instrument he says it even more plainly. There is only one way in true seeking, and that is through meditation. Many of your people are in a negative state of mind, mainly because they are unaware of their own negatives. Through meditation they will see their negatives and eliminate them. Meditation, my friends, is the one true way.

Unaware of their own negatives. That is a gentle diagnosis. Not wicked. Not broken. Just unaware. The meditation does not punish the negativity. It reveals it, and the revealing dissolves it, the way light dissolves a shadow without touching it.

The information is simple, he admits, and in many cases may be profitably recycled, so that it may serve its purpose as well when heard a second time, or a third, as the first. It is an everyday job to live a spiritual life, and to keep the truths immediately before you. I love that phrase: an everyday job. Not a peak experience. Not a revelation. A job. Show up daily. Keep the truths where you can see them.

And then he gives the practice for the hours between meditations, and it is one of my favorite passages in this whole wave. This is what meditation is designed to do: to put you, part of the creation of the Father, into direct communication with the Father, which is all that there is. The creation of the Father is all about you, my friends. Remember it as you go about your daily routine. If you can see something which was not made by those upon the surface of your planet, such as the clouds, the water, the vegetation, or the animals, observe what you see, be it large or small. Truly observe the creation of the Father. There is much to observe. You yourself are a creation of the Father. Truly observe yourself.

Look at the clouds. That is the instruction. Not as a metaphor. As a practice. Find something not made by human hands, and truly observe it. The cloud, the water, the animal, yourself. In this way, as well as meditation, you may become more aware of the truth of what is. The creation of the Father is all about you. Meditation is within, and needs only to be beckoned forth.

The session also carries a long thread about the new channels learning to trust the contact: to speak the word that is given without looking ahead or behind it, without analyzing, without doubting. Concentrate only on saying the word that you are speaking. Do not try to anticipate what is to come next. Simply say the word that is given to you. It is the same teaching as the meditation, really. Be where you are. Say the word you have. Look at the cloud in front of you.

So tonight, two practices, one for the morning and one for the day. In the morning: the quiet, adhered to daily. In the day: the observation. Find one thing not made by hands. A cloud will do. Truly observe it. Truly observe yourself observing it. The confusion will come to your door soon enough. You will want the path to peace already worn smooth.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Hallmark of Joy
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the hallmark of joy.

April twenty-eighth, nineteen seventy-four. A Sunday. Hatonn opens, and for the first time in this stretch, the tone is celebration. My friends, he says, we wish to rejoice with you. We were aware that there was within your group, and there is now within your group, a great and growing core of joy that is beginning to gain strength as you proceed upon your path of seeking understanding.

Your contact with the Father within has begun to yield to you this heart of joy, this ecstasy. And we rejoice to see it in you, and in your group as a whole. This is the hallmark of those who will be able to say that they are joyful. Not as the world is joyful are they joyful, but joyful in a most transcendent way.

Not as the world is joyful. The world's joy depends on circumstances going right. This joy does not. It is the hallmark, he says, the identifying mark, of contact with the Infinite Father. You can tell the real thing by this: it does not need a reason.

Daily meditation carefully practiced yields this joy, he says, and service as it develops magnifies it many times. We rejoice exceedingly with you, my brothers, for you have entered the discipleship of the Creator.

Meditation yields it. Service magnifies it. That is the whole economy in two clauses. The quiet fills the cup. The giving multiplies what is in it.

This joy is your gift and your service, he says, just as our joy is our gift and our service. This joy is expressed in many ways: in overflowing love, in understanding, in truth, in healing, in diverse matters, as it is said in your holy work, is this joy come forth into manifestation within your daily life. But it is the hallmark of your contact with the Infinite Father.

I love that he claims joy as their service too. The Confederation is not a solemn bureaucracy. Their gift to the universe is their gladness. And yours is the same.

Through another instrument he describes how it works. Clearly comes through meditation the ability to contact this infinite joy, and the ability to avail and share it with all whom you may come into contact with. As a disciple of the Creator, you have chosen to do just this: to share your light and radiate His love to all. The service to any is service to yourself, for through this service you can gain an even higher awareness of this joy.

And then the practical warning, stated with urgency. In the days which shall shortly come, he says, it will be vitally important that you develop the ability to radiate this love to the peoples you serve in a manner in which they can relate to it as pure. Without this ability, there can be no service. You cannot serve any without this ability, though you may attempt to do so, for those who seek shall not accept that which is not distinguished as an infinite amount of love.

Those who seek shall not accept that which is not distinguished as an infinite amount of love. Read that as a standard. The people coming to you in their confusion will not be convinced by your arguments or impressed by your knowledge. They will accept only one thing: love, in an amount that feels infinite. Anything less, and they will turn away. So the work is not to sharpen your answers. It is to deepen your radiance.

Through His wisdom, the Creator saw that in order for His disciples to be of service, He would give them this great love and the ability to use it. If this needs to be done, then we suggest that all you need do is meditate. Attempt to raise your vibration rapidly, for the time grows short. The greater you develop yourself, the more benefit you shall receive. It is your choice, through His gift to you of free will. Once aware, work can begin. Only you can do it for yourself.

Only you can do it for yourself. After all the sessions, all the conditioning, all the craft overhead and the voices through instruments, it comes down to that. No one can meditate for you. No one can rejoice for you.

The rest of the session is the patient work of building new channels, the repeated gentle instruction to relax, to stop analyzing, to speak one word at a time. It is unglamorous and it is the whole mission: more people able to sit in the quiet, receive the joy, and carry it to the ones who are waiting.

So tonight, the teaching is not a task but a recognition. If you have sat in the quiet, and felt something rise that needed no reason, that is the hallmark. That is the contact. Rejoice in it. And then, as the service develops, watch it magnify, many times over, in the giving.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Action of Desire
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the action of desire.

Hatonn has one thing to say this evening, and he says it three ways until it starts ringing like a bell. You are experiencing exactly what you desire. Even the parts you swear you never wanted.

Listen to how they put it. The Creator, he says, intended that all of his children be able to have exactly what they desire at all times. That is the design. And man on Earth, he says, is at this time experiencing exactly what he desires to experience. This is always the case.

If that lands hard, it is meant to. For then comes the question nobody can dodge. If he truly did not desire these experiences, Hatonn says, they would not come to him. So why do people keep meeting things they insist they never asked for? Because man on Earth is very confused about his desires. The thinking mind does not know its own true wishes.

The intellect, he says, is a very poor tool when not augmented in its abilities through meditation. An intellectual appraisal of your desires is far shortsighted with respect to your actual desires. I love that phrasing. Far shortsighted. As if the mind is squinting at its own wishes and getting them wrong.

So how do you find the true ones? The ones running underneath, ordering your life without your permission? You cannot think your way to them. You can only sit your way to them. Within you, he says, is the truth of this statement and all others. It is necessary, if you are to experience your ultimate desires, to reach your ultimate thinking through meditation. We realize, he says, that this cannot be done instantaneously. But we are attempting to point out to you the pathway to controlling your thinking, so that your experiences will conform with the desires you will discover that you desire at a later time.

Then he turns the lens on his own side, and this is where it gets beautiful. The Confederation, he says, desires one thing. Just one. To be of service in the love and in the light of the infinite Creator. This is the original thought. The thought of our infinite Creator: to serve all of his parts, so as to bring them, in each and every instance, that which they desire.

And the experiences that accompany such desire, he says, are free from any problem or difficulty that could be imagined. I sat with that line for a while. Free from any problem that could be imagined. Not because the world gets fixed, but because desire itself finally lines up with what is.

There is a middle passage in this session about a sign that will come within the week. New instruments fumbling, long pauses, messages half lost. Hatonn himself admits he has entered the area of the intellectual and the explanatory, and he apologizes for it. Truth does not reside there, he says. I will leave the sign where the transcript leaves it, as a small piece of history. The heart of the evening is elsewhere.

The heart is this. A return to simplicity. Many people on your planet, he says, are in a state of absolute confusion, and the answers they actually seek are answers of infinite simplicity. They have fabricated a system of thinking so complex that the return to simplicity is very difficult. But this is all that is really necessary, he says. A return to the simplest form of understanding. A return to the simplicity of the love that generates all of us. This may be done by anyone at any time. The door is meditation.

And then the ending, one of the loveliest closings in these early sessions. What is about to come to you, he says, is no more than you have already experienced. It is simply different. There are an infinite number of experiences, and you have met only a small number.

Many of the people of your planet have labeled certain events as miraculous. And he asks: does it take another one to awaken those who seek? Do not they see that which surrounds them? My friends, he says, you are surrounded by the miraculous. There is nothing but a miracle. A miracle created by our Creator.

The illusion, he says, is within your thinking. Destroy that. And become aware of the love that has brought about the miracle you have always experienced.

That is the whole evening, really. What you desire is what you are getting, so find out what you truly desire. And there is only one way that works. Sit down. Get quiet. Let the love that made the miracle say what it has been trying to say all along.

Thank you for listening.

title: Service Must Be Taken
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: service must be taken.

The group has asked about service. And Hatonn begins with a sentence that stops the whole room. The most difficult thing to accept about service, he says, is the fact that you cannot give service. There is no way to give service. Service, my friends, must be taken.

This is a spiritual law, not a riddle. Each entity, he says, has a complete universe to himself, through which nothing can come without his expressed approval. Many things seem to come into people's lives that they do not desire. But in truth, that which comes into each entity's environment is what he has desired. Nothing else may enter. So there is no way to give service to an entity. There is only the ability of each entity to request and accept service from another.

Which means the seeker who wants to serve will discover, more and more, the difficulties of service. You cannot push it on anyone. You cannot argue anyone into receiving it. All you can do is be ready.

And then he gives the image that carries the whole evening. Consider the tree which produces fruit. The tree spends much time, much love and much care, all of its energy, producing the edible fruit, which it then offers to any who would desire to take the fruit. That is its service. And it may be that one tree goes through an entire cycle without benefiting any entity. The fruit withers. It drops to the ground.

But the tree does not become discouraged. For it knows that after rest it will be ready again to be of service. And it knows that even though the fruit withers, the seeds within it may produce, for many years to come, other fruit trees and other fruit, and an endless amount of service.

I love that line, and I keep coming back to it. The tree is never wasted. Nothing offered in love is wasted. It only changes form.

What he is really telling you is that you cannot know, inside the illusion, what your short-term objectives of service may be. Do not try to measure the yield. It is sufficient, he says, that you be ready to serve by abiding within the light of a spiritual consciousness, and that you respond to any request for service, from whomever it comes.

The abiding within spirit that you do by constant meditation, he says, is of the greatest service. Think back over the past five years of your life, he suggests. Do the events not come into clearer focus now that time has detached you from the illusions of the moment? That is how service works too. What is meant will occur. Fill your consciousness with the environment you truly desire. Do not fear that you will not be of service. Only be ready to be of service, for you will surely be asked if you are ready to serve.

The greatest desire which one may have, he says, is to be of service. And the proper way to desire it is to desire to serve at any opportunity, at any entity which requests it. There is no special service, for all service is special.

And then a warning for the impatient, which is to say, for all of us. In your daily life you will wonder about the path of service you desire to find. Do not wonder in this way. If you truly desire to serve, your path shall be given unto you. Walk the path, and do not walk the last part of the path without fully walking the first. You cannot bring about that which is to come without experiencing that which comes before. Patience is required.

Your greatest service, he says, is your love for all of the creation. Love any part and you love all. But love all and you shall love any part. Do not separate the two.

And the closing note, simple as a seed. If you truly desire to serve, do not be concerned as to how you may serve. Concern yourself only with developing your awareness through meditation, and your opportunities shall be presented to you. You need not search in order to serve. Your service shall be sought.

Be the tree. Bear the fruit. Let it be taken, or let it fall. Either way, the seed is already doing its work.

Thank you for listening.

title: Waking from the Dream
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: waking from the dream.

This evening Hatonn wants to talk about the physical illusion. And he begins with the simplest possible image for it. The illusion is very difficult to comprehend from within the illusion, he says, for like a dream it often defies identification from within itself. However, when one wakes up from a dream, one is aware that one has dreamed.

And when this segment of your infinite and eternal journey is complete, you will be aware of that which is known as life. You will be aware that this life is an illusion. The illusion of the physical.

It is a staggering claim, stated the way you might state the weather. Not argued. Just offered. When you wake from this, you will know you were dreaming.

Inside the dream, one thing is taken very seriously. Personality. The concept of personality, he says, is highly respected within the illusion. But consider what function personality truly has, seen in a spiritual light. As one sees the world from the standpoint of the Creator, and sees what is real and what is not real, one sees that the personality is completely involved with the illusion, and that no part of personality as such is involved in the spiritual consciousness.

He gives you a tree again. A tree may not have personality, he says, for it is a part of the real creation. What it has is an awareness of the Creator's law and the Creator's love.
