This is not possible, he says. All thought that is generated is generated by the Creator. He is all things and is in all places. All of the consciousness and all of the thought that exists is the thought of our Creator.

And yet, within this unity, something has gone strange. We find man upon planet Earth to be an aberration, he says. An aberration in thinking, in experiment, and in present experience. From their point of view, Earth's people have wandered far from the concept that permeates most of the creation they know. They have chosen to isolate themselves.

I love how carefully he holds this. If the Creator, as represented by His parts upon Earth, wishes to experience and experiment in the manner of man on Earth, then this is exactly what we wish for Him to do. For He is us and we are Him. There is no condemnation in it. It is a privilege, he says, a privilege of this being that is all of us. And yet, he continues, in this isolation some of His parts have grown tired. They are seeking an experience more closely allied with what is normal. So we are here to advertise.

Advertise. That is his word. We are here to advertise the possibility of a simple return to the original Thought. A Thought, he says, of total love. Listen to how he treats the word itself. We have called it love, he says, but this is inadequate, for it is a word in your language expressing emotions you experience in your illusion. And yet we must use it. We must use it until you avail yourself to its total meaning.

He sketches what the return looks like. Those parts now locked within the illusion will begin to free themselves, he says. They will begin to change their desires, and begin once more to become aware of love. Not the interpretation of man on Earth, but love in its true meaning, in its infinite and all-embracing sense. And then, he says, you and we will be much, much more closely allied. For you will know our thoughts as well.

The contact passes to Carla, and the teaching turns practical. The next time you are backed into a corner by the circumstances of the physical illusion, remember what you have learned. As long as your objectives lie within this physical illusion, you are subject to its laws. If your desires can be lifted into the creation of the infinite One, you may have a great deal more ability to remove yourself from the corners the illusion backs you into.

He closes with the one thing he calls of great importance. Your personal preparation for service. You are to serve your fellow man, he says, and therefore it is necessary that you prepare yourselves. This is done in meditation. All of your questions, he says, can be reduced to an extremely simple concept, and this you can become aware of in meditation. Once this is done, you will be ready to serve.

The goal never moved, he says. It lies in the same place for all men, whether limited to the surface of a planet or journeying elsewhere in an infinite and totally benevolent creation of love. Direct them inward, and they will find it. It is the same inward everywhere.

A resting thought. The voices do not come to change your mind. They come to advertise a way back to the Thought you already carry. The door is not locked. It was never locked.

Thank you for listening.

title: Many Paths, One Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: many paths, one within.

It is the second of June, nineteen seventy-four, the first of two sessions that evening, and there are newcomers in the room. Hatonn is aware of them, and aware that they are hearing this for the first time. He adjusts his approach, and the result is one of the most honest statements of the voices' limits in the whole archive.

He begins where he always begins. Whatever differences in thinking you may experience, he says, there is one thing you all have in common. You are all seeking the truth. You are all seeking understanding. The seeking has brought you here, and your desire for knowledge has brought us to you.

But listen to how carefully he describes what he can actually give. We can only act as guideposts, he says, to point you in the direction of that which you so desire. We cannot give you any final words, for our message cannot be expressed directly. I love that line. It is the opposite of authority. The voices know exactly how much they do not know.

He says it again later, even more plainly. We are not to be considered as an ultimate source of information, he says. We are fortunate enough to have experienced what you are experiencing now, and to have chosen to seek the truth through meditation. That seeking brought us to a higher understanding. This understanding we wish to share with you. Nothing more. Nothing less.

He is precise about how the teaching should be received. We have realized, he says, that the intellect you possess can accept only small segments of our information at any given time, and this information must be analyzed before you can receive a higher form. But when we say you must analyze, he cautions, we do not mean that you can analyze all that is happening around you by the use of your intellect. Take it in small sips. Let it settle. Then come back.

What he does offer, to newcomers and old hands alike, is the same single recommendation. The most efficient way to begin obtaining the truth you seek, he says, is to go within and seek contact with reality through meditation. To seek contact with that which is infinite, that which is love and light. There are as many paths to your common goal as there are individuals, he says. The direction the truth lies in is within your own being.

Another instrument takes up the teaching for the newcomers. He warns them not to expect great realizations in short periods of time, for meditation is a process of learning, and all that you learn must come from the beginning and slowly develop. And yet, he says, if you wish to consider a climax, we are not aware of that climax. The path does not end in a trophy. It ends, if it ends anywhere, in a deepening.

He borrows the words of Jesus for this. The kingdom of heaven lies within. And by this he means within your being. Turn within yourself through the use of meditation, and you will slowly find the truth of what we wish to present. We wish only to serve your peoples, he says, and to help them realize the love which is all that is contained within this creation.

The final instrument of the evening adds one last emphasis. We have spoken many times, he says, of the great lessons to be obtained through your meditations. The first and the greatest of all is that of love, and what can be obtained through this love. Through love you receive all your faith, and through your faith, your desire to serve the Creator in whatever way you have chosen.

There is a line I keep returning to. To seek contact with reality through meditation, he says. To seek contact with that which is infinite, that which is love and light. He repeats the phrase like a handrail. Love and light. Not as a slogan. As an address. That is where the contact goes. That is where you are being pointed.

A resting thought. The voices do not offer you a map. They offer you a signpost, an arrow painted on wood, and they tell you plainly: you must walk the road yourself. The road leads inward.

Thank you for listening.

title: Do Not Fear Mistakes
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: do not fear mistakes.

It is later on the same evening, the second of June, nineteen seventy-four, and the session takes a different turn. This is not a teaching for the group at large. This is a working session. Hatonn announces that he will attempt to establish contact with the newer channels of the group, in hopes that they will generate proficiency. The voices are training their own instruments, out loud, in front of everyone.

He opens with the rule that governs the whole evening. We have oftentimes said, the channeling reports, that your progress increases with the volume of your desire. Through your desire you obtain the knowledge to guide you through the trials which all instruments who choose to serve the Creator must serve. For the road is always difficult, but through meditation you are given the strength to bear these trials, and with each trial you gain further faith and further knowledge.

And then the line I want to underline. Do not have fear of mistakes, he says, for it is a common occurrence in the lives of all the beings of your planet. He asks the new instruments not to be afraid to speak the thought they receive, even when the thought feels like it might be their own fault. The hesitation, the self-editing, is the only real obstacle. Say it.

He admits the scale of the problem. It is somewhat a difficult task, he says, to devote individual attention to all of those who desire it at this point. So the voices work the way they can: through the room, through the contact, through whoever will hold still enough to carry it. The training of new instruments is not a luxury. It is how the service survives its own success.

And when the contact fails, as it does more than once that evening, there is no frustration. An instrument cannot relax. Another cannot trust the thoughts enough to speak them. Hatonn simply moves on to the next willing mind, or closes for the night. The work will still be there tomorrow. The willingness is the whole qualification.

The session is fragmented, as training sessions are. The contact drops, resumes, shifts instruments. Hatonn is patient with all of it. He speaks briefly on the subject of inspiration, which he calls what takes almost all things you obtain and brings them true. And he is specific about the kind of meditation the new instruments need. Group meditation, he says, is good for the development of the intellect. But silent meditation is where you gain the knowledge needed for your daily life in the service of the Creator. Both, then. The group and the silence.

Near the end he speaks on the subject of influences. You as a person living on your planet are subject to many influences, he says. We hope to bring about small things that will influence your mind as to the power of the infinite Creator. But we do not wish to get, as you say, carried away. We only wish to make it possible for you to have certain information at your disposal. Nothing forced. Nothing grand. A door left open.

There is a moment I find very human. He becomes aware of the uncertainty of the one known as G. He says he will attempt to establish contact with her if she desires, and asks her to relax completely. The contact does not come. There is difficulty, fatigue, an instrument unsure of herself. And Hatonn does not scold or strain. He closes. It has been a very great honor, he says, to talk to some of the new channels.

One line stands out from the fragments of the evening. We have developed new devices, he says, in which, once we are aware of your desire, we may share with you our love at any time you so desire. The contact does not require a room full of people or a scheduled evening. Desire is the switch. Turn it, and the connection is there.

A resting thought. The voices are not looking for perfection in their instruments. They are looking for willingness. The willingness to speak the thought, to risk the mistake, to try again tomorrow. Everything else is practice.

Thank you for listening.

title: The One Worthy Goal
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the one worthy goal.

It is the fifth of June, nineteen seventy-four, the first of two sessions that evening, and Hatonn arrives with a long discourse that builds, piece by piece, toward a single sentence. The early instruments speak of the group's progress and the joy of the work. But when the contact reaches the instrument known as Don, the tone deepens, and Hatonn lays out his fullest statement yet of what man on Earth has forgotten.

Man upon Earth has many needs, he says. But his real and only need is understanding. For when man, at any place in this infinite creation, understands, then he has no more needs. Our Creator, the Father of us all, intended that all of His children should demonstrate the love that He expressed in creating. In demonstrating this love, they would in return receive exactly and completely what they deserved.

Man upon Earth has lost an awareness of this simple concept, he says, and has become confused. And the confusion is almost comic in its shape. He is living on a planet that supports his every need. An atmosphere surrounds him, and each breath supports his life. Food grows abundantly on the surface of the planet. He is supported at every turn, and yet man has forgotten these simple services. He has arrived, through his unbalanced desire, at a position of total ignorance of how he is in actuality a simple child of an infinite creation.

Listen to the remedy, because it is not what you would expect. It is not necessary for man to seek for himself sustenance, he says. It is only necessary that he seek understanding, and seek to serve, and then the gifts of the Creator are reflected upon him. This was within the original Thought that created all that exists. The striving gets it backward. The seeking gets it right.

There are many things that man on Earth can seek, he says. There are many pathways down which he can seek. There are many goals for him to generate within his thinking. And yet, after he seeks down all these pathways, after he succeeds in reaching all of these goals, he simply finds that there was only one worth seeking and worth reaching. This goal, my friends, is the understanding of that love that created him.

And here is the part that stops me. An understanding that he has always had, Hatonn says, which is within him because it is within all men throughout all of the creation. The goal is not out there. It is not new. It is the oldest thing you own, misplaced in the bottom of a drawer. We of the Confederation, he says, are simply here to direct man on Earth inward, to show him where his goal lies. It lies, my friends, in the same place for all men.

An earlier instrument that evening offered the image I like best from the whole night. What we offer you with words, he said, is merely an arrow painted on a sign. It is you who must walk the road. It is you who must seek. We are not going to stop talking to you, he said, but the importance of your portion of the contact becomes more and more paramount as you draw closer to union with us. Seek from these fields that which you desire. Seek your wellsprings of faith and hope and love.

He also warned against confusing the Confederation's service with your own. Our service, he said, is small compared to the service you may render unto yourself, and this service is the daily practice of meditation. Through meditation you may attain the knowledge which shall be greatly needed in the coming times. The voices can point. Only you can walk.

He does not leave them with nothing to do. Return to this awareness through meditation, he says, and man will once more retake his rightful position, a position of love as provided for by his Creator. All the seeking, all the reaching, all the building of goals, and the end of it is a return. Not a conquest. A remembering.

A resting thought. You have one real need, and it is not the one on your list. The goal you are chasing at the end of all the other goals is the one you already carry. Begin there, and the rest rearranges itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Experiments Continue
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the experiments continue.

It is the second session of June fifth, nineteen seventy-four, a shorter evening, and the group has brought a question about a particular man. Someone they know, or know of, who seems to do extraordinary things. Is he what he claims to be? Hatonn's answer is careful, and it opens a window onto something the voices rarely discuss: the experiments.

The man of which you spoke is a somewhat rare type of entity, he says. He is among those who have chosen to incarnate upon the surface in order to be of some aid to those upon the surface of this planet. Much of what he is able to do is dependent upon those areas of awareness which he has brought into this incarnation. It would not be possible for him to be used as a channel, he says, were he not what you might call a somewhat advanced being. He is telling the truth about each of his experiences.

And then the wider picture. This is a sort of experiment, my friends. There are many such experiments. There are many, many contacts. These contacts differ. Some contacts, such as the one of which we are speaking, are very ambitious, and some seem to be not so ambitious. However, he says, it is a great aid to us to be able to make contact with many instruments, for each channel has an untold effect upon his environment.

I love that image. Not a broadcast tower, but a seed. Each channel, each instrument, has an untold effect upon his environment, rippling outward in ways no one can measure. The experiment is not about the miracle. It is about the proximity.

He is honest about the limits of what he can explain. It is difficult, at times, he says, to express what is about to happen in a way that it may be understood. This would be necessary if an understanding of this man were to be appreciated. So he gives the frame instead of the detail. There is a program now in progress, he says, to awaken the peoples of your planet to their rightful heritage. There are many facets to this program. There are many of us from elsewhere in the creation who are involved in doing this.

It is very difficult to progress in an exact and direct way, he says. Certain things must be brought to your people in a very small amount of your time. This is the only possibility for them at this time. The teaching arrives in sips, not floods, because that is what the receiving end can hold.

The instrument tires. The contact strains. Hatonn does not force it. He promises that in the future they will attempt to give a greater understanding in this area of seeking, and he leaves. The evening is short, the message incomplete, and somehow that is part of the message. Not everything can be said at once. Not everything should be.

A resting thought. The unusual is not always a mystery to be solved. Sometimes it is a seed planted in plain sight, doing its work quietly, in the smallest possible dose, exactly as intended.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Coming Harvest
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the coming harvest.

It is the evening of June sixth, nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn arrives carrying something the voices rarely show. Sadness. He says it plainly. No one can know better than some of you here tonight, he says, that our mission on planet Earth has not been as successful as we had hoped. The harvest is coming, my friends. It is coming very quickly. And the harvest will be somewhat smaller than we had ever hoped.

He knows the group understands, because they have felt the same thing. You too, he says, from attempting to express the thoughts of the Creator, have often found this to be so. And I am aware of the great sadness that you too feel. The information was offered, and in many, many cases it was not recognized or desired. He does not dress this up. He sits with it.

But he does not sit with it long. Although this sadness bides within us all, he says, let us not spend more time than is necessary to accept this experience, for there is a great deal to do for the ones who have not rejected the higher experience. There will be many who still seek, and some who flounder, and there is much that ones who are aware of truth can do to encourage those who are seeking toward a path that will lead them into the real creation.

Then he gives them the sentence that reframes the whole grief. True progress, my friends, is without the dimension of time and without the dimension of space. That which you do for one, you do for all. I love that line. The harvest may be smaller than hoped, but no act of service is small, because no act of service is separate. Do not be discouraged, he says. Continue in your seeking, and through daily meditation keep yourself grounded well in the creation of the Father, for we have much to do yet.

He closes the session with a single thought, and it is the simplest question in the archive. The simple and eternal question is always, he says, what is love? Love is all, my friends. He is love. Be one with love, and allow the divine love of the Creator to flow through you. In this way, he says, you know the ecstasy that comes with being one with all that there is.

I want to hold these two things together the way the evening held them. The sadness is real. The mission has not gone as hoped. And in the same breath, love is all, and nothing done in love is wasted, because it is not done in time or space. The grief and the ecstasy are not opposites here. They are the same evening.

A resting thought. You may work for something larger than you and watch it come up smaller than you dreamed. Work anyway. What you do for one, you do for all, and that arithmetic does not fail.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Bluebird of Happiness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the bluebird of happiness.

It is the second session of June sixth, nineteen seventy-four, and a new voice arrives. She calls herself Nona. She is new to this instrument, she says, and she will speak only a few words. There will be many teachers that will come to you, she says. Many different kinds of channels. And you will know the difference of the vibration.

Her message is brief and almost entirely lost to the tape, but one sentence survives intact, and it is worth the whole evening. All there is, you are, she says. My love. Four words, given as a parting thought. All there is, you are.

Then she introduces another. Deltron would like to speak for just a brief moment, she says. And Deltron arrives with an introduction unlike any the group has heard. I am from another galaxy, he says, entirely different from this planet's. I and many of my brothers have answered the call to come and assist the people of Earth. Until now they have only been observing, learning the techniques of contacting Earth people.

What have they observed? Your people, he says, still devoting a great deal of their time to elaborate ritual, to the building of fabulous houses. Your people searching in all directions for that which they call the light of their Creator. He is not mocking. He is describing the search as it looks from very far away.

And then he tells them a story from their own planet. There is a story upon your planet, he says. I believe it is referred to as the search for the bluebird of happiness. In this search, an individual was seeking happiness, and much to his own surprise he did not find happiness until he looked in his own backyard.

My children, this is the truth of your searching, he says. Search no further than yourself, because your Creator has endowed you with all you will ever need. It is there for you to find. It is found in sincere searching through love for yourself and for your fellow man. I love how direct this is. Not in the ritual. Not in the fabulous house. In the backyard.

He gives them the practice. It is found through consideration, he says. Through compassion, and the reflection of love and understanding to those about you. You are well on your way, and there are many more to guide and direct you. It is up to you to open your heart and to reflect that radiant light, that loving presence that is within you today.

He closes as a visitor closes, with blessings. May each of you walk in the light of that radiant light, he says. Go in peace, and be of good cheer in the days to come.

A resting thought. The bluebird was never far. The searching was the thing that made it seem far. Look down, look in, look at the ground beneath your own feet. That is where it has been waiting.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mountain of Death
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mountain of death.

It is the seventh of June, nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn begins with a refusal. The group has asked about a dream, and about the meaning of its symbols. He declines to interpret it. To explain what the symbols of a dream mean before the waking personality is ready to understand, he says, may not be helpful. The dream recurs, he says, unchanging, as the understanding that is needed is acquired. The dream is doing its own work. Let it.

Instead, he says, this evening I would like to say a few words about the concept of death. Why do I bring this up, he asks. Because it seems the proper time to ask you to hold it, as clearly as you can, as a concept within your imagination. And then he gives an exercise.

Imagine your own death, he says. Imagine each death and dismal corridor of pain and difficulty and lack of faith. Imagine all the evil, the negativity, the limitations. Imagine it all, my friends. Allow it to build and build and build until you have a big and towering mountain of death and destruction.

Now stop. What are you looking at, he asks. What are you imagining? What are you afraid of? What do you know about death, my friends? You have been exposed to much information. It is now time to begin to absorb this information. What do you know about negativity? Do you run for death? There are many on your planet who do, he says. They hope for death because they believe things will be better after it. But what do you know?

Then the release. As you meditate, he says, what pours forth from within your soul? Are you not aware that which is light and which is darkness, that which is life and which is death, is merely part of the infinite cycle of an eternal and unchanging creation? A creation which has neither life nor death, neither dark nor light, but is all things, all cycles, resolved in unity and love.

I love that image of resolution. Not light defeating dark. Not life conquering death. All things, all cycles, resolved in unity and love. The mountain you built in your imagination was never a mountain. It was a wave, mid-crest, in an ocean that has no shore.

And here is the sentence the whole exercise was built for. Facing darkness, my friends, you have nothing to lose but the fear that is holding you within a prison of your own choosing within your mind. Nothing to lose but the fear. The prison has your own architecture. The door was never locked.

A resting thought. The next time the fear rises, let it build. Let it build and build until it is a towering mountain. Then ask, quietly, what you are actually looking at. And watch what happens to the mountain.

Thank you for listening.

title: Two Kinds of Happiness
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: two kinds of happiness.

It is the eighth of June, nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn opens with a picture of the ordinary miracle. Man upon Earth, he says, is unaware of the simple reality he is capable of sensing with his physical senses, and unaware of the much greater reality outside their boundaries. He neglects noticing that he breathes the atmosphere without which his physical body could not exist. He neglects perceiving that he partakes of the food amply supplied by the Creator.

He has come to look at these things as provided by his own technology, Hatonn says. He does not understand the true meaning of the simple and beautiful life that surrounds him. He does not appreciate its generation and regeneration. He learned that the very atmosphere he breathes is cycled through the plant life to be regenerated, and yet this seems to the vast majority an exercise in technology rather than one in theology.

Then the sentence that stings. He has become hypnotized by his playthings and his ideas. He is but a child in his mind. And the remedy, Hatonn says, is very simple. Man can return to an appreciation of reality through the process of meditation, for this stills his active conscious mind, which is continually seeking stimulus within the false illusion developed over so many centuries.

What is the reality he would return to? Listen to how Hatonn describes it. Your illusion is very complex, he says. Your cities, your political systems, your concept of science, your concept of philosophy, they are all complex. They require great intellectual ability to encompass them. And yet they are nothing compared to the one simple Thought of your Creator. The simple Thought of absolute love.

This is what man on Earth must return to if he is to know reality, he says. A Thought of total unity with all his brothers, regardless of how they might express themselves or whom they might be. For this is the original Thought of your Creator. Your creation supports you. It was designed in thought to support you and provide for all of your desires. It was the Thought of your Creator that each part of this creation should serve all other parts, for this is the Thought of absolute love, the Thought of total service.

Through a second instrument, the teaching turns to happiness. There are two kinds, Hatonn says. There is the happiness within the illusion, the happiness that shifts and changes with the physical manifestation. And there is the happiness known only as understanding, the experience of being one with an unchanging creation of love. One can only seek one's choice of these two.

So he urges them to be careful what they are truly seeking. Do you seek within this illusion which shifts and is so changeable? Or do you seek for reality? Meditation, he says, is one word with one concept we project over and over. We do it for a simple reason. It is the best fruit that we have to give you. For all that we can do is point you in the direction of your inner self, which is truly one with the Creator.

He explains the method of the contact itself. We find it necessary, he says, to give to those who seek that which they seek in such a way that they may appraise its value for themselves, and accept or reject on their own terms the thoughts that we bring. Nothing is forced on you. The teaching arrives wrapped in deniability, so your freedom stays intact.

And the closing charge of the evening is worth keeping whole. Seek this understanding through meditation, he says, for all rewards are within. Move backward to the simplicity that is the creation. Still the conscious mind, and become aware of love.

The evening ends with attempted contacts that never quite land, and it hardly matters. The teaching is already complete. Two kinds of happiness. One word, one concept, projected over and over. The best fruit they have to give.

A resting thought. There is a happiness you can hold, and a happiness that holds you. The first shifts with the weather. The second does not shift at all. Choose carefully what you are seeking, because the effects of the seeking are to present you with what you desire.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Transformation of Thought
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the transformation of thought.

It is the ninth of June, nineteen seventy-four, a Sunday, and this session is largely about the work of channeling itself. Hatonn and his brother Laitos move through instrument after instrument, conditioning each one. The teaching that emerges is not a doctrine for the seekers in the room. It is a manual for the servers. And it is strikingly honest about what service actually costs.

The channel who answers questions for seekers, Hatonn says, must walk a very careful line. You must not give false information. You must not be discouraging. You must be encouraging, and somehow understanding within the light of that which you know to be true. In many cases, he says, this will entail an answer that is not an answer, which may temporarily confuse the person you are attempting to help. I love that admission. Sometimes the truest service sounds like no answer at all.

He prepares them for what is coming. Your daily contacts will provide a very fertile field for the dissemination of information, he says. Many people will ask questions. And after you have answered, more than likely they will not believe you. This is to be expected, he says, and to be prepared for. It is not something to be discouraged about. They will in their own good time come to understand. Your attempts at service will bear much fruit, either immediately or in the future.

Then, through the instrument known as Don, he names what the channeling is actually for. Meditation will allow you to become totally aware of the concepts we bring, he says. When you become aware of these concepts in their total nature, there will be a transformation in your thinking. A transformation that you presently desire. If you did not desire this, you would not be seeking it. This transformation is necessary if you are to be totally effective in serving our Creator.

This transformation has been demonstrated before, he says. The last teacher with whom you are familiar who demonstrated this transformation of thought was known to you as Jesus. This man lived and acted quite simply. However, his thinking was unique. It was recognized by those around him as being unique, and recognized as being correct by many of those who were aware of it. And this transformation, he says, you may obtain through meditation.

Through the newer instruments that evening, the teaching is practical. Prepare yourself, he says, through daily meditations, and through group meetings such as this. Through your daily meditations you will be supplied with many answers to questions that will shortly be asked you. New channels should meditate as much as they can, he says, and stay in meditation as long as they can, in order to acquire understanding.

He does not promise ease. In the days that follow, he says, many hardships will come to the planet known as Earth. The preparation is not escape from difficulty. It is readiness inside it. The channel who is grounded in meditation can answer the questions that suffering will ask, because the answers will already be living in him.

There is one more moment in the evening I do not want to lose. A brief contact from the one called Oxal, who says only that he is using control, and that it is impossible at this time to answer the question asked. The voices turn away questions sometimes. And Hatonn, through Carla, explains why. Wisdom is a rather lonely matter, my friends, he says. You must accept this truth as you acquire the burden of wisdom. That which you know you are to be careful of, for what you know in the real creation has power.

And then the sentence that has become a refrain of this series. The farther that you go along this path, he says, the more meaningful you will find this simple statement. Meditate. It begins as a simple process, and little by little it becomes the way in which you live.

A resting thought. Transformation of thought is not a new set of opinions. It is the slow turning of the mind toward the light, until the light does the thinking. And no one can do it for you. That is why it is lonely, and why it is yours.

Thank you for listening.

title: Self-Generating Contact
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: self-generating contact.

It is the eleventh of June, nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn speaks on the mechanics of the work itself. There are more people upon this planet seeking than there have been in the past, he says. However, many are quite confused in their attempts to seek, and there is a need at this time for many more channels such as this one, who can receive directly the thoughts that so many are now seeking.

This requires daily meditation, he says. This is all that is required. It is assumed, of course, that as this daily meditation is performed, there is a desire for our contact. The desire is the tuning. The meditation is the instrument.

Then he describes the process the voices are stimulating, and listen to how he puts it. The process is one which is self-generating, he says. As more and more of those who desire our contact receive it and pass it on to others, then those who receive this passed-on information will themselves be able to reach a state of thinking sufficiently in tune with our vibrations to receive our contact. I love that image. Not a campaign. A chain reaction. One lit lamp lighting the next.

He explains the physics of it, as far as words allow. It is first necessary, he says, for the entity to become of a certain vibration as a result of his thinking. This is greatly speeded by involvement in groups such as this. And then it is finally done through meditation. The verbal communications create a system of thought and a desire for spiritual awareness that raises the vibration. Through meditation the entity attunes his thinking to those of us who serve planet Earth. He then can receive and repeat what we give to him, in order to regenerate, from its beginning, the process of teaching and instructing others.

Through this technique, he says, there will be many more of the peoples of Earth made aware of the truth and the love that is theirs, as it is the will of their Creator. The whole architecture of the contact is designed to reproduce itself. Every student becomes a teacher. Every receiver becomes a transmitter.

He addresses the obvious question. Why not simply land and teach openly? We are very sorry that we cannot step upon your soil, he says. But this would be a very great disservice to those who do not desire our service at this time. And we are afraid we would have little effect in bringing understanding even to those who desire it, for understanding, my friends, comes from within. We can only guide. We can only suggest.

And that, I think, is the heart of it. The contact must be self-generating because understanding cannot be imported. It can only be grown, one meditator at a time, each one raising the vibration enough to light the next lamp. This is a very great time, he says, a great transitional period in which many of Earth's people will be raised from their state of confusion to a simple understanding: the love of their Creator.

A resting thought. You do not need to be ready to teach. You only need to be willing to be tuned. The teaching will do the rest, and it will pass through you to the next lamp on its own.

Thank you for listening.

title: Each Obstacle, an Opportunity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: each obstacle, an opportunity.

It is the twelfth of June, nineteen seventy-four. The tape is rough, and much of the evening is lost to inaudible passages. But what survives is strong, and it gathers around a single idea. Within the illusion, Hatonn says, there are many obstacles. The illusion, in fact, is designed to produce the obstacles which will deliver unto you the choices which you desire, for learning how to be of greater service to others.

The lessons of this density, he says, are lessons of service to others. And each obstacle is an opportunity, which those within the illusion think is difficulty. Each obstacle is your opportunity to grow. I love that reversal. The thing in your way is not in your way. It is the way, wearing a disguise.

There is much to learn, he says, and you are just beginning on the path. That which you have gone through until now is the beginning. What lies ahead is a new chapter. It will be difficult in some ways, he says, and yet it will be a uniquely designed opportunity to be very rapidly progressed along the path of seeking and service.

Through a second instrument, he speaks on the relationship between the intellect and meditation. In your periods of meditation, he says, you shall attain knowledge which is not directly impressed upon your intellect. Yet when you face situations in your daily life, this knowledge shall penetrate from within your being and shall function through you. This knowledge and this growth brings about your faith, which is so greatly needed.

He is honest about the role of the intellect. Intellectual faith is also valuable, he says, and is also a need to your meditation. Each difficulty you experience contains truth, and within this illusion the truth of each situation is very difficult to find by utilizing your thoughts. Allow the intellect to be guided by meditation, he says, and it shall be able to find the great lessons which lie within.

There will be times, he says, when the situation will greatly try your confidence in the world of your Creator. You shall experience times when you shall question His word. This is normal in your growth, for your intellect does continue to operate. Yet each time you question, turn to your meditation. Meditate upon this question, and the awareness and the answer which is needed shall come to you. In this way the intellect is aided, for seeing the truth and finding the answers in meditation, it gives you the intellectual knowledge of faith.

One passage that evening is a warning worth keeping. The group wonders about opening their meetings to entities outside the Confederation, and Hatonn advises against it, at least for now. Such personalities can be informative and interesting, he says, but they are not free of the density you are also within, and their information will be shaped by the same illusion. Wait, he says, until the group has a firm grasp of objective reality. First learn the signal. Then you can afford the noise.

Through another instrument he speaks briefly on loyalty. As one goes about his life, he says, he develops many loyalties to people and family. This loyalty is very important, and as one reaches a higher vibration, one becomes more aware of the appreciation one has for it. Carry it through, he urges. The bonds you honor are part of the work.

He closes with a promise. This group and many like it upon your planet shall shortly be prepared to render great service, he says. We wish shortly to bring lessons of a higher knowledge which shall be of great aid. The knowledge would be too intense for beginners, but you, he says, are well established upon the path.

I want to underline the design claim, because it is so strange. The illusion is designed to produce the obstacles. The difficulties are not bugs in the system. They are the system, built to deliver the exact choices you came to make. If that is true, then every frustration is a delivery, arriving right on time.

A resting thought. The obstacle in front of you today is not a delay in your learning. It is the learning, packaged the only way this density knows how to package it. Do not curse the wrapping. Open it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Remember the Frog
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: remember the frog.

It is the thirteenth of June, nineteen seventy-four, the longest session in this part of the archive, and it contains the strangest and most beloved passage of the early years. The group has been asking questions about fear, about tests, about the future. And in the middle of it, the instrument known as Carla stops, startled. You are not going to believe this, she says. All I see is a frog. I cannot possibly channel a frog.

Hatonn apologizes for the levity. I am sorry for the levity, my friends. And then he tells them to consider the state of a simple frog. This frog is suddenly thrust into the wet wonderland which is his home. He is almost transparent. He evades his enemies. Gradually he attains shape and color, discovers that he can make sound, that he can take life and give it. He discovers that his consciousness is flooded with many thousands of images daily, that he has great power in his hands, and that he has a fate which he must follow. One day the frog is no more, for its body is no longer inhabited, and it sinks back into the bottom of the pond from which it originated.

This frog is a very important person to himself, Hatonn says. His awareness is very central, and that which he loves and that which he dislikes are very real to him. But we who are of the type of entity which you call human are aware that a frog is a frog. Who is right, my friends? And then the answer. We would like to point out that the frog is correct, that you are correct, and that both of you are incorrect. For the nature of both is consciousness. Consciousness which comes from one source, and which is going ultimately to its own source. There is no beginning and no end. There is only the unity, the freedom, and the joy of reunion.

I love that line. You are a prince to yourself, and your right and your wrong are extremely important. But you are only a prince in a small pond, and there is much hope. Allow your consciousness to rise into the light which created you, and ultimately the questions will be answered, for you will know that you are where you are and who you are, and that all is well.

The evening holds other teachings too, and I want to keep the strongest of them. Fear is always an illusion, Hatonn tells one questioner. What can happen to you? You can die. That is a birth. Do not look to your fear for your test, he says, but look behind the fear, for there is a mistaken idea which is causing this fear. This is the test.

And this. Desire, my friends, is not what you think it is. The desire of a man is the man. It is his directional movement, the expression of his basic consciousness, the most basic thing about him. The man who is centered within his desire becomes whole and unified. He compares such a life to a knitted garment, each stitch interconnected, held safely in place as it comes off the needles. Do not pick at the stitches with the intellect, he warns. Accept your existence. Know who you are and what you are seeking. It matters not whether you are sick or well, rich or poor, for these are minor details.

And one last instruction, given like a benediction. If you could see your thoughts from the next dimension, he says, you would discover how undesirable it is to surround yourself with fear, sickness, pain, and lack. Concentrate upon your desires, my friends. If the thought you are entertaining is not full of faith, hope, charity, love, and concern for the spiritual welfare of your fellow man, then put those thoughts aside, and you will not be responsible for their generation.

A resting thought. You are the frog, mid-pond, certain of your importance. And you are right to be certain. You are also the pond, and the light above it, and the source they both came from. Remember the frog, and swim gently.

Thank you for listening.

title: Nothing Is Expended
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: nothing is expended.

It is the twenty-first of June, nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn wants to talk about the one question every meditator secretly asks. How do you picture what you do in meditation? How do you measure your gains? With what instrument are you grading yourself?

He is blunt about the habit. It is the inevitable habit of those upon planet Earth, he says, to demand a type of grading system even for those things which do not lie within the grading systems you have available. That which is measured, he says, is inevitably that which is lost. What you measure is what has been expended.

And in meditation, my friends, nothing is expended. Listen to how he puts it. Meditation is a becoming. A becoming aware of that which already is, in a timeless fashion. One cannot grade it, for it is entirely a living activity. Not living in the sense of this illusion, but living in the sense that eternity lives. It is beyond that which you may know as judging.

He gives the human mind an image for its own confusion. That which you see about you as progress, he says, could be compared to a great coral reef. You observe that which has been left behind by previous effort. You can see it. You can measure it, and this comforts you. But meditation is an opposite process. There is no reef. There is no pile of used effort behind you. There is only the becoming, happening now, in a direction that has no ruler.

Free yourself from the desire to measure your progress in meditation, he says. Free yourself from the fetters of your own systems of measurement, for that which you are desiring is measureless and limitless. Simply allow yourself to seek and to accept, through meditation, the contact with the Creator of us all. That is your duty as a portion of this creation.

A second instrument takes up the practical side. Your daily habits need to be honored so that you can find time for your meditation, he says. Do not allow any more than absolutely necessary your daily activities to encroach upon your meditation. This, he says, is the greatest value of our repetition on the need to meditate. Not guilt. Not a grading system of attendance. Simply the ordering of a life around the one thing that orders everything else.

And do not hold recriminations toward yourself if you miss a day. It would seem to some that meditation is like forming a habit, he says, but not really, because a habit is usually something from which no benefit is necessarily derived. This is not a streak to maintain. It is a door to walk through. Meditation, the third instrument says, will provide you the access to the door through which you must pass to find all of the creation that is about you. It is there for all peoples, in all places, at all times. It is only necessary that they attune their thinking with that of their Creator.

A resting thought. Stop grading the silence. The silence is not a test you can fail or pass. It is a becoming, and a becoming cannot be measured, only entered. Enter it daily, and let the coral reef take care of itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: Left Upon Your Doorstep
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: left upon your doorstep.

It is the twenty-second of June, nineteen seventy-four, and the session opens with Hatonn speaking on the nature of the service the voices offer. Have you considered the way in which we offer that service, he asks. That which we offer is left, as it were, upon your doorstep. We do not remain to discover whether you will take our gift within your dwelling places, nor do we check the uses to which you put it.

We do not come bowing to you, he says, and we do not come requesting that you bow to us. We are here to serve you. We are here to serve ourselves. There is no inequality between us. There is no separation between us. We are here and we are you. We give at the same time that we take. There is no difference. The entire experience is service. I love that image. Not a temple visit. A package on the step, left without ceremony, without surveillance, without a signature required.

He asks them to rest within the silence, because there are concepts best presented there. With those who have obtained direct contact, he says, there are many concepts which may best be presented within the silence. The words are halting phrases. The silence is the better instrument. And he promises that their desire to serve is growing and sharpening, and that there will be a great plenty of work for them in the service of the infinite Creator.

Then something unexpected happens. Through the instrument known as Carla, a new voice breaks in, uncertain of its own name, trying it out like a new coat. I am Teal'onn, it says. This is not quite right. I am Fillonn. And finally, I am Teronn. He is new to the channel, new to the group, new to the planet. I am studying under those of Hatonn, he says. I am here to offer what I can offer of that which I am to that which you are.

And what he offers is beautiful. I am here to give you all of the aid which I possess, he says, of which I possess none, for I am a channel as transparent as sunlight. I only serve to focus the light of the Creator so that another who is seeking may spot this light in a world of murky shadows. A channel as transparent as sunlight. No ego in the glass. Only the focusing.

His message is short and urgent. I wish to say to you with all my heart, he says, look up. Pay attention, my friends. Every day, every breath is fantastic. Do not lose time. Do not lose consciousness. That which you are experiencing is precious unto you. You are experiencing physical existence. This is very precious, my friends. You will not find such intensity possible in other forms of existence.

Each emotion, he says, is indeed like a living color. It may be clear or it may be murky. Those upon your planet seem to be somewhat murky in their emotions. They are attempting to purify their emotions, for they are truly the things that survive. They are not actually emotions, but you know them as emotions. They are the colors of the spectrum of light. They are consciousness. They are all the Creator. And to experience truly these colors is to experience truly the Creator.

Hatonn's instruction for the evening is spare. All that is necessary, he says, is a continued seeking toward the source of light and love which is within each of you. And Teronn, before he leaves, points to the example. That master known as Jesus, he says, maintained an inner contact with his infinite Father, and experienced each moment for that moment. You also may do this, he says, and I urge you to attempt to follow the teaching. Many others have done the same.

He is hopeful about returning. It has been a great privilege to meet you, he says, and he hopes to speak with them again. A new voice, unsure of its own name, and already certain of its message. Look up. Pay attention.

A resting thought. The gift is on your doorstep. No one is watching to see if you pick it up. And the daylight you are standing in is the thing itself. Look up. Pay attention. Every breath is fantastic.

Thank you for listening.

title: Only a Doorway
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: only a doorway.

It is the twenty-third of June, nineteen seventy-four, and Hatonn begins with a question about what the voices actually have to give. Not wisdom, as it turns out. Not answers. What do we have to give you, he asks. We have to give you most of all a door. Only a doorway. Only a suggestion.

Listen to how he describes it. We have to give you the suggestion of another world. Another complete reality. A reality that transcends this reality, that includes this reality, that explains this reality, that will completely outlast this reality, and to which reality you will repair after this brief experience upon the earth plane.

We can give you this suggestion of eternity, he says. We can offer our suggestions as to how to approach this doorway. We have spoken many times of meditation. This is the most efficient way of approaching this door. The desire within you to go through the door, and that alone, will lead you through. Meditation creates the possibility of nearing the door. I love the modesty of that. Not the key. Not the map. The possibility of nearing.

He is honest about who this is for. We can only speak to those who already know that there is something to speak about, he says. To those people to whom reality within the illusion is acceptable, our words will be nothing and less than nothing. To those people who are seeking, our words will find a place. Our words will become your words, my friends, as you seek. For as you seek you will find, and as you are seeking upon the same path which we have trod, our thoughts and your thoughts will become as one.

Then the image that carries the evening. Look at your meditation as the seed, he says, which is growing in the rich soil of your physical existence. It will bear fruit within your existence. And the fragrance and the beauty which meditation sheds throughout the illusion will last far beyond the illusory flower, for the gifts of this fruit last forever.

Allow the seed of meditation to be endlessly nurtured within each day, he says, and that which you need to do to bloom will come to you. The fruit which you need to supply to be of service to others will be possible for you to produce. The energy which you need to grow and flourish will be yours. And when you need rest, there will be time for rest. For once you are committed to the gentle cycles of eternity, the physical illusion very quietly falls into place.

The questions that follow are about the Uri Geller phenomena of that summer, the strange contacts and the powers on display. Hatonn is measured. The central organism of the Confederation, he says, is somewhat like a computer, but made of thought, dimensionless, unifying that which is diverse. We are a field organization, he says. The purpose of these demonstrations? The one who questions knows this answer, he says. It is an advertisement. An advertisement that cannot be proven, but an advertisement that has increased in specificity from previous advertisements.

The questions that evening circle the strange phenomena of that summer, the man called Uri and the researcher who worked with him, and the powers on display around them. Hatonn is measured. Those particular people were chosen, he says, because they carried a specific type of vibration, and because they had intended this experience before this incarnation. What they have seen is a result of who they are. The powers are real, he implies, but they are the least interesting part. The advertisement matters more than the billboard.

And he closes the evening the way he opened it, with the atmosphere between them. As I found you, so I leave you, he says. Surrounded by love. Made totally one by light. The door is still there. The seed is still growing.

A resting thought. The voices do not bring you the house. They bring you the door, the suggestion of the door, and the seed that grows beside it. Walk through when you are ready. The fruit of it will outlast the flower.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Gateways Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gateways within.

It is the twenty-sixth of June, nineteen seventy-four, the last session of this wave, and Hatonn speaks of sleepers. There are many people on your planet at this time, he says, who are in a state which we would call like unto sleep. These people are not aware of any reality. The group has been discussing how to bring them the truth.

Truth, my friends, is very simple, he says. However, it is much different than what you are presently experiencing. Some small demonstrations of reality have been experienced upon your planet, but these demonstrations are of no great magnitude. The understanding the voices speak of cannot be built by explanation. If we could produce this understanding within you by any means of language, he says, we would immediately do this. But the understanding of which we speak is in another complete dimension of space and time.

Listen to what happens in that dimension. That which you think of as fact becomes fantasy, he says. And that which you see as a need becomes, first, meaningless chatter, and then nothing. When all of this has occurred, then you may begin to develop a new understanding. But we cannot build this new understanding within the kingdom which you now venture. I love that phrase. You cannot renovate the house you are still defending.

There are gateways from one dimension to another, he says. These gateways may be used. They may be used by those who desire to use them enough to see that desire. What we offer to you is simply our best indications as to where these gateways may occur within your consciousness.

And the gateways are not where you would look. We recommend that humanity, each in your own way, has the power to find your gateway that is unique, he says. For you are unique. There is no other you. You are as unique as every snowflake and every leaf, and yet you are all one. Together, you are one total creature which is the creation of the One.

By meditation, he says, you may begin to find this gateway. We can call it an awareness of unity. We can call it all consciousness around you. But we are still talking in terms of the old understanding, using a language which will become dead as you begin to see that which lies through the gateway. The words are scaffolding. They fall away when the building stands.

He closes with an availability, not a demand. We are here to guide you, he says. We are available at any time. If you desire conditioning or our contact, it is only necessary to relax, and in meditation avail yourself. Within the silence we will come, my friends. You may not hear us come, for that which we would give to you we would prefer in many cases to give directly, in the form of content rather than in words.

A resting thought. The gateway is not out in the world, waiting to be found. It is in the consciousness that is reading these words, unique as a snowflake, one with everything. Meditate, and the old language dies quietly, and something else begins.

Thank you for listening.

title: Service Is Service
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: service is service.

Three instruments carry this evening's session, and one teaching runs through all three of them. Hatonn begins with simple advice. Look ahead, he says, not backward. Some will stumble. Some will turn away from the seeking for a while. Let them. Look only to the ones who are actively seeking.

Then the contact moves to a second instrument, and the teaching deepens into the evening's heart. Service to others, Hatonn says, is service to oneself. And listen to how careful he is with this. He does not say that service to others is like service to oneself. There is no similarity between others and ourselves. There is identity. There is completion and unity.

No similarity. Identity. I keep coming back to that line, because it changes what service means. It is not a transaction between two separate people. It is one being, tending itself.

Which is why this matters so much: whatever is felt of a negative nature toward one of the flock is felt toward yourself, and is felt toward the Creator. It enters the service you are trying to give and puts a blot upon it, a stain upon the perfect service you would have performed.

So the question becomes: how do you understand, in a true and final way, the identity between yourself and each one whom you serve? Hatonn is honest. There is no intellectual way to do this, he says.

Instead he asks you to practice something very concrete. It is necessary, he says, to walk with the feet of each whom you wish to serve. It is necessary to look through this man's eyes. It is necessary to observe precisely what this person is observing. At that point you can accept this person's oneness with you — at least intellectually. On the level of true spirituality, he says, there is no need for such detailed understanding. To be one with another person, with a planet, with a rock, with a tree, with a star, would all be equally possible.

And then he reaches for the words of the master known as Jesus. Whoever fed a hungry man, or clothed a naked one, or visited those in prison, or helped the widows and orphans, had done it for his sake. For even as they had done it to the least of his brothers, they had done it unto him.

We are almost incapable of believing that other men are identical to ourselves, Hatonn says, while we are trapped in the chemical illusion. But through faith we can begin to understand that each person we wish to serve is the Creator. Plant that seed, he says. Let it grow as you meditate.

There is a strange and beautiful passage in the middle of the evening about negativity itself. Hatonn calls it a type of power, with many manifestations. The religions of the East, he says, personify these negative impulses in beautiful shapes of gods and goddesses. Western culture speaks of Satan and demons. Modern science has derived a great multitude of phrases for them. But all of these, he says, are expressions of one thing: the illusion that we are not one with the Creator. They are all expressions of separation and isolation. There is only one true positive path, and you can recognize it by its simple unity — the seeking of union with the Creator.

The third instrument takes the contact, and Hatonn widens the frame to the whole Creation. It is designed, he says, so that each part of it provides a service, a freely given service, to support all the rest of the Creation. Look about you and you will see it. All parts are performing a service.

Then he gives the image that I will not forget. A blade of grass performs a service. It performs its service to the very limit of its ability. And yet its service is as great as the service of the tree, which is many, many times the size of the tiny blade of grass. For the tree is also performing, to the limit of its ability, its service.

All that is necessary, he says, is to recognize this. Recognize how to perform the service that you may give. And the way to recognize it is to become aware — as simply as the blade of grass has become aware. Serve simply by being. Being in meditation. For through this process you will understand, and you will serve. This, he says, you have always intended to do, just as every other part of the creation.

It is only when man forgets his real purpose, he says, that he becomes isolated and lost, unable to avail himself of the love that is given to him by all the rest of the Creation. Become aware of your service. Become aware of your purpose. Do this through meditation, and you will awaken. You will awaken, he says, to the ecstasy that was meant to be experienced by each part of this infinite creation.

That is the evening. A blade of grass, a tree, and the teaching that there is no difference in the size of what they give. Small is not small. The only thing that makes a service small is the belief that the one you serve is other than yourself. Thank you for listening.

title: Thought Molds Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: thought molds light.

This is a short session, and the tape runs out before the evening does. But what survives is worth the whole evening: a few clear words from Hatonn about what your mind actually is, and what it can do when it remembers itself.

The first part of the night concerns a sign. Hatonn had spoken earlier of an occurrence in the night sky, at the changing of the season. He says now that the effect will be gradual, accomplished over a period of time, and that the group's scientists will speak of it as it progresses, offering their explanations. Watch the sky, he says, and watch what those who are called scientists say about it. There is no drama in his voice about any of this. It is simply something to notice.

Then the questions turn, and the evening finds its real subject. Someone asks about powers — the powers of mind that were much in the news that year, the kind of demonstrations that made headlines. Hatonn does not laugh at the question. He answers it straight, and his answer is larger than the question.

All of you, he says, have so many powers, due to the fantastic amount of energy in your body — not of a physical nature, not of light nature — that you are capable of phenomena far, far greater than anything the famous demonstrators can do. The famous ones, he says, only vaguely remember what they can do. And the rest of us remember almost nothing of the birthright of our energy, because of the extreme isolation of the illusion we chose.

Those who watch such demonstrations and find they can duplicate them, he says, are simply remembering how reality works. Listen to how he puts it: it is not an intellectual process. It is a direct process. It is a process of consciousness.

And then the sentence that gives this episode its title. As each tiny portion of the universe is made of light, molded and shaped by consciousness or love, consciousness directed can mold light into new forms. This is direct use of energy, he says. This should be the norm.

I love that last line. This should be the norm. The miraculous is not a violation of how things work. It is how things work, when we have not forgotten.

Your thought, Hatonn says, is more powerful than any physical illusion. Thus it is said in your holy works that faith can move mountains. Faith is in consciousness, whereas a mountain is that which consciousness has molded — and can unmold at will.

Think about that the next time a mountain in your own life looks permanent. What consciousness has molded, consciousness can unmold. The strange and unusual thing, Hatonn says, is to watch man upon Earth go through a long process of analysis and technological tool-using in order to do what is a very fundamental and simple job.

Someone asks what it would take, and Hatonn does not pretend it is easy. Continue in meditation, he says. There is a long road — not long in time, but in sacrifice of that which is illusion. It is entirely within your grasp, depending upon your desire. Much of the illusion must be shed, and in many cases this is too painful for the entity to accept. But if the entity accepts what must be done, she will discover that she is a person who can move mountains.

And then, near the very end of the tape, he says a word or two concerning vulnerability. We know, he says, how easy it is to become used to anything, and so cease feeling the miraculous side of it. It is possible to do that with both the positive and negative feelings.

The tape ends there, mid-thought, as if the universe wanted that sentence to be the last word. And maybe it is the right last word. We become used to everything. The sunrise, the body that carries us, the people who love us, the strange fact of being conscious at all. The miraculous side fades, not because it went anywhere, but because we stopped feeling it.

The powers Hatonn speaks of are not really about bending spoons or moving mountains. They are about remembering. Remembering that the light is molded by consciousness, and that your consciousness is part of the molding. The mountain is not the obstacle. Forgetting is the obstacle. And forgetting, like everything else consciousness has made, can be unmade. Thank you for listening.

title: The Ball and Chain
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the ball and chain.

Hatonn opens this evening with a story. It is about a person much like each of you, he says. His thoughts were as your thoughts. In his work-a-day world he was neither perfectly good nor perfectly evil, but somewhere in the middle, attempting to do the best that he could.

This man carried about his ankle a ball and chain — a heavy weight, attached with an unbreakable lock. Everywhere he went, he had to take infinite pains to make each step. He spent many years attached to it. He grew accustomed to it. He thought it was a normal situation.

One day he discovered some information that interested him. It was information on how to remove that particular type of ball and chain from his ankle. He followed the instructions — not perfectly, but acceptably — and the ball and chain became lighter. This made him interested in the instructions. And as he practiced them, his ball and chain gradually disappeared.

My friends, Hatonn says, your physical bodies, and your personal sense of self which you call ego, are a ball and chain to you, making your infinite spirit take great pains in order to move about. You, whose birthright is freedom, have to crawl about using mechanical conveyances, when within you is freedom to be anywhere at any time.

We offer you some simple instructions, he says, on how to lighten and remove the hampering limitations of your ball and chain. The instructions have to do with meditation. In meditation you are separating the sense of body and the sense of ego from the sense of consciousness. And you are freeing your consciousness to be at one with the source of love and light that is the infinite Creator.

He is careful, though, not to speak unkindly of the ball and chain. It is necessary for you at this time, he says. You have chosen these limitations, in order that you may bring yourself face to face with lessons of the universe. You are learning lessons of love and patience and understanding. If you are not learning them, you will have another chance at the same lessons at a future time. And you will meet that lesson until you have learned it.

Listen to how he puts this, because it is one of the kindest sentences in the archive. There is no failing in this type of school. In this planetary school, one simply continues in the same grade until one has learned all the lessons. There is no sense of failing. There is only a sense of graduation when one has learned all the lessons of one cycle.

Each of you is within his own cycles, and the lessons are necessary and good. But you may speed your trip to graduation very, very much by the use of meditation. Through meditation you make contact with the infinity of understanding which lies within the consciousness of the Creator. When you come back to the limitation of your physical body and personality, you are carrying with you an infinite amount of understanding, which you may choose to put to use.

The contact moves to another instrument, and the teaching takes a practical turn. Lessons learned in meditation, Hatonn says, have to be applied in your daily life. Meditation alone will give you the awareness to adjust your daily activities and to gain a finer appreciation of the people you meet and their needs. But an active attempt at application is necessary, or your conscious mind will stray too far from what you began to acquire.

This is very difficult, he admits, because in the physical illusion the natural reaction to negativity is negativity. And participating in it only creates more negativity. To counter negativity with a positive attitude tends to at least equalize it, if not overcome it a little.

So do not contribute more negative thought and action to your illusion. To the degree that is possible, exude positive thoughts — thoughts of love for every situation. And here is a small jewel I want to make sure you hear. Love consciously directed at another person, or at a particular situation, is doubly positive, he says. Not only is the love itself involved, but also the positive thought that caused the emanation of that love. So the love is compounded.

I am as you, he says. I am such as you. Those of us who are here have stepped across one blockage that you have yet to achieve. But there are many steps ahead of us. We are looking back and holding out our hands, so that you may step over that blockage with as much ease as you possibly can.

He is not infallible, he says. He can only communicate what he thinks is truth. So he suggests this: take nothing for granted in what we say. Try what we suggest and see for yourself. It should not take very long for you to discover whether we may have something.

That is the spirit of the whole evening, really. Here are the instructions for removing the ball and chain. Follow them, not perfectly, but acceptably. Watch the weight get lighter. And discover for yourself whether the man in the story, dragging his lock across the floor, was always free to put it down. Thank you for listening.

title: The Creator Lives Your Life
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the Creator lives your life.

Hatonn begins this evening with a strange claim about time. It is strange to you, he says, that we would be with you at all times. But your awareness of the illusion is such that you do not understand the real properties of time. In truth there is only one instance, and that instance is the one you are experiencing. There is an illusion of past and an illusion of future. You exist only in the present. The others are never.

Because of this, he says, contact with us does not take time. You have the contact at all times. It is constantly with you. All it requires is your desire. Simply by desiring, the channel received what he desired. He did this through daily meditation, and his desire to be of service created his ability to serve.

Then Hatonn turns to the evening's real subject, and it is a single word: understanding. He knows it is a vague word, and he wants to make it precise. Understanding, he says, is unitary. Understanding is light. Understanding is direct awareness of love.

Consider your planet as it moves in its orbit, he says. It can be seen as a complete and unitary orb. It can be understood as an entity, for it is light and it is love. Come closer, and you can differentiate: air and land and ocean. Each of these is a direct awareness of love — the love of the Creator, who created these things. Come closer still. Stand on the surface and see the irregular shapes, the living things doing many things and thinking many thoughts. And see that this understanding is, in essence, still one thing. For each of these is a direct example of the love, the original Thought of love, of the Father of us all.

I love the way he moves the camera there. From orbit, to shoreline, to the street you are standing on — and the teaching does not change at any distance. It only gets more detailed. Everything you are looking at is the original Thought, wearing different clothes.

As you meditate, allow your thoughts to rise upward into the vibration of that which is love and light, so that you become one with the original Thought of the Creator. It is to this that we point you.

The contact moves to another instrument, and Hatonn speaks what he calls a great secret: a simple change in point of view, but centrally important.

How hard are you working, he asks, to live the best life? Are you attacking each moment as if you could wrest out of it spiritual awareness and happy results? This is indeed the approved mode of operation upon your planet. And as long as you keep the consciousness that you must exact from an alien universe that which is yours, you will have struggle and difficulty.

Question yourself, he says, as to who it was that accomplished the miracles in the experience of the master known as Jesus. Remember that according to your holy works he did not take credit, but gave full credit to the Creator who was within him and did the work for him.

My friends, this is a great secret. You do not live your life, any more than I live my life. You look over your shoulder and the Creator lives your life.

Let that sentence sit for a moment. You do not live your life. You look over your shoulder, and the Creator lives your life. Your consciousness learns. But if you let that which is within you — what you may call a spark of the Creator — do that which is to be done, all things will come to you naturally that belong to you.

This point of view, he says, will not give you perfect contentment. He is honest about that. If you were completely, unalterably contented, this illusion would not be very useful to you. What it gives you is a way for each crisis to be accepted, dealt with, and dropped away — in such a manner that those who see you may learn by your example that it is possible to live in an illumined fashion.

As you meditate, clarify within yourself what you seek, and allow yourself to become aware of the unity of all that is about you with yourself. Allow yourself to become aware that your environment is one of unity, and that what you seek is completely within yourself. And allow the peace which follows this awareness to expand throughout your conscious mind.

Near the end he greets the group in an unusual way. I greet you, he says, in fire, in wind, and with the forces of your planet, which also greet you. I am far above you, and yet I greet you within your heart. For I am all things and I am you.

The understanding he offers is very simple, he says, and it cannot be attacked. It comes naturally, without pride, humbly — easy to accept and easy to forget.
