Accept it, he says, as it becomes natural to you, not before. And know that the path leads upward, and that it is possible to follow it. Because someone is always one step ahead on it, holding the lantern. Thank you for listening.

title: The Turning Point
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the turning point.

Hatonn calls this a slightly more personal message. The whole evening is one question, asked in different ways: are you reacting to your life, or are you using it?

He begins with the purpose of the illusion itself. In truth, he says, the only reason for the illusion you now experience is to act as a catalyst — to generate a condition which helps the individual to initiate a spiritual seeking. It might seem strange that you should go through such an unusual experience only for this. But this, in fact, is true.

Each of you in his daily experience is acted upon in many ways, he says. The actions and experiences you feel cause changes in your attitude, cause reactions which you interpret and identify as emotion. All of this is for a specific purpose, and you have chosen to experience your present illusion in order to achieve it. The purpose is the evolution of your spirit.

Only the very few, he says, are consciously aware of this. Most have not reached what he calls the salient point of transition — the point that causes a great acceleration in spiritual evolution. That point at which they become consciously aware, and then begin to use their experiences, in a conscious manner, to teach themselves.

And then he asks each person in the room to question himself. Am I, he says — and I am putting his long sentence in plain words — am I still in blind reaction to everything that happens to me? Or have I begun the transition to conscious and full use of my lessons? Each of you will draw your own conclusion.

The heart of the evening is self-awareness. It is necessary, he says, to be aware of your reactions, to be aware of your emotions. To be aware, my friends, is to know yourself. To first know yourself — this is the initiation of awareness.

Each action, each thought, each word you say is of utmost importance, he says. For this is you in expression. And what is you in expression, to those about you, is of very great importance. For this, he says, is the reason for experiencing the illusion.

This is the difference, he says, between mastership and the simple growth of spirit. And what creates this difference? There is one, and only one, thing that will allow you to make this transition — from emotional reaction, from blind and stumbling reaction to your environment, to a controlled and sincere seeking path.

The only thing that will allow you to do this is meditation. Daily meditation will create the foundation. And then, he says, each of you will grow at such a fantastic rate that it will be beyond even your own comprehension.

Spiritual growth, he says, is the function of the individual. It is not given to you. It is something you have always had, but it must be uncovered — uncovered through your own activities, through your own understanding. We can provide only the guideposts. Only the simple instructions. Only a helping hand.

Late in the evening the contact shifts, and Hatonn speaks to one who questions about service. And here is a teaching I want to make sure you hear, because it dissolves a worry I think many seekers carry. You need not worry, he says, about recognizing the service you are to perform. What you must do, by some method, is realize that you are fragmenting your precious consciousness when you desire more than one thing.

It is necessary only to desire to be in the presence of the Creator, he says, and to know his love. If that desire is perfect within you, you will be of enormous service. You cannot help being of enormous service if you are aware of your identity in seeking. Only seek to know the Father, and you will pour forth the fruits of this knowledge as readily as the sun gives light.

As readily as the sun gives light. The sun does not decide whom to shine on. It does not worry about whether its shining is the right service. It shines, and the shining is the service.

Your problem, he says, will never be what your service will be. It will be whether you are capable of accepting each service. You will find yourself placed before your service, and it will be your choice whether to accept it. You are a channel for the Father, he says. It is necessary only to keep yourself open, and the love and the light that is needed by others will flow through you. Let it shine out of your eyes, he says, and let it flow through your fingers.

And then this, as the evening closes. Be aware, my friends, that you are already serving. Each of you in this room has served, is serving, and will serve. We are not speaking to those who are not of service already. We are speaking to those who are already seriously seeking. And so we give encouragement. We give you our support, and our love, and our light. We are with you always. Know this, my friends. Never doubt it.

The turning point is not ahead of you. If you are listening to this, you may already be standing in it. Thank you for listening.

title: Neither Add Nor Subtract
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: neither add nor subtract.

Hatonn arrives this evening with a watering can. His words. I come, shall we say, with a watering can, he says. I come to encourage your growth in the spirit. It is a small image, and a gentle one, and it sets the tone for everything that follows. This is an evening about the gentlest kind of seeking.

His advice about meditation is simple, and it runs against every instinct of the achieving mind. In your meditation, he says, neither add nor subtract. It is very easy to make demands of yourself and to attempt to accomplish goals through meditation. It is also very likely that at some time you will try to remove some part of yourself through meditation.

He does not speak against these practices. They are simply outside of our interest, he says. There is one choice which is outside of the illusion, and that choice is the choice to seek your Creator. This is the choice that ultimately transcends illusion. And within this choice there is neither addition nor subtraction — but an opening. Precisely as you are now accomplishing, he says, not even really aware that this is the heart of your seeking.

Then he gives an image for the body. Imagine, he says, that this mortal physical body is a door which you may go through. Each of you will go through this door. It is called, upon your planet, death. And there is a certain joy, for those who understand these things, connected with going through it.

But within you, he says, there are many such doors. They are opened, and you transcend each shell, when the experience for which it was provided is no longer necessary. If you truly seek to open yourself to the innermost core of all these shells, your journey will be immeasurably quickened, so that you may at last become one with that which you seek.

That which you seek, he says, is unimaginable. We can call it a thought. We can call it an impulse. You have the word consciousness in your language, and in some dim way this concept is correct. The source of all consciousness is the Creator. We are all a part of this consciousness. And in its infinity it yet remains a gloriously illuminating source of light — perfect light and love within each of the Creator's children.

That which you seek, then, rests within yourselves. The separation is within yourselves. This separation is not evil, he says. This separation is functional. Your consciousness has been given to you by all consciousness, so that you may individually seek and find the beauty and the understanding which is the Creator. And all that is necessary, he says, is that you do so.

He knows the group has questions about difficult decisions, and he speaks to that too. In his experience, he says, the attempt to decide what to do — even at the most spiritual level — becomes a negative experience. Circumstances which require the application of patience are designed to instruct one in patience. The answers you are seeking will evolve with a naturalness which may be sudden, but which can be experienced without the negative effects of having imposed an arbitrary decision upon your higher self.

Then he takes up an old misunderstanding. Man considers himself master of all he surveys, he says. And man is indeed master of all he surveys — if he is master of himself. But to be master of yourself does not mean the ability to control, according to arbitrary decisions, what you think and do. To be master of oneself is to know one's reality.

Listen to how he describes this mastery. It is given from within, he says, through the gentle and passionless unfolding. And yet — and I love this turn — there is no greater passion than the blazing desire which fills the heart of those who seek to know, to really know, the presence, the love, and the light of the Father.

Late in the evening a second voice speaks. Laitos, who serves those learning to be instruments, offers something practical and kind. If you take five minutes, he says, and you call for me, I will be there. At any time you can go into a light enough meditation to call for this contact, and I will attempt to bring you a conditioning wave.

He knows you will doubt. Accept this, he says. Go right ahead and doubt. But if you wish to serve as an instrument, simply continue availing yourself, and it will not be long before you can register our contact. It does not take a great solemn meditation to begin to become a channel, he says, for we are most eager to speak with you. And it is your seeking, more than any other characteristic, which creates the correct vibration for us to make contact.

I leave you, he says, but only the sound of my voice is leaving you.

That is the evening's teaching, from the watering can to the five minutes. Do not add. Do not subtract. Do not demand, do not decide for your higher self. Open, like something being watered, and let the blossoming happen at its own speed. The blazing desire is enough. It has always been enough. Thank you for listening.

title: Clear, Aware, Expand
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: clear, aware, expand.

Hatonn says there is only one thing worth seeking. Nothing else is of any value. That one thing is understanding — an understanding of your Creator's Thought. This, he says, is the only thing that lasts. Anything else you might seek will be transitory, and will vanish with time.

When man realizes this is his true objective, he says, then he has made that great turning point in his development. We are here to aid those who have turned the corner, so to speak — turned the corner toward their ultimate goal, the goal of reuniting with their Creator.

And this evening he does not speak in generalities. He comes, he says, to instruct the group in a specific technique. Three steps. That is all. But he warns you first about what this understanding is not. It has nothing to do with your intellectual understanding, your ability to manipulate ideas or propositions. This understanding is your awareness, which totally transcends all intellect.

Here are the steps. First, clear your mind. Let the thoughts of your daily life drift away, he says, for these are very transient thoughts. These thoughts will be gone in a few days. Let them go now. Let the influence of your material environment leave your thinking. Let your mind be clear. Let it be as a child.

Do not attempt to understand, he says — do not attempt to understand, my friends, and then you will know. For you cannot understand by a process of trying. You must understand by a process of knowing. Do not try to come to a conclusion. Do not try to analyze. Do not try to use past experiences. Simply allow your mind to become clear.

Second, become aware of yourself. Nothing else matters — simply yourself. Do not think about your thinking. Do not analyze yourself. Do not use the intellectual mind. Simply become aware of your own being. Allow this awareness to grow, from a very clear and unfettered mind. Become aware of yourself and nothing else. Think of nothing else. Become aware of only yourself, surrounded by nothing.

Third — and this, he says, is the all-important step — expand. Let your own being expand. Let it move outward in all directions. Let it encompass all of infinity. Let it then know that it, in an infinitely expanded state, is all that there is. It is one and the same with every other thing, with every other experience, with every other particle in this entire infinite creation. Nothing is excluded.

In the illusion, man has been conditioned to think of himself as a separate, isolated being. This bias creates vibrations of thought unlike the vibrations that created you. The exercise changes those vibrations, so that you return to the vibration that created you. That vibration, he says, is reality.

When you have accomplished it, you will no longer be able to identify anything that exists as anything but yourself. This will not be intellectual. You will not have to tell yourself this. It will be a simple reality — a reality you experience automatically, as you breathe the air about you automatically. And then, he says, you will be known as a master, for this is all that is necessary to attain this dignity. This was all that was necessary for the man known as Jesus. He was aware of his relationship to the creation. He was aware that he and all were one.

Clear the mind. Become aware of yourself. And then expand. Expand infinitely and be one. If this is practiced in daily meditation, he says, you will no longer question anything, for you will know — you will be with the knowledge that has created you. A very simple knowledge. It has been called by the people of your planet a knowledge of love. A knowledge of a love so intense that it is beyond expression in your language. This you will know. This you will experience.

Late in the evening, speaking through another instrument, Hatonn adds two things I want you to carry with you. First: meditation is you. He says it plainly. As you learn each lesson, remain aware enough of what you are doing that meditation does not become separate from you. Meditation shall not be something that you do. Meditation is you.

Second, he speaks of the lions that guard the temple of understanding. You have become aware, he says, that outer experience is illusion and that reality lies within. And after you became aware of this — did the lions not harm you whenever you slipped and behaved as though you were not aware? Have you not been painfully aware of the times when the lions turned on you, when you demonstrated that which was not love?

I think anyone who has tried to live by what they know has met those lions. The teaching is not new, and suddenly the old behavior hurts in a way it did not hurt before. That pain, Hatonn suggests, is not punishment. It is guardianship. The temple is real, and you are inside it now.

Three steps. Clear. Aware. Expand. Everything else — the lions, the questions, the whole long road — is commentary. Thank you for listening.

title: The Circle Is Complete
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the circle is complete.

The group has been asking about categories. Densities, levels, the colors of the rainbow — the architecture of the spiritual universe, named and ordered. Hatonn has been listening. And this evening he answers, gently and without apology, that the question itself is the problem.

We know your people, he says. We have become more sophisticated in your ways through the years we have spent in this sector of time and space, and we know the desire of your people for their categories to be named. The instrument herself is almost reluctant to speak this, because her own thinking has been on these very thoughts.

But, he says — and listen, because he chooses his words with care — we can only tell you that the very idea of density and category, the colors of the rainbow, each of the categorical functions which the human mind so values, is a trap and a delusion in the spiritual sense. We cannot put it any more gently, he says, and have you understand what we mean.

You must understand, he says, that all categories are occupants of this illusion which you now enjoy — which you have enjoyed since your physical birth, and which you will cease enjoying upon your physical death. There is no harm in understanding the categories you must cope with inside the illusion. But to let them seep into your spiritual search is to let a crippling influence, a halting and blinding influence, encroach upon your search for the source of life within you.

Our understanding, he says, is that all things are one. Nothing could be simpler than this understanding. To ask for ramifications, categories, colors of the rainbow, densities, or any other list of characteristics, is to attempt to impose illusion on reality.

Reality is not a process, he says. Reality does not change. That which is light, simply is. It is neither active nor passive. It occupies no paradoxes.

I want to sit with that sentence a moment. That which is light, simply is. Not becoming. Not improving. Not ascending through levels. Simply is. Everything we add to that — the ladders, the grades, the maps — is the mind doing what the mind does inside the illusion: sorting.

The beginning and the ending, he says, are this unity. At the end of the physical lies all eternity. And yet eternity implies a process, an endless process. This is true, he says, for there are many lessons to be learned as you grow closer to your beginning and your end. But it is our understanding that there is a point at which eternity itself is no more. And in the eyes of one who truly understands, one simply becomes that which is.

Becoming is done. The circle is complete. Unity is truly known.

Information about densities and categories, he says, is of the lesser type. Information such as this — the philosophical kind — is of the higher type. It is the difference between studying the map and standing in the country.

The contact moves to another instrument, and the teaching turns practical. The group sits inside what Hatonn calls a myriad of confused thoughts and ideas — the noise of the society they live in. Meditation, he says, erases that noise and allows it to be replaced with a single Thought: the Thought of your Creator. A Thought of total and absolute love. A Thought so complete, so total, and so pure that it and it alone was able to create this entire creation.

A Thought so powerful, he says, that it generated itself in every other thing.

This is what you are concerned with, he says. Returning to this thinking. This was also our objective, for we are still seeking. We think it absolute in its most purest form.

And then the honest admission. It is a very simple task, he says — and very complex, it seems, for man to follow. Complex, my friends, because it is difficult for you to return to simplicity.

Difficult to return to simplicity. The categories were never the destination. They were the mind's way of postponing the simple thing: the single Thought, the total love, the circle that was already complete before you started drawing it. All that is necessary, he says, is desire. We are here to inspire the desire. You will find your path because of your desire.

Put down the map. Stand in the country. The circle is complete, and it never wasn't. Thank you for listening.

title: Returning to Simplicity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: returning to simplicity.

This session was given the same day as the last one — a second sitting, a second meditation, and the same teaching spoken twice. When a teacher repeats himself in one day, I pay attention. Some things need to be heard more than once before they land.

The heart of it is a single Thought. Not a system, not a map of densities, not a ladder of levels. A Thought — capital T, in Hatonn's language — of total and absolute love. A Thought so complete, so total, and so pure, he says, that it and it alone was able to create this entire creation.

Your daily life fills your mind with what he calls a myriad of confused thoughts and ideas. The noise of your society, the churn of its concerns. Meditation, he says, erases that noise. It allows the confusion to be replaced with the single Thought of your Creator.

Think of it as cleaning a window. You do not paint a new view on the glass. You remove what is in the way, and the view was there all along.

And here is the part that stings a little, because it is true. It is a very simple task, he says — and very complex, it seems, for man to follow. Complex, my friends, because it is difficult for you to return to simplicity.

Difficult to return to simplicity. We left simplicity a long time ago, and we have built such elaborate structures in the meantime — philosophies, categories, the colors of the rainbow, the names of every level — that the way back looks too plain to be real. The mind distrusts what it cannot complicate.

But the simplicity is the point. With this Thought, he says, all things are one. Even the complexities you experience within your society are accomplished by this Thought, as it expresses itself in infinite and variable acts. The Thought does not abolish complexity. It contains it. The way back is not around the world you built. It is through it, to the quiet underneath.

All that is necessary, he says, is the practice of daily meditation. The elimination of the transitory. A rebirth, a transition — from thinking of nothing that matters to thinking of the one thing that does. This requires no special instruction, no special technique. All that is required is desire.

Listen to that again. All that is required is desire. Not worthiness. Not readiness. Not the right teacher or the right book or the right decade of your life. Desire. We are here, he says, to inspire the desire. You will find your path because of your desire.

There is something deeply kind in the idea that the whole enterprise rests on wanting. Not achieving, not perfecting — wanting. The wanting is the engine. The single Thought does the rest.

The evening's teaching, heard twice in one day, comes down to this. Stop adding. The categories, the questions about which level and which color — Hatonn called them a trap in the earlier sitting, and he does not soften it here. They are the mind's way of staying busy while avoiding the one thing it fears, which is also the one thing it wants: the simple, total, blindingly plain love at the bottom of everything.

Return to it. That is the whole instruction. Return to simplicity, and let the single Thought replace the myriad. It was never far. It was never complicated. It was only waiting for you to want it. Thank you for listening.

title: Already Total Perfection
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: already total perfection.

Hatonn begins with a kindness for anyone who feels they are not getting anywhere. I am aware, he says, that it sometimes seems very little is accomplished in your seeking. But this is far from true. Your seeking is the most important activity in which you engage. There is nothing you do, no thought you make, that is more important or necessary than the simple seeking for understanding.

Then he says the sentence that gives this episode its title. It is very difficult, it seems, to become a reflection of total perfection. My friends, he says, this is an illusion in itself. For you are already total perfection.

You are already total perfection. Not becoming. Not approaching. Already. The Creator of us all, he says, has created nothing but perfection. Any discrepancy from this is an illusion brought about by the individual. All that is necessary is that you realize your total unity with the Creator. Realize this through daily meditation, and then express it — express it in every thought and in every deed — and you will have found precisely what you seek.

It is a very simple formula, he says. And one might ask: if this simplicity is so evident, why is it not practiced? There is only one reason. The individual has allowed the illusion in which he finds himself to become real. This supposed reality occurs only if an individual allows it.

If you find yourself influenced in your daily activities in a way that does not conform to the thought of your Creator, he says, it is simply due to insufficient meditation. He suggests, for those who wish to progress at an accelerated rate, periods of daily meditation — several periods daily — sufficient to dissolve the seeming negative catalyst that acts upon your awareness.

The contact moves to another instrument, and someone in the group's mind is carrying a question: why does the Confederation come at all? Why speak through channels to a small room? Hatonn understands the puzzlement. Within your density, he says, that approach would not work — it would not cause the change in the group that is intended. And there is the matter of free will. Most attempts by the advanced to uplift the less advanced — the missionaries, the government social programs — have ended, he notes, with a very low success rate. The Confederation hopes its own success rate is higher, and this is why it does not come among you and attempt to force you to understand.

Instead, he says, think of us as a cheering team. You are at the beginning of a truly new age, he says. The vibrations are being made new. Those who embody the consciousness of great beings will become that which they know. We have made the step. We exist within this environment, and we know what a cheering team can do. So we cheer you along. Do your technique, he says. Do your homework — so that you may be what you desire to be. These things do not happen by accident. They happen by desire. And that desire must originate within you.

There is much joy and beauty, he says, in the constant presence of the Father, very apparent within the new vibration. The new vibration is love, as is the old vibration. And yet the truth of love becomes a little more obvious with the higher vibrations.

Through meditation, he says, you may begin to see the heart of love in all the clumsy actions of all those who enter your atmosphere in your daily activities. There may be misspent time and mistaken words. And yet each action and each desire is, in truth, a manifestation of love — shadowed and twisted sometimes, for man is also a creator and can change the shape of love. Yet the heart of all action is love.

I want to stay with that a moment. The heart of all action is love. Not the heart of noble action, or wise action. All action. The rude stranger, the failed plan, the wasted afternoon — somewhere underneath, love, wearing a disguise it chose. Know this in your inmost self, Hatonn says, and then you cannot be touched by the illusion which attempts to strike you. The freedom this gives you — to give forth love in its original state, at all times, to all people — is a very precious gift, we think.

This is why the Confederation is here, he says. We are all here — many of us, from different planets, from different vibrations, from various densities, in many circumstances — yet we all work together. For we have all come to know the Creator, and we all wish to be of service to him. And that alone is enough for us.

We only wish to help you, he says. We are here always — in words, if you may find a channel, and without words, if you desire our presence. We are always with you, to lend our vibrations to your meditation, if you so desire.

You are already total perfection. The cheering team is already cheering. The only thing left is the simplest thing: realize it, express it, and let the illusion be what it is — a costume party that love threw for itself. Thank you for listening.

title: Give Away Everything
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: give away everything.

This evening Hatonn speaks directly to those learning to be channels, and his teaching is not gentle. Or rather — it is gentle the way a surgeon's hands are gentle. Precise, and not flinching.

Your inner eye is unclouded, he tells them. It is only your outer eye which becomes confused, and which sees mists and quicksand. In your work, which is a good service, use your inner eye — for that alone will serve you as you do the will of the Father.

Each of you sits bathed in light, he says. From inside each of you I perceive your desire to be of service. That this fountain may run clear and sweet is our chief concern.

And then the hard teaching. As you desire to go forth and serve, he says, know this: you must be prepared to give away all that you have to give. You must be prepared to walk away and not look back. For there is nothing that you can do for your Creator — but everything.

It is a hard lesson, he says. People always have the illusion with which to part within this lesson, and they say: everything? Not everything. But everything must belong to the Creator.

Listen to how he puts the promise that follows. If you may realize this within your own thinking, your service will become such a thing as I cannot possibly describe.

Then he gives the image of the plant. There is an inevitable blooming of every plant, he says, and each tree will bear fruit in its time. The fruit of your service is a long time coming. You have worked toward this moment for a long time. But the final fruits come only after the fruit has dropped from the plant which gave it life.

Do not take these words intellectually, he says. We are not speaking of the physical, but of the spiritual. Do not think in terms of the visible, for service is invisible. All those things which are visible, in reality, are invisible — eternal, and completely without end. For they are all one thing. They are all the Creator.

Everything must be given to the Creator, he says, because the Creator is everything.

I think about the plant that has to let the fruit drop. The giving is not complete while you are still holding it, still checking whether it is ripe enough, still standing close enough to watch it land. The fruit has to leave the branch. The service has to leave your hands. That is the part we resist — the part where it is no longer ours.

The indifference you will meet, he says — the massive indifference, the difficulties, the hindrances of service — may be turned in an instant, by the service of your own thinking, from a neutrality to a glorious joy. The hindrances are part of an illusion which is not yours to understand. It is simply yours to experience.

And then the most beautiful passage of the evening. This service, he says, begins within your heart — which is completely empty and open, for you have given all that you have to the Creator. And in return, the Creator has come into this empty and open place. The Creator has filled your essence with his love and his light, and you have become a true channel, able to illuminate each moment with love.

Empty, so that you can be filled. That is the whole economy of it. You give everything away, and what returns is not yours either — it is the Creator's, passing through. The channel does not own the water. The channel is the shape the water takes on its way somewhere else.

Your service will come, he says. As you desire, it shall be. You may therefore prepare — and having prepared, you may lie down in rest, content with the glory shining around you.

Prepare, and then rest. Give away everything, and then lie down. There is a trust in that sequence that undoes all our striving. The fruit drops when it is ripe. The fountain runs clear when nothing is damming it. Give away everything — and discover that everything was never yours to keep. Thank you for listening.

title: The Great Choice-Maker
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the great choice-maker.

This evening begins with a question that lives, unasked, in many minds. Why are you here in this room, seeking — while so many others feel no desire to seek at all? What makes the difference? Hatonn gives the question a name. What, he asks, is the great choice-maker?

It is not an easy concept to understand, he says. But it is an extremely simple concept.

What you know as energy, or consciousness, or love, he says, is far wider in its definition than you can imagine. The vibration level which forms the density you now enjoy has a lower and an upper limit. Within those limits there are infinite varieties of vibration. And those upon this planet are existing within many, many of these various levels.

Within the lower levels, he says, there is an excess of certain types of energy, which express themselves in aggressive and energetic action. These are often seen among the very people who do not wish our aid. Gradually, one begins to use up — or transmute — this energy, and another type begins to manifest. For energy is never destroyed, as you already know.

The higher levels have a less physically energetic aspect, and the intellectual aspects of vibration begin to be experienced. After enough experience, that energy too is used up, transmuted again to a higher level.

And the catalyst for this transmutation, in all cases, is either experience or meditation. Experience, he says, is an extremely sure but somewhat slow-moving catalyst.

I love the honesty of that phrase. Sure, but slow. Experience will get you there. It will just take the long road — lifetime after lifetime of bumping into the same walls until the walls teach you what they were built to teach. Meditation is the shorter road. Same destination, fewer bruises.

It is possible, he says, to speed your progress by contacting the creation that is within you. And this is what we have been attempting to guide you toward.

Then he turns to the group, and his tone warms. Each of you, he says, is attracted to what we have to give because you have, in the past, managed to accumulate enough experience within this vibration that you are now vibrating at the level where your desires are attempting to satisfy themselves by moving into the higher vibrations of spiritual seeking.

You have traveled far, my friends. It has been a long journey. You have an infinity of traveling to do yet, I assure you — but the lessons are good.

Think about what that means. You are not here because you are better, or luckier, or chosen. You are here because you have been traveling a long time, and you are tired in the particular way that makes a person start looking up. The seeking is not a virtue. It is a symptom of distance traveled.

He is sorry, he says — indeed sorry — that they cannot aid those who have not desired aid. It is not allowed to interfere with anyone's free choosing of their path. They will desire this aid in good time, he says, and we or our brothers will be there to aid them. For this is the plan of the Creator.

There is no urgency in that sentence, and no judgment. The great choice-maker is not choosing between the worthy and the unworthy. It is the slow transmutation of energy, level by level, until the desire itself changes. Everyone arrives. The only variable is the road — the sure, slow road of experience, or the quicker road of turning within.

So if you are listening to this, and you are seeking, Hatonn would tell you that you have already answered the question about yourself. The desire is the evidence. You have traveled far. The lessons are good. And there is an infinity of traveling yet to do — which is not a burden, but the whole point. Thank you for listening.

title: A Knowing That Is
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: a knowing that is.

Hatonn speaks this evening from a craft high above the house where the group sits. It is a craft known to you as a flying saucer, he says — and then, with a kind of cosmic humor, he adds: yes, my friends, we are here and we are very close. Yet you cannot see us. Your instruments cannot see us. The radar and other devices are not useful. Yet we are here.

There are millions, he says, surrounding your planet — surrounding it with one purpose in mind. To bring to you understanding. But this is something we can only offer, he says. It is necessary for man on Earth to reach out and take it. For understanding must always come from within. We cannot bring it to you and force it into you as a food. We can only stimulate your seeking through suggestion, through teachings such as this one — so that you, through your own understanding, can once more find the light that is within all men throughout all this creation.

Tonight, he says, we will speak to you about understanding. We will speak to you about reality. They say upon your planet that it is difficult to understand the meaning of life. But it is not difficult, he says, if you avail yourself of this understanding through meditation.

This meaning will not come to you in words. You will not be able to explain it in sentences or paragraphs. But you will begin to understand it. You will begin to obtain an awareness of it. And when this awareness has reached its fullness, you will then be with your Creator. And the understanding will be as it is — and you then will once more act as Creator.

Meditation, he says, is actually the only real avenue to this understanding. For this understanding cannot be given by words. It can only be reached through knowing. And this knowing can only be reached through meditation.

Many upon your planet have been known as masters, he says. Each of them became aware of truth — aware of truth from the truth that was within them. Each perceived this awareness through the process of meditation.

If a person keeps his interest in things that are external, he says — if he continues to use the intellect for analysis of each daily activity, each confrontation as he moves through life — then he is working in a very, very shallow way, with a very shallow objective and a very shallow opportunity to understand.

It is necessary, he says, to avail himself of a truth that is not intellectual. A truth that cannot be explained in words. A truth that is only a feeling — a knowing. A truth that is.

A knowing that is. I keep turning that phrase over. Not a knowing about something. Not a knowing that can be written down or defended in argument. A knowing that is — the way a stone is, the way light is. It does not refer to anything else. It stands on its own.

All men in all places, he says, are drawn toward understanding the single truth that lies within them — the truth of the creation. For the truth of one thing is the truth of another. All things are one and the same, impossible to separate. They have all been created by the same Thought. They are all made of the same substance, and they are all related in the same way.

Become aware of this, he says, in such a way that it is the knowing within you that is not an intellectual knowing — but a knowing that transcends everything you could think or do. A knowing that is the love, the infinite wisdom of the Creator.

This is only available through meditation, he says. You cannot spell it out. You cannot set it down on paper. You cannot express it in words, for all of these fall very short. This understanding is infinite. It is total wisdom, total love.

It is within you, he says, when you learn to express it in every thought and every deed, in every move, in every breath. Regardless of what you do, regardless of what confronts you — when you are expressing this understanding, you are at one with the truth. At one, as you were meant to be, as a result of the original Thought.

Reach this understanding, he says. Reach it through meditation. In reaching it you will reach the only joy that there is — a joy so profound, so total, so far-reaching that you will not be able to express it. You will only experience it. And then you will know it.

This knowledge, he says, is what you seek. It is available quite easily. All that is necessary is that you reach out. Reach out by going within — going within to all there is. For this is the direction to the infinite. The infinite wisdom that is yours, and your Creator's.

They are very close, and you cannot see them. The understanding is within you, and you cannot spell it out. The joy is available, and you cannot express it. Everything real in this evening's teaching is something you cannot point at — only reach for, by going within. Thank you for listening.

title: The Entire Game
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the entire game.

The reason for this excursion, Hatonn says — this excursion from a much more delightful environment into one of severe limitation, the one in which you now find yourselves — is for the purpose of realization.

It is difficult, he admits, to understand why such an experience should be necessary to reach an awareness that seems like it should be reachable anywhere, at any time. It is within reach anywhere, he says. But it is very difficult to test the total understanding of this realization in any other experience. It is most easily tested in the one you are in.

This testing, each day, each moment, is automatic. It is simply your reaction to each experience. Each of you has had reactions you now see as foolish. If you want to reach your goal during this experience, he says, it is necessary to adjust your thinking so that your automatic reaction to any experience is always a reaction of love and understanding.

This was demonstrated by the master known as Jesus, he says. He set an example of reaction to experience. If there is doubt in anyone's mind as to how to react, it has already been set down. And these reactions were not the product of his analysis or intellect. They were automatic reactions, based on a realization he had accomplished within the same physical illusion you now experience.

This is the only reason for the illusion you now experience. If this is the only reason, he says, then once you are aware of it, you should spend your time learning to react to each experience with only an expression of love and understanding.

To do this is very simple. It is simply to express love and understanding, regardless of the experience that confronts you. All that confronts you is illusion — everything. This is very clear to us, he says. It is not always clear to you, because the illusion you are in is a very, very good illusion. A very satisfactory illusion. A very efficient illusion. It is accomplishing exactly what you wish it to accomplish. It is accomplishing a deception. It is putting before you continual tests of your ability to express our Creator's love.

And then he says it. This is what the entire game is about. And it is a game, my friends. Especially from our point of view.

You have chosen to be participants in a game, he says — a game within an illusion. An illusion bounded by a narrow layer upon the surface of a small planet, in an infinite amount of space.

Consciousness is evolving throughout all of creation, he says. In your particular place, you are experiencing personal evolution. If you can maintain at all times an awareness of reality — and therefore an awareness of the game you are in — you may do precisely what you set out to do: lift yourself a very great degree in spiritual understanding.

This is what we are all attempting to do, he says. This is our only objective. Anything else is simply part of a game. And there are many, many games in this creation, at many levels — each played with different sets of rules, but all with the same goal. The goal of understanding. The goal of arriving at the ability to express love that is the Creator's.

Then he turns his gaze on the world's great seriousness — the warfare and plans for warfare, the political ideas, the thousands of objectives totally involved with the game, having no objective outside it, no objective in reality. If the individual immersed in these activities has no realization of their real value — and their real value is nothing, simply nothing — then he is not making the use he should of his existence within this illusion.

Do not let the illusion that meets you with each dawning day be too much of an illusion, he says. Recognize it for what it really is. Recognize each day what your objective is, and you will make full use of the illusion.

Late in the evening his brother Oxal speaks, and adds one thought. To give love, Oxal says — to emit a vibration of understanding — is to form a consciousness which is not an illusion. And how is it possible to express love at all times? It is impossible, he says, if you are relating to the illusion — to the imperfect, foolish, sometimes ridiculous people you meet in daily life. Of course it is impossible. The illusion is designed so that it is possible to act correctly only with knowledge. It is only possible to express love when you begin to have an awareness of the Creator.

Each person may seem to be a human entity, Oxal says. Yet he is the Creator. Each natural object, each manufactured object, the very air around you has a consciousness which is the Creator. You yourself — the originating agency of this love you wish to express — you are the Creator.

A game, with rules, played on a narrow layer of a small planet. The objective is not to win. The objective is to remember, in the middle of the game, that you are playing — and to let every move you make be love. Thank you for listening.

title: The Gadfly
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the gadfly.

Hatonn does not come this evening to comfort anyone. He says so himself, in the first minute. I am here, my friends, that I may aid you. And yet I am here to sting you and to stimulate you, as a gadfly. I am not here to give you comfort, in that I do not wish to put you to sleep, but to awaken you.

The gadfly was the name the philosopher of Athens gave himself — the insect that stings the great horse of the city awake. Comfort puts you to sleep. He has come to do the opposite.

You, my friends of this group, are very close to your desire, he says. You are close to the opening. Going through this opening will unite you with your desire, and then the progress you make will be much accelerated.

But we must wake you, he says. We must help you become aware not only of the beauty, but of the freedom — and of the terrible responsibility of freedom.

The terrible responsibility of freedom. Sit with that phrase. Freedom is usually sold to us as the good part, the prize. Hatonn says it is also the weight. You are free, which means the shape of your life is your doing, and there is no one else to hand the responsibility to.

It is so easy, he says, to forget that you are free. Your intellectual minds insist that you accept all of the words and all of the conditions. They insist that you accept hot and cold. And then you accept right and wrong. And that you accept each and every description of your illusion. And yet this illusion is a cunning system of limitation. The limitation is designed to produce heightened awareness, strong emotion, and the resultant understanding. But if you believe too strongly in the illusion, you will react blindly to it — and you will not understand, and you will not find the freedom, and you will not find your desire. And this, he says, is your responsibility.

We speak of beauty to those who are beginning, he says, for truly all is beauty, all is joyful, all is full of love. All these things are true. But they are more than true — they are actual. And in that they are actual, there is no beauty, there is no joy. There is only one thing, and that is the Creator.

We cannot say to you, that is the Creator and that is reality, he says, for that is a word. We are speaking the very limitations that we wish to bring you past. Your desire is to come past these limitations, so that you may express the infinite and incandescent love and light that is within you and is the Creator.

There is peace beyond peace, he says, and there is understanding beyond all things. And these things must be found through the paradoxes of spiritual awareness — through the limitation of all that is a word.

The contact moves to another instrument, and the teaching turns to thought itself. Everything that occurs within the illusion you experience, Hatonn says, is caused by your thinking. The illusion is caused by the thinking of those within it. Everything that exists throughout the creation is created by thought. Everything you are experiencing is created by thought. Everything you will experience is created by thought.

Therefore, he says, there is only one thing of any importance: that is thought. And as far as you are concerned, the only thought you are able to control is that thought which you call your own. Therefore it is necessary to completely and totally understand your own thinking, prior to dealing with anything else.

And what will you create, once you understand it? There is only one thing you can provide, he says: an example. An example of thinking. If this is done by enough of the people upon your planet, your planet will achieve a state of thinking that is truly within the thought of our Creator.

The contact returns to the first instrument, and Hatonn speaks the evening's final teaching — the one the gadfly was stinging toward all along. Your limitation, he says — your illness, your lack, your need — all of these are due to only one thing. And that is your belief that you are limited. That there are lacks. That there are limitations. That there are illnesses.

What do you believe? You are very tempted, he says, to believe in limitations of all kinds. If you could believe the truth, you would have no lack, no limitation, no illness — nothing of any kind except the unity which is the truth.

My friends, you are perfect and you are fulfilled. Your only mission is understanding and service. Understanding brings its own service. Therefore your only mission need be understanding. The service follows of itself.

Do not believe in limitation, he says, and you will become unlimited.

That is the sting. Not a new technique, not a new cosmology. A question, pressed like a thumb into a bruise: what do you believe? And the suggestion that the bars of the cage were never locked — they were only believed in. The gadfly stings, the horse wakes, and the field was always open. Thank you for listening.

title: Reach for the Sun
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: reach for the sun.

Hatonn opens this evening with the first question. Not the first question of the night — the first question, underneath all the others. What are you seeking? Is this not the first question, my friend?

There are many questions under the general heading of spiritual enlightenment, he says. But in knowing the simple answer to this first one lies the open door to a great deal of further inspiration.

And then he tells a story. Not a parable with a moral nailed to the end — a picture, left standing in the mind.

Imagine, he says, the open skies, and beautiful puffy clouds, as they slowly gather and drift, blown by the wind across the green country. The sun shines warmly upon the country, and nature abounds in the warm sunlight. And the clouds grow heavy, and the waters gather, and they unburden themselves upon the thirsty ground. And the life-giving water enters all the plant life, and the plant life teems and grows and flourishes. And then the clouds pass, and the sun shines forth once more — and the countryside turns and reaches for the sun, in a never-ending cycle of growth and appreciation.

What questions, my friends, did the flowers ask? Do you think they asked why they are the color that they are? Do you think they questioned their shape, or asked how they may be useful?

Their beauty is a blessing, and their fruit of benefit. Plants give love and service without question, he says, for they know the one question. They know that they are reaching for the sun, and for the water which gave them their life.

And you, my friends — who gave you your life, and who nourished you, but the Creator? The one Creator, Creator of us all. And in him we all abide, he says — some of us knowingly, some of us not. The reality is independent of our awareness of it.

What is your question, he asks again. What are you seeking? I suggest to you that you are seeking the Creator. You are seeking, as you may say, the Thought that created you. This is a simple — a very simple idea. Perhaps too simple for the intellect to accept.

All he suggests, he says, is to disengage the intellect, and allow your moments of meditation to speak to you regarding your true desire. Once in possession of the knowledge of your true desire, that which you desire will come to you.

So much time within the physical illusion is wasted, he says — wasted, from our point of view — upon the pursuit of questions like: why am I this shape? Why is my situation so and so? These are questions which deal entirely with the illusion. Brief, phenomenal, and unimportant in the extreme. Questions which waste your time while your true desire must wait until you can give it attention.

I think of the flowers again. They did not ask why they were red instead of yellow. They did not hold meetings about whether their shape was useful. They reached. The reaching was the whole teaching.

It is written in your holy works, he says: seek, and you shall find. This is a true and extremely accurate statement. If you wish to open the door, and open the next door, and so on — you have only to knock.

The contact moves among the instruments, and the voices agree on one thing: in reality, all is very simple. In the physical illusion, things become extremely complex. We come to you, they say, with the purpose of jogging your desire.

Late in the evening Laitos speaks, and for the newer members he explains the conditioning wave — the blanket vibration of a spiritual nature which carries all communications through the instruments. It is something like the tuning of one of your electronic instruments, he says. For those who wish only to experience the spiritual vibration, it is useful. For those who wish to become channels, it does two things: it strengthens the spiritual vibration that will carry our thought, and it exercises the physical being of the instrument — so the instrument may be sure we are actually transmitting, and not a figment of imagination.

I will offer the conditioning wave to those who desire it, he says. If you will relax and avail yourself, we will make our presence felt.

The evening began with a question and ends with an image. The countryside, after the rain, turning its face to the sun. No questions asked. No answers demanded. Just the reaching — the never-ending cycle of growth and appreciation. Your true desire is not a puzzle to solve. It is a direction to face. Turn toward it, the way the field turns toward the light, and let the rest be weather. Thank you for listening.

title: The Eternal Present
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the eternal present.

The contact is difficult this evening. The instruments are restless, the connection cycles in and out of clarity. And yet — or perhaps because of this — Hatonn speaks one of the most practical teachings in this part of the archive. It is about illness, and it is about time, and it is about the instrument sitting in the room with an aching body while the words come through her.

That which is known upon your planet as illness, he says, is due to lack of understanding of the principle of living. And the principle is this: there is only one. One place, and one Being. The time is the present. The place is here. The Being is love.

The time is the present. The place is here. The Being is love. Three short sentences, and he says they equal what is known in your intellectual framework — which is to say, everything the mind has built its systems to describe, compressed into nine words.

It is in the misunderstanding of these truths, he says, that all lack comes forth — showing itself as physical discomfort, physical need, mental agony, emotional need. If you were able to live completely within the moment, and to realize the love which is all around you, and to sense the immediacy of your surroundings, you would no longer be other than truly perfect — within the illusion as well as outside of it.

And then he turns, with great tenderness, to the instrument herself. This instrument, he says, is having trouble receiving even these abstract thoughts, for she is maintaining a state of tension within her physical being — due to the fact that she is living in the future, and is awaiting the next time in which an uncomfortable feeling will come within her physical being.

And yet, he says, it is this tension that produces the future discomfort.

Read that again slowly. The tension produces the discomfort it is bracing for. She is living in the future, waiting for the pain — and the waiting is what summons it. How many of us do exactly this? We rehearse the bad appointment, the difficult conversation, the symptom's return. We live in the future to prepare for it, and the preparation becomes the event.

Without the tension, he says, perhaps a lingering misunderstanding of a more basic type — what you call karma — may yet manifest. But this can be made shorter and easier, and finally can be made to disappear, simply by the application of a higher truth than the law you call karma.

There is a higher truth, my friends. Each of you may consider that your discomforts, whatever they may be, may be alleviated and finally removed by the application of the higher law of love — and of understanding of the eternal present, and the eternal immediacy of the entire creation.

You are one being, he says. One perfect being. In reality, this is true. The realization of reality causes your illusion to correspond with that reality. Live in harmony, my friends, with reality.

Someone in the group has been asking about the New Age — the great turning everyone senses coming. Hatonn's answer is characteristically simple. It is a large subject, he says, and we could speak upon it at length. But if you understand what we have said about the truth of love, of oneness, of here and now — you may begin immediately to comprehend your New Age.

The New Age is not a date on a calendar. It is not an event that arrives while you wait for it. It is the present, entered fully. The place, inhabited completely. The Being, recognized as love. The future you are bracing for does not exist. The past you are carrying does not exist. There is only the eternal present, and the immediacy of everything in it.

The instrument could barely hold the contact, and the tape is short. But sometimes the shortest sessions carry the heaviest teaching. Put down the future you are tensing against. It is the tension, not the future, that hurts. Come back to here. Come back to now. Come back to love. That is the whole of it, and it has always been the whole of it. Thank you for listening.

title: The Valley of the Shadow
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the valley of the shadow.

Hatonn opens with a practice for hard times. Meditate, he says, upon the complete unity of yourself and all that you see. Do this not once, and not only in easy circumstances — but at all times, and especially in difficult circumstances.

Insofar as you love and feel at one with what is difficult for you, he says, those circumstances will be alleviated. Not by any law of your physical illusion, but by the law of love. For that body which is of spirit, which is interpenetrated with the physical body, is higher than your physical body. And the changes you make by love upon your spiritual body will, of necessity, reflect themselves within the physical illusion.

All is one, my friends. My voice is now the voice of this instrument. My thoughts are her thoughts. Please believe that the vibration we offer you is not a vibration of personality, but is a vibration of the Creator. We are also channels, he says. There is only one voice.

Even if the universe around you remains disharmonious and difficult, he says — if your mind is stayed upon the unity of the Creator, your own universe will become harmonious. And this is not by your doing, but by the simple love of the Creator.

Hatonn answers carefully. The physical reasons for what is coming are varied, he says, and your scientists will spend a great deal of time cataloging each condition. The vibration within the mind and heart of the peoples of your planet is determining, and will determine, the precise events. It is not permissible for us to tell you precisely what will occur, or when. Nor would we wish to.

But he will say this. The rain and the wind and the fire will destroy only those things which are in what you call the third density of vibration. Spend no time, he says, concerning yourself with maintaining your third-density existence after the change is complete. If, within your spirit, your graduation day has come, those things necessary for your emergence will be done for you.

It is extremely possible, he says, that damage will occur to those things you identify with yourself in the third density. If we may speak plainly: you will observe the valley of the shadow of death.

These very words, he says, we have spoken to you before. And yet you cling to that physical body and those physical surroundings, as though your spirit were permanently attached.

May we suggest to you, he says, that you can find your spirit neither in your head, nor in your hands, nor in your chest, nor in your legs, nor in your feet. That nowhere can you find your spirit. Nowhere can you operate to remove it, nor to aid it. Your spirit resides within a shell. The shell may be removed — but that is no matter. The spirit does not perish.

You will be undergoing a journey, he says, quite unlike any journey within third density. And those who graduate will thoroughly enjoy this journey.

If you can know in your heart that your spirit is not dependent upon the state of your body — if you can realize that the valley of death is but a shadow — then you may aid those about you in the days to come. If you have confidence in those days, he says, you will shine like a beacon, that you may carry many with you toward their graduation.

Another questioner asks about the old prophets — whether the Lord of the Old Testament was the Confederation. Hatonn's answer is worth hearing in full. When we refer to God as the Creator, he says, we tell you that he is all that exists. To look upon the face of the one next to you is to look upon the face of the Creator. Those who experienced those great moments met beings who radiated the beauty and love and knowledge of the Father — which they took to be held by the one called God.

We do not wish to be considered as gods, he says. We are but your equals. We are sorry that we have been misunderstood. And the knowledge we shared could have been much more helpful, if not improperly used and interpreted by your many religions.

You shall not find peace within a religion, he says. You do not need to support the spirit with money or goods. The religions upon your planet teach physical ideas, and when they approach the spiritual points, many of them brush them aside.

But to answer the question: we have been referred to in the Bible in many portions. And as the master Jesus attempted to tell the people of your planet — you are yourself a god. Within you lie the powers which were demonstrated by the one known as Jesus. He himself told those around him that they were capable of doing greater things than he.

The valley of the shadow is but a shadow. The shell may be removed, and that is no matter. What remains — what was always there, underneath the head and the hands and the chest — does not perish. It shines, like a beacon, for the others still walking through. Thank you for listening.

title: The Miraculous Ordinary
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the miraculous ordinary.

Hatonn begins this evening with a disclaimer, and it is one of the most honest openings in the archive. I will not try to prove to you, he says, that I am a being from another planet. I will not try to prove to you that these words you hear are my thoughts rather than the thoughts of this instrument.

Not proof. Stimulation. He chooses to communicate in what you might term odd ways, he says, and there is good reason for it. Most of the Confederation's work is done below the level of consciousness, presenting ideas that may be accepted or rejected. We hope, he says, in time to lead your people out of the darkness in which they dwell. This darkness is not necessary. Your peoples may join ours in the light of the infinite Father — as you would call that state of consciousness which is the oneness of the creation.

We are here to help you understand, he says. And your peoples need this understanding. In truth, this is all your peoples need — for in truth, this is all that there is. For when this understanding is acquired, all that there is is acquired. For all that there is is a state of mind.

Your thinking, my friends, is in truth all that there is. For without your thinking there is nothing. Your thinking governs all that you experience. And in this we are here to aid you: your thinking.

For many generations, he says, your peoples have been engrossed in a false world — a world of thought which was meaningless. They have acted from instinct, and evolved intellectual philosophies which are in truth meaningless, for you have no basis for understanding that can be termed intellectual. They have been unaware of that single source of understanding which would free them from the pain of the physical existence in which they find themselves.

We rely instead on a more satisfactory method: contacting your people directly, mentally. We can do this if they quiet the conscious mind and make themselves receptive. For those aware of our purpose, he suggests meditation. We will only offer suggestions, he says. We will only offer concepts. We will never impose our will upon your peoples — for this would break the very laws we are attempting to deliver.

You have but one thing that is not transient, he says. You have only your thinking to keep for all of eternity, as you call it.

Your thinking is all you have to develop, and it is all that is really yours. The physical body in which you now find yourself is not in truth yours — and is transient. All that you create, whether material or intellectual, is transient.

We are attempting to bring to your peoples an awareness of that which is not transient. That which will reawaken an awareness that in truth is all that there is.

And then the sentence that stops me every time. We cannot understand, he says, how your peoples can stand upon the surface of what you call a planet, and totally overlook the creation of the infinite One. For this, my friends, is all that there is. There is nothing but this creation — this infinite creation of the infinite Father. This creation is far more fantastic than any of the toys of your civilization.

Become aware of this first, he says. Use your time for meditation and contemplation of the true creation — that which is you, and that which surrounds you. Become aware of this, and you will begin to understand. Your peoples are not even aware of themselves. This awareness will grow as you avail yourself in meditation. And as it grows, you will more closely attune your thinking to that which was intended by the Creator. As your thinking becomes more attuned, you will begin to experience that which was intended.

He closes with the old words. Seek, and ye shall find. Knock, and the door shall be opened unto you. It is first necessary that you desire more than it is possible to experience in the physical. This seeking is necessary, he says. This seeking is the only real purpose for your existence in the physical.

Seek ye first the kingdom of heaven, and all else shall be added. But first it is necessary to seek. This is quite necessary.

The miracles that occur about you in your daily life are routine to your thinking, he says. But they are in truth miraculous.

Routine to your thinking, but in truth miraculous. The overlooked creation, under your feet and behind your eyes, performing its miracles on schedule while you study the toys. Become aware of the miracle of the creation about you — which is you. When you are able to do this, he says, then perhaps we will meet in a more tangible fashion. Thank you for listening.

title: One With You
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: one with you.

This is a short session. The tape cuts off early, and what survives is only a few minutes of Hatonn's voice. But the message is whole. Sometimes the shortest evenings carry the simplest teaching, and the simplest teaching is the one we most need to hear again.

We identify ourselves, he says, as the Confederation of Planets in Service to the Infinite Creator. Yet in truth, my friends, we are one with you, in spirit. For in spirit all things reside. And from one spirit comes the source for all experiences. And from one spirit shall all things become known.

It is the destiny — or the birthright, he says — for each individual to evolve in awareness, so that he may truly comprehend the origin of his being. And that origin is contained within the oneness of the entire creation: the knowledge that all things form, with the whole, an entire being — infinite in experience and knowledge.

Infinite in all things is this being, he says. Yet within you is it contained.

I want to stay with that sentence. Infinite in all things — yet within you it is contained. The whole of it. Not a piece, not a spark, not a share. The entire being, infinite in experience and knowledge, contained within you. The part that contains the whole. The drop that holds the ocean.

And to know this being, he says, it is only necessary to turn within yourself, and speak in silence to the one universal spirit known as the Creator.

Speak in silence. Not with words, not with arguments, not with the long lists of questions we bring to every teaching. Turn within, and speak in silence, to the one who is already there.

You truly contain this knowledge, he says, and it is yours to gain at your own choosing.

The contact moves to another instrument, and Hatonn greets the group once more — and then he says something that makes me smile, because it is so honest. This illusion in which you dwell, he says, does not seem to be as we describe it to you, does it? It does not seem to be within you.

And this, he says, is why we call it an illusion.

It does not seem to be within you. Of course it doesn't. It seems to be out there — solid, separate, happening to you. That seeming is the whole of the illusion. Underneath the seeming, it is within you. It always was.

The tape ends there. No closing, no farewell. Just the sentence hanging in the air: this is why we call it an illusion.

We are one with you, in spirit. The infinite being is contained within you. The knowledge is yours at your own choosing. Turn within, and speak in silence. That is the whole evening, and it is enough. Thank you for listening.

title: One Unit of Infinity
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: one unit of infinity.

In the winter of nineteen seventy-five, the voice that calls itself Hatonn tried to do something nearly impossible. He tried to explain what oneness means, in a language built for separations. And he starts, wonderfully, by admitting his own name is a kind of fiction. He only uses the name Hatonn, he says, because we need a handle to hold onto. In reality, the name belongs to a planet, and upon that planet the people have united in consciousness around a single desire. That desire is to know the Creator, and to be instruments of His love. That is why they have come, he says, and that is the only credential he offers.

Then he takes the word one apart. One, as you understand it, he says, means a unit without any extension. A single coin. A single dot. A thing fenced off from other things. But one as we understand it is a unit of infinity. And since infinity has no end and no beginning, what else could it be but one unit of infinite experience, which contains all things, all knowledge, all beings within the universe. I love that line. It turns the whole idea inside out. Oneness is not smallness. Oneness is everything, held at once.

And listen to where he puts it next. Not up in the sky. In you. Within yourself, he says, the true identity of the concept of one has been implanted by the Creator. Within each being on your planet and throughout the creation there is the concept of one, its knowledge and its understanding. Within you lie the answers to all problems. Within you lie the experiences of all other beings. Because once you are truly aware of the oneness of the entire universe, you cannot separate the experiences of your brothers from your own experience. The border comes down.

Self-identity, he says, the name and face you wear so tightly, is something you adopted for a short period of time while existing in the physical realm. You adopted it so that you may learn. And within this physical realm, the lesson you must learn is love. And love is one, and love is all. He knows this sounds contradictory. That is because you have taken these concepts, he says, and separated them within the physical illusion. Within the creation there are no separations.

Then he follows the thought one step further. Your thoughts, he says, as the thoughts of all other beings, are emanated truly from one source of intelligence. And that intelligence is the love of the Creator. And it is the Creator.

Which brings us to the sentence that has probably startled more listeners than any other in these early sessions. You are creators, as are all other beings. And all together, as we understand it, are the Creator. He hedges it at once, and the modesty is worth hearing. We do not know as a fact all realities or all truths, he says, yet as close as we have been able to understand it, this is the truth. That all beings unite, that they take away the separations which they have implanted within them, and unite to form the omnipotent being we call the Creator. We are but particles of His consciousness. Yet within each particle are His abilities.

And here the evening turns from philosophy into something you can use tomorrow morning. We must learn, he says, to focus our consciousness on His love, which is readily available to all. And we must learn to utilize properly the abilities which have been implanted within us. For within us is the ability to create, the infinite ability to create experience through all eternity. Do not take it lightly. As you go through your day, you have many thoughts. Many thoughts are kind and loving. Yet within your world you are constantly bombarded by negative experiences and thoughts. Your thoughts, negative and positive, are in reality creations of experience. Therefore, he says, you must learn to control and utilize properly your ability to create.

It is a quiet ending to a vast idea. One unit of infinity. You are inside it, and it is inside you. Your thoughts are not weather passing overhead. They are creations. And the love they come from was never far away, because it was never anywhere else.

Thank you for listening.

title: Child of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: child of love.

There is a small group in nineteen seventy-five, meeting in meditation, trying to dedicate themselves more deeply than before. And Hatonn meets them exactly where they are. He tells them he speaks to them at a time of dedication, a rededication, and then he sets aside the usual lessons and talks about the one thing standing in their way. Themselves. Their habit of keeping score against themselves.

He begins with an image I keep coming back to. He says the group has heard so many of his words that it must seem as though he appears to them as a tailor, measuring and cutting and detailing and analyzing, trying to tailor the spiritual path for them with tools, laying it all together in a measured way. In reality, he says, we are not tailors, and there is no measure. Our message is infinite, and there is no set pattern for progress. And that which we truly have to give you lies within the silence. The words are comforting, and he is glad to speak. But the real gift is not the talking.

Then he comes to the heart of it. He wants them to think about their own nature, and about what they call their sins, their errors, their mistakes. You who try, sometimes very hard, to be upon the spiritual path, he says, are often very hard upon yourselves because you have erred. You made a mistake. You manifested that which was not positive. And you say, why did I do that? I did not mean it. Why did I make this error? And you concentrate on the error. And this does not seem to prevent you from making the error the next time.

Here is his suggestion, and it is the whole evening in one sentence. Instead of concentrating upon your mistakes, ask yourself how much time you have spent this day investigating that portion of your unique person which is totally perfect. How much awareness have you had this day of the love and the light of the Creator you have within you? How aware have you been of your own innocence? When you concentrate upon your mistakes, he says, you dwell within the world of mistakes. And mistakes will occur again and again. But if your consciousness dwells in the realm where you know you are a creation of the Father, where you know you can manifest His love, then the opportunity to make a mistake will be that much farther from you.

Meditation, he says, is not upon your mistakes. It is not upon the past. It is upon the eternal present, and upon your innocence. You are a child of love.

He borrows from their holy works. It is written that you do not know when the spirit will come. He may come in the morning. Or in the evening. Or at midnight. And if your lamp is lit, all will be well. And if it is not lit, you will miss Him. To dwell in the awareness that you are watching for the One Who is All, he says, that is the source of the inspiration behind the kind of service you wish to give, the kind of life you wish to dedicate yourself to. You cannot analyze your own motives, or your acts, or other people's motives and acts. They will tangle you all up. Only dedicate yourself, not just now, but in all the nows, to the Father. Watch and wait, for you do not know when He will come.

He is honest about how hard this is. People have become each other's watchdog, he says, and those who refuse to concentrate on the negative are often considered unaware, or even stupid. Yet the will you create by your continued innocence of heart, he says, will be a light within this world, which is dark at this time.

And he closes with an image for the dark. It is as though the world were deep, deep asleep, he says, and a few of you are attempting to remain awake. For you, love may yet light up the sky. For those who sleep, it may be a long night. But other people's reality will remain real for them, and yours will remain real for you. It is truly written, he says, that to those who are innocent in heart, those things which are needed will come.

So the dedication he asks for is not to trying harder. It is to looking away from the mistake, and toward the part of you that was never broken. The child of love. It is still there. It never left.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Faraway Sun
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the faraway sun.
