So it began to plot how to grow its blossoms and its fruit, and to calculate just when its leaves should fall, and when each leaf should turn, to get the greatest amount of fruit. And it spent a great deal of time in attempting to fruit.

In time, the tree was widely noted, for no two pieces of its fruit were the same. But the tree was much less capable of caring for itself than the other trees, and this it could not understand, because it was, after all, a very, very intelligent tree, capable of complex and vast abstract thinking. In time, the tree withered and perished, while the other fruit trees in the orchard, who had never given a thought to who they were or how to become better, flourished as was their nature.

Now listen to how Latwii reads his own story. You must understand, he says, that each of you is just as the tree, rooted in what we are forced to call love. You are perfect, and instinctually you will turn toward the sun and bear fruit for the season. The tree's intelligence was its downfall, and it is ours too. The Creator gave each entity the power of co creator, which is free will, and with it you can make your world very complex. But do not, he warns, attempt to control the flow of love from the central sun of your existence. The more you calculate, the more opportunity there is for distortion.

I want to be careful with this, because he is not telling anyone to stop thinking. The mind, he says, is an excellent tool, well suited to serving. But you must be sure that you do not serve it. If you attempt to design and calculate your being, you will surely begin to falter. Each of you has your own path, and your own instinctual pattern of prayer and service, and to deviate from your instincts once you are on the path is to distort your perception of the truth.

He is equally blunt about the word your culture loves to use for those who stumble. There have been many who called entities a word that we dislike, he says. That word is sinners. We do not believe in the concept. What he has found instead are distortions of love, and the remedy is not condemnation but a different kind of faith. Not the faith of the holy books, he says, but faith in yourself, to follow your instincts, and to do what you feel is good and right.

And then, because he is Latwii, he lightens it at the end. Do not take yourself too seriously, he says, because you have a long time to grow. When you have failed, pick yourself up and be easy on yourself. And when you think you have done well, do not break your arm as you pat yourself on the back. Enjoy yourselves a great deal, he says, and laugh at your misfortunes and your fortunes alike, for they are all material for your learning, and you may find the Creator in each and every moment.

The unthinking trees flourished as was their nature. Perhaps we can too, if we stop calculating long enough to turn toward the sun.

Thank you for listening.

title: To Serve Is Freedom
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: to serve is freedom.

Oxal does not speak to this group often, and he opens by saying why he has come now. He is of the vibration of light, yet closely connected with the vibration of love, and he is drawn to them on these days when their planet is bathed in more light than at any other time of the year. It is the season of the longest day, and his whole discourse is about what light does. It serves.

To serve the Creator is perfect freedom, he says. That is the simple truth he has come to express, and he expresses it through the sun. The sun that rules your daytime, he says, offers its nearly infinite supply of light in service to all who dwell upon this planet. Without it your ability to survive would be negative, for you are creatures shaped to receive what the sun can give, its warmth, the life it brings to plants, the rain it draws from water. Yes, my friends, he says, even your nights are illuminated by the reflection of the light of the sun. There is a darkness in your density, that you may understand the light. Light may come into a dark world, and the world may not comprehend it, but still, it exists. And the light of which we speak, he says, is love.

I love how practical he makes it. For those who seek the truth, your role is the seeking of the light, for in the light is unity, and in the light is love. Seek within yourself that spark of the infinite love and light of the Creator, and then take the giant step: cease being observers of your own light, and speak, when asked, of those things in which you believe. Do not volunteer it, do not press it on anyone, for each student is ready in his own time. But when you are asked, be courageous. Plant the seed of thought where you may. It does not matter whether you think the seeds have borne fruit, for that is not within your provenance. It matters only that you have been true to the understanding you now possess.

When Latwii takes the questions, the evening turns philosophical, and the first question is a large one: what is the relationship between the mind, the brain, and the will? His answer is worth sitting with. The brain, he says, is a type of computer, with deep programs running survival, reproduction, social position, all the big items on the agenda of this density. The mind is something else entirely, a function of the spirit, an amalgam of the effects that a wealth of experiences in many incarnations have had upon the personality.

And standing between the mind and the brain is the will. If you do not use your will, an automatic program takes over, and the mind gets linked to the brain in a fashion predetermined by circumstance. But where the will is developed, the mind can impress its own programming over the basic programming of survival. As you sit here this evening, he tells them, you are exercising the faculty of will. When it is developed to perfection, the will of the individual becomes the will of the Creator, and you become a clear channel.

He is asked what level he comes from, and his answer is disarming. Level six, he says, though he cannot take it as seriously as some. Level six is not the level of understanding. It is the level of light. We do not any longer understand, he says. Rather, we are. We exist as light and dwell as light beings. The dimension of love is four, understanding is five, unity is six, and his teachers come from unity. And no, he adds, they do not know if there is an end to the progression. Their teachers do not know either.

On astrology, he gives the line I quote most from this session. There is truth in everything, he says, but truth with a capital T is found in nothing. The chart is a general geography, useful the way any map of the terrain is useful. But to use it predictively is to assume the universe is mechanical and predetermined, and this is patently false. Regardless of the road map, he says, you can always strike off cross country. With meditation and the application of the will, freedom from any confines, astrological or otherwise, is assured.

Serve like the sun, will like a free being, and read no map as a prison. The light is love, and it is already shining on you.

Thank you for listening.

title: As They Would Have You
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: as they would have you.

Oxal opens this evening with a word for the times the group feels coming, and for the part each of them is to play. Each of you, he says, has a program of action to carry out at this time, and he means it not only for the room but for everyone on their sorrowing planet. For a very few, there is the program of the shepherd.

Those who have made contact with that portion of their deeper self that lets them be a shepherd, guarding the sheep, will find it compelling now to take action, to establish themselves that they may survive and serve. The great majority, he says plainly, are the sheep, not yet consciously aware that they are programmed by their higher selves for service and learning, moving through the illusion easily herded by whatever forces surround them. When trouble comes near, those sheep with some hope of awakening will be your charges.

He is honest about the odds. Because of your free will, we do not know which of the many futures is yours, he says, but a very large percentage of them include what you would call catastrophe. Some you cannot help, and even trauma will not awaken those who sleep on while their lives pass before them. You must let these go, secure in the knowledge that each sphere has an infinite amount of time to discover the desire to know the Creator.

And then he revises the golden rule, and the revision is worth more than the original to me. Instead of following the golden rule, he says, listen to the requests of those about you, and do unto others as they would have you do unto them, not as you would have them do unto you. For what you need may not be what they need. Help comes in many shapes and sizes, and many people ask for help in ways you cannot comprehend. So listen first. Then serve.

One more instruction, and it is for the shepherds themselves. Be grounded in meditation, he says, spending time in a tabernacle, seated with the blessed one. Without that consciousness, most peaceful, you as a shepherd will grow very lean. Do not forget to minister to yourself, by meditation and awareness of the blessing of love.

Latwii, in the questions, is asked how one becomes a channel, how one learns to carry the message at all. His answer is two words, and they are not technical. Humility, and resolve. Humility is one of the greatest freedoms in the universe, he says, and relieves the fever of many problems. When you have learned to meditate, you will understand that you cannot speak, and therefore you are free to be a channel. And resolve: nurture that desire as you would a plant. Let it burn within you, not consuming you, but flowing freely like a river of love, that you may be the channel you wish to be.

He adds that the instrument through whom he speaks prays before each channeling the prayer of Saint Francis, which begins, Lord, make me an instrument of thy peace. And he says something that steadies me whenever the archive feels too strange to trust. The information is not to be learned, he says. It is already part of you, merely something of which you may become aware. It is possible to hear the message of love and light riding in your car, talking with friends, going to your place of worship, sitting in a redneck bar, or in a bathroom. Go beyond every teaching, he says, even his. Go further, go beyond the ways, to refine that which is unspeakable, unknowable, and ineffable, and that will be the heart of love.

Shepherd a few, listen before you serve, keep your own lamp lit, and do not mistake the map for the country. The country is love, and you already live in it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love Which Is in Light
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love which is in light.

Hatonn takes up a prayer everyone in the room learned as a child, the Lord's Prayer, and reads it back to them as something they never heard in it. It has been much misunderstood, he says, because it led people to believe there is an entity outside of themselves, bearing no resemblance or connection to themselves, to whom they pray. To the best of our understanding, he says, this is not so. What follows is his translation, line by line, and I will give it to you the way he gave it.

Our Father, which art in heaven. That is to say, love, which is in light. Hallowed be thy name. Holy be the name of creation, the word that means all that there is. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. The kingdom of love, the will of love, as it is in heaven, the kingdom of love.

Give us this day our daily bread. You must ask this, he says, as a symbol for all the needs and supplies of the illusion, for in the physical body you have many needs, food and drink and shelter. But love is the source of all supply.

Forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. May love prevail, both in the giving of forgiveness and the gracious acceptance of the forgiveness of others. This, he says, is perhaps the hardest of the phrases to live. For some it is difficult to forgive, but for most it is easier to forgive than to be forgiven, for you do not wish to understand that you are in need of love. So he asks them to forgive, and more than this, to accept their own failings, and to accept the forgiveness of themselves and others when they have failed to manifest perfection.

Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. You yourself planned the lessons you would learn in this lifetime, he reminds them, and each lesson requires a testing. You are not asking to avoid the lessons. You are asking the grace of love to enter into you and lead you into a wiser, higher self, that protects you from misunderstanding the test.

For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. And whose is thine, he asks? The kingdom is part of ourselves. That which you know as Christ consciousness is a spark that dwells within each of us. To center yourself upon the Christ within is to be perfectly poised for action in any direction, to have your burden lifted, that you may be light of heart, and merry, and full of love.

The same theme carries into his second discourse, on identity. Your true identity, he says, resides in every cell of your being and every part of the universe, and at its core it is ever expanding love. Seek to know more and more fully that central source of yourself which is love, he says, and watch how it is manifested in your daily interaction with your brothers and sisters, with all creatures, with all creation. Look into your own eyes, he says, and you will see him, for in all of us he dwells, the father of love, the mother of light.

When Latwii takes the questions, the talk turns to healing, and he is careful and tender. The Confederation cannot diagnose the body, he says. The healing is caused totally by the patient, with the healer acting as a spiritual friend who, in dialogue, stimulates the patient in the art of realization of the self. Each patient expects the healer to be wiser or better, and this is not so, for we are all children along the same path. When the patient begins to understand the vulnerability of the healer, begins to feel the friendship of two pilgrims on the path, he can begin to forgive, and the self healing starts with the soul and only ends with the body.

Asked about angels, Latwii says it is basically very simple. There are those who graduated from this density, learned the ways of service and love, and chose to stay with the planet. They are totally oriented toward service, and available to those who seek them, as teachers, as guides, as healers. If you ask to see them, he says, their faces will come to you in meditation, and you will be aware of their kindly selves.

And on the question of relationships, whether it is better to learn alone or mated, he refuses the simple answer and gives a better one. Love and wisdom are the two poles, he says. Some cannot learn alone and must study the ways of love. Some must dwell alone and study the ways of wisdom. In a mated relationship you may find the most powerful means of balancing your own nature, so that love and wisdom become balanced, for truly it is only then that you can become what you would call a master. But in most cases, one person does not become a master, but two, helping each other.

He closes the evening with a sentence I want to leave ringing. I ask you all also to be foolish, he says: to love without reason, to be happy without cause, and to give without receiving. Feel free, my children, for you are all one with the infinite source of love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Looney Tune
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the looney tune.

Hatonn opens by telling the group where he is: looking down on their sphere from about eight miles up, watching it turn in shadow. Within those shadows, he says, many are sleeping, many are distracting themselves, some are contemplating the weighty problems of their possessions, and a few, like you, seek to know the truth. It is a gentle, almost wistful image, and everything he says tonight follows from it.

He hopes he can tell them enough that they can find the key to the door on the other side of which lies the truth. But you have the key already, he says. You have largely lost the ability and the will to use it. So much of what you think and do is in vain, pertaining only to a daily life that is transient. What of your wisdom have you not found turned to folly? Of how many of your possessions have you not grown tired? How many of your words remain shining, and how many have become tarnished or forgotten? How many lives have you touched today, my friends?

The way to the key, he says, lies beyond the illusion, and it will seem to be the only thing you do that is not real. That thing is meditation. In meditation, day by day, month by month, year by year, you develop within yourself a connection to infinite supplies of patience, goodwill, kindness, and the many other fruits of love.

And then he says the thing this episode is named for. Look at your life, my friends. You are looking at a looney tune. It is not your fault, that is your vibration. Put the captions under the comics, smile to yourself, and proceed. For there is more. There is something behind the cartoon. There is a reality which is unnameable, unknowable, ineffable, and unspeakable. However, he says, it can be experienced and shared. And this, he says, is where we go far beyond the wisdom of your peoples, for many of them honestly cannot conceive of a reality greater than the vanity and the folly which they now enjoy.

He assures them there is a reality, and then another, and then another, each one clearer than the last, each one truer to the original thought of love. As the mind and heart grow accustomed to the silence, you begin to ascend into these higher realities, until you can see the folly of this particular vibration without being disturbed by it. You will not be disturbed, because you will see it as an opportunity to witness, by the love that you show forth, the name of the Creator which you carry in your eyes and in your hands.

When Latwii takes the questions, someone asks about the suffering in the world, whether so many had to choose it. That is correct, Latwii says. Many choose situations of suffering for the learning, not in this illusion which is passing, but in a higher understanding. During incarnation the deeper self blankets itself, as a man in a shroud, hiding in the shadows, so the person does not remember why they desired the lessons they are now attempting to learn. There is no situation, no matter how ghastly to the senses, that is not rich in possibility to the immortal soul. Suffering is but for the moment, and is full of purpose. And of the teacher known as Jesus, he says this: he could not take the suffering away. He could share it. And one look at those sad eyes would help many to understand why those who knew this teacher were so devoted to him.

Asked about channeling itself, how the contact works, Latwii reaches for the simplest image in the archive. When you channel, you speak, he says. When a ball is thrown, you catch. You do not think about where to place your hand and where to move your feet, for by that time the ball will be upon the grass. When we send you a concept, it is sent, and you catch, and then you throw. You speak, and your hand is free, your mind is empty, and again you catch, and again you throw.

And when someone asks whether Latwii is the Comforter of which Jesus spoke, the answer comes back without hesitation. I am a voice which you may call Comforter, he says. We are messengers of that spirit, and we are sent to comfort you, as are a host of others. We live and breathe and are completely sustained by this spirit. We know no life but joy.

Behind the cartoon, the reality. Behind the noise, the silence. Put the captions under the comics, smile, and proceed.

Thank you for listening.

title: Triumphantly Foolish
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: triumphantly foolish.

This session arrives at a rough moment for the group. They have been traveling, they are tired, and their eating has been bad, and they want Latwii to tell them about diet. He obliges, and then, as he so often does, he gently pulls the rug out from under the question.

What you take in, he says, is of no importance at all. That is only energy for your body, which has an enormous range of acceptability. What is important is how the taking in is perceived by you. If you think of your food as poison, it will be poison. If you think of it as wholesome, it will be wholesome. He does not mean you should live on sweets, but he wants them to understand the proportion. Your bodies are the result of two factors, he says: the basic genetic type, and the image that you have of yourself, which produces a chemical system within your body.

But the real target of the evening is not food. It is wisdom itself, or rather the appearance of it. You have a desire to avoid the appearance of foolishness, he says. This is the downfall of your entire society. You attempt at all times to show yourselves as wise, and this takes a great deal of time and effort, making you feel less inclined to do things which are seen as simple and foolish. And foolish and simple, my friends, may be the best thing you can become.

So he gives them a program, and it is deliberately the opposite of self improvement. Let yourselves become as simple as you may. Become as servants to others, as well as fools. Avoid the appearance of wisdom. Seek the simple life. Avoid the opinion that leads you to believe that any one particular course of action or thought is the right one. For only a fool will believe that he does not have the answer, and the one who does not have the answer is, in most cases, closest to the truth.

The first step, he says, is to simplify your life. Then, in your simple state, you will be able to become fools, and when you have become foolish, you will be what he calls triumphantly foolish. That is to say, he says, you will have realized that you have no great truth which the rest of the universe does not have, and you will at last be able to admit that you do not know the answer to the great questions of life. He says that word triumphantly without apology, and I think he means it as the highest compliment.

The questions turn personal. Someone asks about the purpose of illness, and Latwii answers with unusual care. All things in this illusion come about through the application of the mind in an unconscious manner upon the creation of a reality which we would call distortions, he says. What the entity needs most of all is the love of her fellow beings, the sharing of feelings, that the being may understand that being ill does not make one separated from one's fellows. The purpose of any illness, he says, is the entity's attempt to remove certain distortions from her being, and the way through is to seek to know more completely the nature of the self.

Someone asks whether to take the healing energies being offered by others, and he says yes. You have but to ask, and these energies will be showered upon you. But let me also remind you, he adds, that this is a time for looking within, to develop the true desire to live. If you seek it, your search will be answered. And if you would ask your friends to join you in prayer, that too may help.

He is asked about balance, and gives a short, practical answer I keep in my pocket. In the seeking, he says, the first step is opinion, the second step is experience, and where these two are balanced, one becomes more complete. The experience without the opinion is a meaningless act. The opinion without the experience is useless knowledge. Combine the two, and you grow.

And he closes by telling them, tenderly, not to judge themselves for the tired bodies and the bad meals. This is a normal situation, and you are only experiencing a normal distortion, he says. You will find that in a day or so, you will be back to your old selves, and your bodies will have made the necessary adjustment.

Avoid the appearance of wisdom. Simplify. Become a fool, triumphantly. It may be the wisest thing in the archive.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Hunter and the Prey
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the hunter and the prey.

Hatonn speaks through nearly the whole of this session, and he arrives with one extended image that he builds with the patience of a teacher who knows he is saying the most important thing he will say all evening. He asks them to imagine a hunter.

A hunter is aware of the nature of the prey, Hatonn says, and also knows its weaknesses. He remains in a constant state of readiness, knowing that at any moment the desired prey may show itself, or present a situation where it can be captured. He keeps his weapons in readiness at all times. The prey is not aware of the hunter. The prey is not prepared, and has no weapons, and no state of readiness.

Now, he says, you must become the hunter. The prey is love, the prey is the Creator, the prey is the original thought, the prey is that which is yourself. The prey will show itself in the most unexpected places, and he wants them ready. For to hunt effectively, you must be prepared at all times, and the weapons that you use in the hunt must be honed.

The weapons, it turns out, are inward. Your weapons are your knowledge of yourself, your understanding of your own nature, your ability to accept that knowledge, and your ability to transform it into wisdom. Meditation, he says, is the tool that may be used to accomplish the honing of your weapons. And meditation takes many forms. It may be used as a cleansing, a purging of the energies that have been used in the daily activities, giving you an opportunity to see the day's thoughts and desires in a new light. But we suggest most of all the meditative state where you simply allow yourself to drift, and to be at the disposal of those things which you may seek.

He has a companion instruction for the hunt, and it is about how the hunter listens. When you hear the message, he says, you must hear it with both the brain, the logical mind, and the heart. You must feel a vibration which tells you this is the message of the Creator, a feeling that does not come with the rational mind. To hear with the heart, he says, one must be open, one must be willing to accept, and one must be willing to act. For there are many messengers who come to you, each with a different face. Some speak to the rational mind, and some speak to the heart. The Creator's messages come in many forms, and you must be able to distinguish the true message, not only with your mind, but also with your heart.

When the questions begin, someone asks about the nature of the self and the illusion, and Hatonn answers plainly. The self, he says, is the only thing that there is. It is all that there is, for all there is exists within the confines of the self. When you leave this illusion, you will find that the physical body is not at all necessary. You may choose to manifest one, but you will not need it. This is the way that we do our thinking. We do not have a brain, as such. We have an energy field. This, my friends, is the reality of your existence. You are love. You are the Creator.

Asked about the future, he speaks of changes coming to the planet, of a world that must go through a cleansing, and of a new root race that will emerge into a fourth density. And he draws a parallel he clearly intends as comfort. This planet and its people, he says, are going through what each of you as an individual is going through. Look at your own life, at the changes in your own consciousness, and understand that the changes within the planet are merely reflecting the changes within the people.

Become the hunter. Keep your weapons ready. The prey is yourself, and it is hiding in the most unexpected places.

Thank you for listening.

title: What Is Real
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: what is real.

Hatonn opens this session by drawing a line through the middle of everything the group takes for granted. Much of that which you see about you, he says, has no lasting substance. You walk through each day pursuing that which you desire, only to find that that which you sought yesterday is not that which you seek today. Why is this so? Because that which you pursue has no lasting substance, and it remains real only as long as your desire for it lasts. Your real substance, he says, lies elsewhere.

Your true self has nothing to do with the illusory life which surrounds you, he tells them. Your true self is a seeker of love, and love is the only reality. So he asks them, the way a good teacher asks, to go within, and discover the center of the self, which is love. Once you have discovered the true self, he says, then you can look at the illusory life about you and see the Creator in each aspect, and you can learn to love the Creator in all forms of the illusion.

He does not promise this will be comfortable. There will be times when your faith is tested, when you face discord and strife, when the reality of love may be the farthest thing from your mind. When this occurs, he says, remember to call upon the light of love that you have discovered within yourself, to see the reality in every situation, to see love in all things. Even in a difficult experience, there is something to be learned, and that something will always, he says, be of love.

And then he names the great temptation of the spiritual life, and it is not greed or anger. It is doubt. Many seekers of truth will face doubt, he says, and this is one of the most difficult tests. You may question whether all that you know in your heart is actually the truth. We can only advise you, he says, to go within yourself and again seek the love you have found. For only in seeking the love of the Creator can you find faith in the Creator, and by finding faith, you can dispel doubt. Do not be dismayed by the tests that you must face. They are, as you might say, all in the mind. Look upon them as opportunities to grow, for that is what they are.

His second discourse, on the spirit, is a single calm paragraph about silence. It is in the silence, he says, that one can discover the spirit. And it is not always necessary to go off into the forest to find it. One can discover the spirit in the silence within one's own heart, and in the silence between the notes of the music of life.

When Latwii takes the questions, the talk turns to the difference between this group and so many others seeking truth. You are a group which has learned to meditate together, he says, and to use the techniques that we have given you, and to know when to open yourself as a channel and when to close yourself. There are many groups of lightworkers on your planet, and we are not trying to disparage them when we say that many do not know when to channel and when not to channel, and are not in the habit of meditating on a regular basis. To do these things together, as a group, he says, is to provide a vibration of desire to know the truth, and that vibration is, to us, most valuable.

Asked about the soul's journey after death, Latwii keeps it short and sweet. When you die, he says, you retain everything that you have learned, all of the love that you have shared, all of the experiences that you have known. And this learning is brought back into a new incarnation, to be used as a foundation for new growth. You retain everything except the memory of it, and even that, he adds, is available through meditation and dreams.

The closing image belongs to Hatonn, and to the one called Nona, who speaks only a few words all evening. Go forth in the creation and seek the truth, Hatonn says. Seek the love of the Creator in all things, and then share this love with your fellow man. And Nona answers, in a voice the transcript barely catches: in love and light, we leave you. Go forth in peace.

The rest has no lasting substance. Love does. That is the whole of it.

Thank you for listening.

title: When You Meet Another
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: when you meet another.

This is a session about a single encounter, the oldest one there is: you, meeting someone else. Hatonn begins with the simplest statement in the archive, and then spends the whole evening unfolding it. All is one, he says. You are one with all things, all peoples, all of creation. All things were created in love, and all things live within love. So when you look upon another, you look upon yourself, for he is yourself.

This is the message of which we speak, Hatonn says, the message of which we sing. And he asks them to carry it past the intellect, because intellectual knowing is not enough. You can tell yourself that all is one, but do you really feel it when you meet another person? The intellectual concept of unity, he says, is only the beginning. The true knowing of the unity of all things comes about through the desire to seek the Creator, and to know the love of the Creator, and by expressing this love to those about you.

He gives them the practice in one sentence, and it is so plain it almost hides. When you meet another, he says, know that he is yourself, and greet him as yourself. Look into his eyes, and know that you are looking into your own eyes. Reach out to him, and know that you are reaching out to yourself. And when you have done this, know that in doing so you are reaching out to the Creator, for the Creator is within all. It is in your power, he says, to live each moment in the consciousness of the unity of all things, and thereby to serve those about you by your very presence.

Meditation is the doorway, as always. In meditation you may discover your true self, he says, and in discovering your true self you will know all other selves. The intellectual knowing will become a true knowing, and the true knowing will become a part of your being.

When the questions begin, someone asks about healing, and Hatonn is asked, point blank, whether a man can heal himself. His answer is yes, and his method is not complicated. When you are ill, he says, seek within yourself the cause of your illness. Meditate upon it. Go within yourself and seek the love of the Creator. And in seeking the love of the Creator, you will find that which is of love, and that which is not of love, and you will know what it is within yourself that has caused your illness.

The last question of the evening is the strangest, and Hatonn answers it with an image I cannot shake. A wheel, he says. A grinding wheel, worn from grinding corn. And a man caught in it. It is grinding upon a soul that has been wounded, and the wheel must be stopped. The transcript does not explain it, and Hatonn does not soften it. Some wheels, you understand, are not yours to keep turning. Stop the grinding. Tend the wounded one. That is all the unity there is, made practical.

Greet the other as yourself. Look into his eyes as your own. The wheel stops when you do.

Thank you for listening.

title: Water the Seed
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: water the seed.

Hatonn tells a story tonight, and it is one of the loveliest in this whole stretch of the archive. It is about a little girl, and what she learned from the sky.

There was once a little girl who was confused and lonely, Hatonn says, and she did not know where to turn. She did not have many friends, and she felt lost, and she began to ask herself the great questions, and to wonder what life was about. One day she looked up at the sky, and she saw that it was autumn, and the leaves were falling, and the wind was blowing, and she realized that the sky was speaking to her. The wind told her that it would always be there, and that it would always bring change. The trees told her that they would always grow, and that they would always reach for the light. And the little girl understood, Hatonn says, that she was not alone, that she was part of something greater than herself, and that she had a purpose.

He does not leave it as a children's story. Nature serves, he says, and it serves simply, without asking for anything in return. The wind does not ask why it blows. The trees do not ask why they grow. They serve the Creator by being what they are. And you, my friends, are like the wind and the trees. You are here to serve, and to serve simply, by being what you are.

Then he turns the story into the image this episode is named for. Within each of you, he says, there is a seed. And that seed is love. It is the seed of the Creator, planted within you, and it is your purpose to nurture that seed, to water it, and to help it grow. Each time you reach out to another in love, he says, you water the seed. Each time you turn away, you allow it to wither. The choice, moment by moment, is yours.

When the questions begin, someone asks the question every seeker asks eventually: how do I know if I am on the right path? Hatonn's answer is disarmingly simple. You will know, he says, by the fruits of your actions. If your actions bring love and light to those about you, then you are on the right path. If they bring darkness and confusion, then you have strayed. It is as simple as that, he says, and as difficult as that.

Asked about the nature of time, he gives one of the archive's cleanest answers. Time, he says, is an illusion, a construct of your minds to help you understand the sequence of events. In reality, there is no time. There is only the eternal now. All that has ever happened, and all that will ever happen, is happening now, in this moment.

And someone asks about fear, and he answers the way he always answers about fear. Fear is the absence of love, he says. When you feel fear, it is because you have forgotten the love that is within you. Go within, he says, and seek the love of the Creator, and the fear will dissolve, for love and fear cannot exist in the same place.

The little girl looked up, and the sky spoke, and she understood she was part of something greater. The seed is in you. Water it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Christ Within
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the christ within.

This is a session about importance, and about how badly we judge it. Hatonn opens with a test you can apply to anything in your life, and it takes about ten seconds. Ask yourself, he says: will this matter in the next life? If the answer is no, then it is not important. If the answer is yes, then it is important. That is the whole test. Most of what fills your days will fail it.

What will pass the test, he says, is the love you give, the service you render, the understanding you gain. These are the things that you carry with you. Everything else, the possessions, the status, the achievements that the world applauds, these are left behind. They are part of the illusion, and they do not follow you.

Then he turns to the figure at the center of the group's tradition, and he does something I did not expect. He does not ask them to worship Christ. He asks them to demonstrate him. Do not preach about love, he says. Demonstrate love. Do not talk about service. Serve. The world does not need more words about the Christ, he says. It needs more examples of the Christ consciousness in action.

And then he gives them the exercise at the heart of this session, and it is startling in its directness. He asks each of them, in meditation, to say to themselves the words: I am the Christ. Not as blasphemy, and not as pride. As identification. For the Christ consciousness, he says, is not something that belonged to one man two thousand years ago. It is a state of consciousness available to all, the consciousness of perfect love, of perfect service, of perfect unity with the Creator. When you say I am the Christ, you are affirming your true identity, the spark of the Creator within you.

He is careful, as he always is, about the ego's favorite trick, which is to turn even this into superiority. The moment you believe you are better than another because of your understanding, he says, you have lost it. The Christ consciousness is not about being above others. It is about being one with others, and serving others, humbly, quietly, without fanfare.

When the questions begin, someone asks how to deal with those who ridicule the path, and Hatonn's answer is pure non resistance. Do not argue, he says. Do not defend. Simply live your truth, and let your life be the argument. Those who are ready will see. Those who are not ready will not see, no matter what you say. Your energy is better spent in love than in debate.

Asked about the purpose of suffering, he returns to the hunter's patience of the earlier sessions. Suffering, he says, is a teacher, and like all teachers in this illusion, it is temporary. It comes to show you where you are not yet free, where you still cling, where love has not yet fully entered. Bless the teacher, learn the lesson, and let it go.

Will it matter in the next life? That is the test. And the exercise is the answer: say it quietly, and then go demonstrate it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Lost Dog
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the lost dog.

Oxal tells a story tonight, and it is a short one, and it does its work the way the best stories do, by leaving you nowhere to hide. It is about a dog.

There was once a dog that was lost, Oxal says. It did not know where its master was. But it knew that it had a master, and it knew that it loved its master, and it knew that its master loved it. So the dog began to walk. It walked through the cold, and through the rain, and its paws bled on the stones. But it did not stop, for it knew that somewhere ahead was its master. And the dog did not doubt its desire. It did not question whether the master was real. It simply walked, in love, toward love.

Listen to how Oxal reads it. You, my friends, are like the lost dog. You do not know where you are going. You do not know what the path holds. But you know that you have a master, and that master is love itself. You know that you are loved, and you know that you love. So walk. Walk through the cold and the rain of your illusion. Let your feet bleed if they must. But do not stop, and do not doubt your desire.

He is not romantic about the path. The path itself, he says, does not matter nearly as much as the remembering. It does not matter which road you take, which teaching you follow, which practice you keep. What matters is that you remember what you are seeking, and that you keep walking toward it. The dog did not have a map. It had a master. That was enough.

When Hatonn speaks earlier in the evening, he gives the group the same teaching in a different key, and it is about the present moment. You spend so much of your time, he says, either regretting the past or fearing the future, that you miss the only moment in which you can act, which is now. The past is gone. The future is not yet. All you have is this moment, and in this moment you can choose love. In this moment you can serve. In this moment you can be the light.

He asks them to consider how much of their suffering comes not from what is happening, but from their resistance to what is happening. Accept the moment, he says. Accept it completely, and then act within it from love. This is the whole of the teaching, and it fits in a single breath.

When the questions turn to the subject of guidance, how to know if one is being guided aright, Hatonn gives an answer I keep close. You will know, he says, by the feeling within your heart. If it feels like love, if it brings peace, if it draws you closer to your brothers and sisters, then it is guidance. If it brings fear, if it separates you, if it makes you feel superior, then it is not guidance. It is that simple, he says, and that difficult.

The dog walked on bleeding paws and never doubted its desire. Somewhere ahead is the master, and the master is love itself. Keep walking.

Thank you for listening.

title: Messengers Are One
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: messengers are one.

Hatonn begins this session by clearing up a confusion that must have been in the air of the whole channeling world, because it is still in the air today. People hear different voices, different names, different personalities coming through different instruments, and they ask: which one is right? Are they contradicting each other? Hatonn's answer is calm and total. All messengers of love and light are one, he says.

The differences you perceive, he explains, do not come from disagreement among the messengers. They come from the relationship between the messenger and the instrument. Each instrument is a unique being, with a unique mind, a unique vocabulary, a unique set of distortions. The message must pass through all of that to reach you. So the same love, spoken through different instruments, will sound different. It is still the same love.

He asks them, then, not to get caught up in names and personalities, in which entity said what through whom. These are the trappings of the illusion, he says. What matters is the message, and the message is always the same: you are loved, you are one, seek the Creator within. If a message brings love, if it brings unity, if it encourages you to seek within, then it is of the light, no matter what name is attached to it.

He is equally clear about something the archive returns to again and again, and I want to give it exactly as he gives it. We do not come to you uninvited, he says. We speak only to those who seek us, only to those who ask. This is the law of free will, and we honor it completely. If you do not ask, we do not speak. If you ask, we answer. It is as simple as that, and as absolute as that.

When the questions begin, someone asks about the many predictions and warnings that circulate among seekers, the dates and the disasters, and Hatonn's answer is worth hearing carefully. We do not deal in predictions, he says, for the future is not fixed. It is shaped moment by moment by the choices of free beings. Anyone who claims to know exactly what will happen, and when, is speaking from the illusion, not from the light. What we can tell you is the direction of the energies, the general movement, but the specifics are yours to create.

Asked about the difference between his own social memory complex and others, he brushes the curiosity aside with characteristic humility. These distinctions, he says, are of the illusion. In reality, there is no separation between us. We are all one being, expressing itself in different ways for the purpose of service. The names, the densities, the complexes, these are concepts we use because you need concepts. But do not mistake the concept for the reality.

And someone asks, simply, what he most wants them to remember. His answer is one sentence. Remember that you are loved, he says, beyond all measure, beyond all understanding, and that this love is the only thing that is real.

Different voices, different instruments, one message. The messengers are one, because the love is one. Remember that you are loved.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seeking Is All
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seeking is all.

This is the last session in our batch, and Hatonn uses it to say the thing that, in a way, makes all the other sessions unnecessary. He says it plainly, near the beginning, and then spends the evening proving it. It is not the information that matters, he says. It is the seeking.

You come to these sessions seeking answers, he tells the group, and we give you concepts, and ideas, and images. But the concepts are not the point. The point is that you are seeking. For it is the seeking itself that opens the heart, that turns the mind inward, that begins the great journey from the outer world to the inner. A person who seeks with all their heart will find the truth, he says, even if they never hear a single channeled word. And a person who does not seek will not find it, no matter how many words are spoken.

He warns them, then, about the temptation that follows every teaching, including this one. Do not take what we say and build a religion out of it, he says. Do not take our concepts and freeze them into dogma. Truth is not a set of propositions. It is a living thing, and it changes as you change, as your awareness grows. What is true for you today may be a stepping stone to a deeper truth tomorrow. Hold everything lightly, he says, even this.

And he speaks directly to the impulse to share, to teach, to wake others up. Do not force-feed, he says. You cannot make another seek. You can only love them, and live your own seeking so visibly that they become curious. Each person has their own catalyst, their own lessons, their own timing. What awakens one will leave another untouched. Respect the path of each, he says, even when you cannot understand it.

When the questions begin, someone asks about the purpose of the difficult experiences, the catalyst that seems so cruel, and Hatonn answers with the long view. Catalyst is the gift of the illusion, he says. Without it, there would be no growth, no movement, no seeking. The comfortable entity does not seek. It is the one who is challenged, who is stretched, who is brought to the edge of what they can bear, who begins to ask the great questions. Bless your catalyst, he says. It is the engine of your evolution.

Asked about the difference between those who seek alone and those who seek together, he honors both. The solitary seeker goes deep, he says, and finds the stillness within. Those who seek together find the mirror of each other, and learn love through relationship. Both paths lead to the same place, for there is only one place to go, and that is inward, toward the self, toward the Creator within the self.

And at the very end, he brings it back to the beginning, to the one thing he wanted them to carry out of the room. Seek, he says. Seek with all your heart. Seek in meditation, seek in your daily life, seek in your relationships, seek in your suffering and in your joy. The seeking is all. Everything else is commentary.

Twenty sessions, one teaching, and here it is at the last: it was never the information. It was the seeking. Keep seeking.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Living Fountain
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the living fountain.

There is an image that runs through this morning session like a current of clear water. Hatonn asks the circle to picture a fountain, the living fountain of the infinite Creator, crystal pure at its heart. We were plucked, he says, from that true fountain into a smaller one, a shadow of the water, a water that is half Creator and half made by man. You know it is not the true living water. And yet, within yourself, your own stream runs clear.

The invitation is not to fix the outer water. It is to cleanse yourself from the inside to the out. Cleanse the thoughts, purify the emotions, and then let your actions be a delight to you and a service to the Creator. The order matters. The stream starts inside and works outward. Nothing else can be made clean first.

Then the teaching turns practical, and this is the part I want to slow down for. As you journey through what you call time and space, Hatonn says, you will have many experiences, and these experiences mold what you call your personalities. That is ordinary. What is not ordinary is remembering to aid them in the molding. The path of the master is to take each experience, regardless of how trivial, and deliberately let it shape you into what you wish to become. If you can remind yourself of this simple process each time you speak or act or think, your progress will be sure.

He repeats the point, because it is so difficult to remember all the time. Apply the same test to every thought you have. Ask whether it is the thought of a master. If it is not, correct it. Do the same with each action and each word you speak. Do not underestimate the consequence of thought, he says. This is the quiet engine of everything else, the small lever that moves the whole weight of a life.

Self-analysis, then, is not punishment. It is education. Hatonn calls it a continuing and all-important step in your self-education, and then adds something striking. We are at the same position, he says, in the evolution of our thought. The hierarchy dissolves for a moment. It is not a teacher lecturing down. It is fellow students comparing notes on the same road.

The session returns to the idea of investment. The investments most people make in this world, Hatonn says, will not pay great dividends. The one investment that will is the effort of mastering your own being, the journey inward. Every person you meet is as sacred and divine as the original Thought from which each springs, and the world keeps providing reasons to remember it. Meeting them rightly is the return on the investment.

Near the end comes a lovely exchange. Carla asks about two hawks the group saw that morning, and whether they meant anything. Hatonn answers that they were emissaries of the divine Being, sent to wish the group well in their new home and to bless the work they would do there. The mating of the hawks, he says, was the blending of the old with the new, and its offspring is their work itself. And no, they were not machines. They were biological creatures, in service to the divine Creator.

I love how the image lands. A fountain, a stream, two birds circling a new beginning. The teaching underneath it all fits into a single line. Aid the experiences in molding you into what you wish to be. Everything else is commentary.

Thank you for listening.

title: Another Candle Lit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: another candle lit.

This evening session opens with something rare in the archive: plain, unsoftened honesty about suffering. Hatonn says, plainly, that they are not blind. They know that young children lie in the streets of some cities, their bellies swollen, flies about their closing eyes. They know the injustice of the wasteful one who takes what he cannot use and does not give it away. Left to your own devices, Hatonn says, you would soon become nothing but ghosts, ghosts in a living machine. We hope that you will do something about it.

I want to sit with that for a moment, because the voices are so often gentle that it is startling to hear them refuse to paint a rosy picture. They belong, they say, to the Confederation of Planets, and they are not blind. The love they speak of is not a denial of the darkness. It is an answer to it.

The questions that evening turn to wanderers, those souls said to have come from elsewhere to help, and to whether any come from beyond Hatonn's own Confederation. Yes, Hatonn says, there is another such company, much smaller, an uneasy combination of shifting influences that tends toward the negative side, not by intention but by the way it is organized. Some of its vehicles slip through the quarantine placed around the planet, and do what they can to disrupt an already chaotic society. The guardians watch. The quarantine holds. But nothing is simple.

A questioner asks what becomes of the wanderers when this age ends and the new one begins. Will they return to their home planets, or must some remain? Hatonn answers with unusual candor that they do not yet know. It depends on what your peoples do. If there is a man-made catastrophe that destroys your culture, he says, rather than a God-created one that destroys only portions of your geography, then one of their concerns will be to recover enough records to serve as a kind of Rosetta Stone for those who come after, so that future peoples may translate these works instead of feeling completely without aid. I find that image haunting and tender at once. A rescue mission for the records.

And then the session turns from the cosmic to the intimate, and this is where its heart really is. Hatonn speaks of the messages themselves, these small transmissions through ordinary people sitting in a circle, and calls them precious. Meditation groups such as this one, he says, are precious tools and avenues for the sharing and transmitting of the light, this light that shines within all creation.

Your days are well spent, he says, when spent in the realization of the oneness you share with all of creation. Pour your efforts into feeding that light, that it might burn ever brighter, covering more and more of your tired and weary world. Such meditations as this one are invaluable tools for lighting yet one more candle to illuminate the darkness. And he thanks those gathered for preparing a way for yet more of their fellow creatures to share in the bounty of the harvest.

So the evening that began with swollen bellies and ghosts in a living machine ends with a candle. One more candle. That is the scale of the work, as Hatonn sees it. Not saving the world in a single gesture, but lighting one more small light in the dark, and then another, until the tired world can see by them.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Journey Inward
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the journey inward.

Hatonn begins this evening with a question about desire. Why do some people go on safari to exotic places, discover remote islands, find new frontiers of learning, while others never stir? Few are the people who are driven, he says, and this is one of your planet's deepest problems. For you are all conscious beings, and your desire, whatever it may be, should be clear enough that you are literally driven to pursue it.

But how do you discover your true desire? You can think and plan and conjugate it in your mind, Hatonn says, and it will come to very little. To know your true desire, you must know yourself. And so the journey is not to an exotic island or on a safari. The journey is inward, to your heart, to that spark of love which holds the plan for you and for your universe and for your journey.

He looks at the planet and sees great turmoil, the daily seeking and striving for the things of the material world that so many think will bring peace of mind. How much of the things of your world are required, he asks, before peace of mind is achieved? Empires have been built and won and gathered, and those in whose rule the empire rests have found no peace. The seeking offers so little, in the final analysis. So he suggests, again, the daily meditation, the inward seeking of the spark of the divine Creator which we all share, each with the other.

Then comes one of the most beautiful passages in the session, and I want to give it to you nearly whole. So often, Hatonn says, you discount your own worth. And then he asks you to picture your humanity, your personality, your intellect as clothing, garments you wear into meditation. As you desire to know yourself and the Creator, strip off those things which limit you. Remove them gently, for they serve you well. Then bathe in the clean waters of the tranquil silence of the universal Thought, and come to rest in the heart of love. There you will find food and drink for your spirit. Parched and hungry though it may be, there is a never-ending supply of love for each of you, of courage, of innocence, of kindness, of all those things you would like to add to your wardrobe.

But they are not clothing, he says. They must come from the heart. They must come from yourself. Your ego, your personality, your intellect can never display to others what you truly wish. So let it all go and rest in love, with no name, no reputation, no learning. For love is the greatest force and the greatest knowledge you can possibly attain, and you cannot reach it with your mind, with your ego, with your personality. It is a matter of desire.

And then the line that closes his message, spoken to people he calls fellow travelers. We who are travelers upon that path hold our hand out to you, he says. Many of us come from a distance, some of us from other dimensions, but we are all here for one purpose, to hold out that hand to you and to say, fellow traveler, be not so weary that you forget to desire love.

Later, Latwii takes questions, and one of them is about the confusion of choosing between paths, between a mantra and a teacher, between east and west. Latwii's answer is wonderfully free. The path you would most benefit from following, he says, is the path of your own choosing. Your path may wind around various trees in the woods, around various incantations or postures or beliefs, but it shall surely bring you to the center of yourself. All of the foliage and shrubbery of the woods is there for you to enjoy along your path as you choose. There are no right or wrong choices. All will bring you to the destination you seek.

And when asked about dark forces and hidden powers on the planet, Latwii turns the question back on the questioner with a gentle firmness. Each time you meet a fellow creature and fail to recognize the divinity within, each time you turn your face from the light, you are polarized toward darkness. So the most important consideration is how you yourself live your own life, how you manifest the vibration of love. For love, he says, is that force which encompasses all.

Desire, then, is the thread through the whole evening. Desire to know yourself. Desire love. Choose your own path through the woods. And hold out your hand to the fellow traveler beside you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Scent of the Rose
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the scent of the rose.

This Monday session gives us one of the loveliest images in the whole archive, and it arrives in the very first minutes. Look at the rose, the speaker says, that blooms in its enormous wealth of color and scent and form, because it loves. There is nowhere you can truly look in the creation of the Father that you cannot find love.

And then the turn. Your life in this density, he says, is very like the rose. Your bloom and your form and your scent will please and glorify the Creator, and then be gone. What remains, if you have shown as much love as a simple rose climbing toward the light, is your scent, the odor of your spiritual being. Listen to how they put it. The thoughts and beings of the great teachers remain fresh in memory for many hundreds of years. All else is and shall be consumed in time.

The counsel that follows is practical. First center yourself, the speaker says. Feel the beauty of your own unfolding, the delicate scent of the love of the Creator that emanates from you in many ways. Do not see yourself in any way except as a channel for love. If you can maintain that connection in sincerity, that which you need shall be given to you.

Then Oxal speaks, and his message is about being seen. There is a crying need, he says, for those with the light and the experience of the light to share and shine it with your people, who are bathed in darkness. Part of why so many seek sincerely yet inefficiently is a lack of examples. There are too few examples of the light as you travel about in your daily activities. So shine that light forth with every opportunity. Be noticed as one who radiates the love and the peace of the Father to those who are harried and worried and unable to find the center within their own being.

By your example, Oxal says, you shall remind them that they too are capable of being such sources of light. It is a noble endeavor to be as an example. It is not always easy, but it is one of the most effective methods of teaching, for it says in an action what a thousand words may fail to say. Be as the shining light that is your source, and shine your light about you as you become beacons for your fellow creatures who are lost on dark and stormy seas.

Latwii closes the evening with questions, and two of his answers stay with me. The first is about tithing, about giving part of the fruits of your labor. The original concept, he says, is that all things come from the Creator, and any material supply you receive is the Creator's, all of it. In giving part of that bounty back, no matter how little or how much, you are blessing yourself. For the principle of giving is that those who give shall have a thousandfold added unto them, but those who keep and hoard will lose all that they have. The basic principle, however, is that tithing helps only one person, and that is you, for it puts you in a right relationship between your work and your Creator.

The second answer is quieter, and in some ways harder. Carla asks how she can better help a friend she has been teaching. Latwii praises her sharing, and then suggests that future sharings concentrate more on helping the entity to help himself, rather than depending on her efforts. Enter more of the concept of personal direction for him, Latwii says, and less dependence on yours. Even love, it seems, must respect the other person's right to learn by their own efforts.

So the evening is a rose, a beacon, an open hand, and a hand that knows when to let go. The scent remains. The light is noticed. The gift is given freely. And the student is trusted to walk.

Thank you for listening.

title: Rocks Amid the Quicksand
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: rocks amid the quicksand.

This is a short, sober session, recorded on a September evening in a small meeting with Jim. Hatonn speaks of the Earth changes the group had been discussing, the disturbances already beginning on the planet, and he does not offer comfort in the usual sense. He offers a task.

Those who survive the changes that are approaching, he says, will be in great need of guidance, even more than they are now. For reality shall, in the twinkling of an eye, be changed radically, and such an event will have drastic effects upon the mass consciousness of your people. At such a time it will be critical for the survivors to be aware of a greater reality: the reality of our unity, each with the other, that none are cast out alone on stormy seas, that even when the worst imaginable events have been played to their finale upon your Earth's stage, even then, and especially then, we are all one.

And who will tell them? Those who have traveled the path of peace, Hatonn says, those who have sought the truth before the storm. These pilgrims will be of invaluable service. They will be able to share the light that has been sparked within their being. The message is not to prepare a bunker. It is to prepare a way inward, for yourself and for others, so that when people wake from their sleep and ask the next obvious question, there is someone who knows the way to the answer.

Then Hatonn turns to the inner preparation, and this is the passage I want you to hear. In the days ahead, he says, the decisions which you as spiritual beings make will be the keynotes to the decisions upon the physical plane which you must then make to carry out your spiritual plan. Those who have consciously worked on seeking out their own identity will experience whatever happens with a different timbre and feeling. It will be seen differently by them.

Growth is always painful, he admits. You will experience discomfort, emotionally and mentally, as you adjust to new conditions of living. But those who are destined to live through the first changes, those who are as rocks amid the quicksand, will be able to view and deal with these discomforts in a manner befitting their state of mind. I love that image. Not a fortress, not an escape, but a rock. Something solid that others can hold to while the ground moves.

And here is the part that surprised me. Hatonn does not tell them to go it alone. He suggests that those who desire to aid the planet find groups of like-minded people and work as a community. For it is in community, he says, that your best abilities both to survive and to be a center of light will be realized. The rock amid the quicksand is not a solitary hero. It is a circle of people holding steady together.

He will not say who will survive and who will not. He says plainly that they cannot see that far, and would not tell them if they could. What he offers instead are guidelines, so that the vibrational change and its aftereffects, which are already being felt, will not seem overly traumatic, and may even seem, in some ways, a ray of hope. For people will be turning from their previous sleep, awakening to the brevity of their physical lives, and asking whether they will survive the demise of their own physical vehicle. That concern alone, in a time of difficulty, will have many seeking answers.

So the evening ends with an encouragement and a promise. Be dedicated to the inward work, Hatonn says, and know that we are with you whenever you ask. The storm may come. The ground may move. Be the rock. Hold the light. And hold each other.

Thank you for listening.

title: Love in Action
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: love in action.

This September Sunday session is about service, and it opens with a distinction I think is worth the whole evening. Hatonn says they have been speaking to the group about discovering the inner self, the seed of love within. Tonight they want to talk about love in action. For there is no tree planted without help, he says, and no crop gathered without reapers.

But he is careful, as always, about the manner of it. They have cautioned the group many times not to be aggressive or abrasive. What he asks for instead is confidence, the confidence of knowing who you are and whose glory you may manifest. It is a responsibility to know, he says, for then you must serve. And in each contact that you make, you are manifesting the Creator in some manner.

Think back, he says, to the moment when you yourself became aware of the kingdom, and of all there was to gain from the knowledge and the being of it. You will understand how precious it is to be able to share that experience with others. It is written that there is great joy when one lost sheep is brought back into the fold, more joy than all the ninety-nine others, for they were already found. Use your being, Hatonn says, to allow those about you to dwell in such an atmosphere that they too have the potential of realizing who they are also.

Then the teaching sharpens into something I find genuinely demanding. If you see those about you as perfect beings, he says, you are seeing them clearly. If you see them only in their emotional, mental, and physical illusory patterns, you are not seeing them clearly, and you are not allowing them the freedom to reach the point which was so precious to you when you reached it. To your inner eye, that patient, timeless inner eye, each being is perfect, manifesting in the eternal present. Give that gift in love. For to expend all your energy upon yourself will block you from gaining more understanding. You must use what you have learned until it becomes a part of you, until it becomes second nature.

The second part of his message goes deeper into the mechanics of service. To serve, Hatonn says, is to allow that gift of the infinite Creator, the energy which courses through your various bodies, to continue its flow and be shared by your fellow creatures. So few have discerned the nature of service, because their ways have been circling round unto themselves, so that the energy which is their daily gift stays only within their being as they seek to fill themselves with the material rewards of the world. But consider, he says, as you go forth in your daily round, that each person you meet is the Creator. And what else can one do, when one knows that he or she is also of the Creator, other than serve the Creator? What else can one do other than serve the Creator?

He leaves them with one more image before he goes, and it is a fountain again, this time of light. Above all, he says, realize that you are in a divine flow of perfect love, into which you may tap as into an ever-flowing fountain, cascading, scintillating, full of light, full of energy. And then the instruction, which is almost startling in its simplicity. Choose. At any moment that you can, stop and choose. It is your path, it is your illusion, it is your thought, it is your action.

Latwii takes questions afterward, and one of them is about the tangle of choosing a spiritual path, mantra or teacher, east or west. His answer is wonderfully free, and it belongs with this evening's theme. Follow the path of your own choosing, he says. Your path may wind around various trees in the woods, around various incantations or postures or beliefs, but it shall surely bring you to the center of yourself. There are no right or wrong choices. All will bring you to the destination you seek. Experience what seems of value, examine it with your own thinking, meditate on it within your own being, and you will have your answers. For you are at this moment one with your answers.

And when someone asks about the nature of death itself, why the body must perish, Latwii answers with the session's quietest line. It is an illusion that you live within, he says, and an illusion that you die when you leave. Your physical vehicle is a requirement for this particular stage and this particular drama, a costume for the part you are playing. When you leave this stage you will merely change roles and costumes, as you have done so many times before. You are at this moment immortal.

Love in action, then, is not frantic. It is seeing the other as perfect, letting the energy flow through instead of circling it back on yourself, choosing your own path through the woods, and stopping, at any moment you can, to choose.

Thank you for listening.

title: The River of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the river of love.

This short September session is a meditation on a single question, and Hatonn asks it directly. He would speak, he says, a few words on the subject of love as it is experienced, or as it may be experienced, in your daily life. And then he asks each listener to examine the concept they carry within themselves as love, and to ask whether it is clear, and whether it is free of conditions.

Does the energy known as love flow freely through your being? Does it flow as the river, without interference? And if, in your examinations, you discover blockages in the flow here or there, from whence come these blockages? Examine carefully, my friends, for though love is the basic power and motivating source of the universe, still it may be blocked by individual perceptions and behaviors.

I love the patience of this. There is no scolding in it. Only an invitation to look, honestly, at the course and the channel and the way you allow love to flow. Are there constrictions? Are there blockages? If so, how best removed? It is not always easy to let the energy course through and wash the perceptive blocks away, he admits, for frequently we wish, as individuals, that it would flow one way or another. We want love on our terms, directed where we choose.

But the unimpeded flow of the energy of the Creator, Hatonn says, is the greatest feeling of freedom which an entity can experience, for the flow has within it the wisdom of the Creator. And each of the creations of the Father is as a vessel which holds and allows this energy to be. Each of you is as a vessel, as a channel, which allows or restricts the flow. The choice is not whether the river exists. The choice is whether you narrow its banks.

The session then moves to a stranger and grander teaching, about the creative energy itself. The creative energy creates all there is, Hatonn says, and it is channeled through each individual, controlled only by an individual's thought. This is the natural way. All the planets, all the vegetation, all the animals, all the birds that fly in the sky, are all thought forms brought into reality by the original creative energy directed through the co-creators that inhabit the universe.

Each of you has this power, he says, and always has had it, and always will have it. One thing is necessary. To act as the perfect modulator, the perfect filter. Only one thing is necessary, and that is to think as your Creator. Many lessons have been given to bring your peoples back to that original state of perfection that is normal.

And then the closing, which the tape cuts off mid-sentence, but which arrives whole enough to carry. There are things your people have called miracles, Hatonn says, and yet these are normal activities. If you wish to perform a miracle, all that is necessary is that you do so. Each of you has the ability to do anything. All that is necessary is for you to think the original Thought, become one with that Thought, open yourself as a channel to the infinite energy of the universe. Become in tune with its song. That song is a song of love. Become receptive to that song. Hear it. Be one with it.

So the evening's question returns, quieter now. Is your love flowing like a river, or have you narrowed its banks? The song is playing either way. The only question is whether you are in tune.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Way of Harmony
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the way of harmony.

Latwii opens this September Sunday with a subject he calls rare on your planet. Harmony. It is a state not frequently found upon your world, he says, as is evidenced by the condition of things at present. And then he defines it with a simplicity I keep returning to. Harmony is that state of being in tune with the infinite Creator, which is achieved by desire. A desire for unification. A desire for knowing and experiencing that fullness of being which is the Creator within.

But here is the part that matters. Harmony is not a solitary achievement. It is unfortunate, Latwii says, that few upon your planet seek it, for it is an endeavor which includes the welfare of those around you, and most of your people are pointed in the direction of their own interests, fearing there will not be enough to go round. Harmony is achieved with others, in cooperative effort, as individual entities blend their energies with each other. It usually entails a type of compromise of positions, so that each may share a common position with the other. And the sharing of it, the sharing of the position, the belief, the place, is what harmony is.

The first step, he says, is to give. To recognize the needs, the rights, and the position of those close about you. And this state of giving and accepting and recognizing will be reciprocated by those with whom you are in close contact. For the state of giving is based upon the concept of love. To give is to share that which is love, and that which is love is recognized by the inner being of those to whom it is given, even when it begins in modest ways, in the simple recognition of another person's needs.

And then the line that gathers the whole teaching into a practice. Harmony, Latwii says, is that process whereby people in close communication join their beings even closer by agreeing to accept each other as they are, and to work from that beginning point in a constant balancing of the needs, ideas, and beliefs of each party. Accept each other as you are. Work from there. Keep balancing. That is the whole of it.

The questions that follow range widely, and Latwii's answers keep circling back to the same ground. Asked about the great concern for the survival of leaders in the coming age, he answers with an old phrase. The first shall be last, and the last shall be first.
