For those who would seek to gain the whole world and yet lose their souls, what in truth have they gained? To hold tightly to the material is to build a house upon sand. Those who have no concern for the welfare of those they were chosen to serve shall find themselves at the bottom of the pit of their own being, which they have dug with their own hands.

The new age, he says, will see many different responses to the flow of energy now sweeping over the planet, and you may expect to see the most absurd of dramas appearing upon your world's stage. But those energies may be channeled and focused into creative centers by those who are truly concerned with serving their brothers and sisters. To focus in the direction of the spirit is the means by which true survival shall be attained.

Asked about other sources of channeled information, Latwii refuses to rank teachers. With all sources of information, including especially our own, he says, consider carefully within yourselves what you yourselves believe. Evaluate on your own what you are reading or hearing. It is your task, as entities upon your planet, to sort and sift through the infinite variety of information available, and to choose that which speaks within your own being.

And to the one who asks how to become a channel, Latwii gives the evening's simplest counsel. To desire this type of service is the most important ingredient. Search within your own being that you might be made an instrument. Meditate daily, at the same time each day, so that you develop a pattern of relaxation and communication within yourself. Use a simple prayer to ask that divine guidance be with you. And spend time with those who have experience, that the vibration may become familiar to you.

Desire unification. Give first. Accept each other as you are. Choose what speaks within your own being. The way of harmony is not complicated. It is only difficult, the way all simple things are difficult.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Season for Sowing
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the season for sowing.

This October session is one of the most solemn in the archive, and Latwii knows it. He opens by saying the channel herself does not understand why he is giving this message, for she herself is not sorrowful, yet she will speak it faithfully. He sounds this somber note, he says, because he wishes to tell them something plain. And then he describes what it is like, for beings such as his, to enter human minds. It is as though we were inside a deep well, he says. And we understand the claustrophobia of those like you who, knowing there are other ways to live, must live in this well, this deep well of sorrow, limitation, and lack.

Against that darkness he sets a single simple truth, and he is almost embarrassed by its simplicity. All we have to tell you, he says, is what you already know. Many have said it before us. Love is all that there is. Light is the manifestation of love, and each of you is vibrating in some area of light, not only in your physical body, but in your thought body and your emotional body and your spiritual body. Some of you are more harmonious than others, and we can see you, as the song you just heard said, as a kind of chord of being. And yet all of you emanate it, and will return to the one perfect light, the one beingness of love. In fact, you have not left. This trip, this journey, is an illusion you created because you chose not to be aware of the original Thought of love.

There are almost no people to whom you may speak of simple things, he says. Almost all who attempt to speak wisdom unto you speak a complex wisdom, one that breaks down so that reality forever recedes before you. The truth is simple. And that is why they urge daily meditation, not as ritual, not to convert anyone from any path, but because in meditation you simply listen. It is written in your holy works that the place whereon you stand is holy ground. You carry your tabernacle and your meaning with you. It is a bag you can never leave behind when you pack.

I love the image he uses next. When something is troubling you in the physical world, he says, it is handy to take a pocket knife and cut away the hanging thread, whatever has begun to seem shabby and extraneous. There is a great deal in your thoughts of the same quality, and meditation has the same effect as a good sharp pocket knife. It cuts through a good deal that you could not cut through with your intellect, in order to bring you to the present, to infinity, to love.

Then the urgency. If you are going to pursue the life of a student of reality, Latwii says, if you are going to attempt to love with the love of the Creator, it is time now for you to decide, and to do it. There will be an hour in the not-so-distant future when you will be what you have become. And like it or not, that will be your time. Becoming will temporarily be at an end, and whatever you have developed up until that point will be your sensitivity, your resource, and your sanctuary.

When Carla asks whether the time for contemplation is giving way to a time for action, Latwii answers with the analogy of the gardener. To reap the desired harvest, one must plant the seeds. Seeds take time to grow. There is a season for growth and a season for harvest. Your people have had many seasons in which to sow the seeds of love. Too often other seeds were sown. Too often weeds were allowed to grow. Too often the flower of love went unwatered. And now the season grows short. There is only what appears to be a single season remaining for the seeds of love to be sown.

One questioner pushes back, uneasy with the talk of light and darkness, of weeds and harvest, insisting that everything is love and nothing is evil. Latwii does not argue. He thanks the man for sharing his feelings, and offers this instead. We would ask each to consider what part of the message has value for them, and to take that part and use it, and to nourish what they hold within their own being to be of love, and to take the part which they do not feel and simply brush it aside, as the chaff is brushed aside from the berry of wheat.

Take what is wheat. Brush aside the chaff. Sow the seed while the season lasts. The well is deep, but the light is real, and the time, Latwii says, is now.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Honest Mirror
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the honest mirror.

This October session introduces a voice heard only rarely in the archive, one who calls himself Monka. He is new to the group, halting, almost shy about the contact, and what he brings is a single image, held up without flinching. A mirror.

You cannot look away from the mirror, Monka says. Look away from your mirror and up to the stars. The stars are a mirror. Look away from the stars and into the face of the person you like the least. Aha. A mirror. Look into the eyes of those you consider robots and thieves. Look into the mechanisms of your government. Behold the mirror.

How little you know of yourself, he says, if you do not know that all things are you. When you study, what do you study? Whatever it is, you are studying yourself. Stare deeply into yourself. Leap at that mirror. What do you feel? What do you deny? You are looking in a mirror. You are looking at your shadow. Drink it.

And then the instruction that gives this episode its name. Look always straight and without sympathy at yourself, Monka says, wherever you may find that manifestation in the mirror of your existence. Continue to be both merciless and idealistic, he urges, both fierce and tender, for those who love mankind must indeed use the sword and the embrace.

Jim asks Latwii afterward to explain this, because it troubles him. How do you balance looking without sympathy against looking with affection and acceptance? Latwii answers with one of the most searching passages in the archive, and I want to give it room. Monka was attempting to give you some idea of the eye of the Creator, Latwii says, as filtered through the tree of duality. When there abounds too much sympathy, when sympathy becomes too sentimental, when sympathy becomes self-pity, when sympathy becomes denial of a part of oneself, it is then that the surgeon's knife must come out. You must cut away that part of yourself that cannot be merciless in accepting all that there is in yourself.

When you deal with that which has no sympathy, Latwii continues, with the murderer, the rapist, the terrorizer, then balance with sympathy. But first, the merciless seeing. If you look into the mirror, you see yourself as you really are. But most cannot look into that mirror, even into their own eyes, for they become quite frightened. To love oneself fully, he says, is to know without mercy the folly of the depths of one's heart. It is to know and accept without mercy the deepest and most degrading parts of one's being. For they are not fantasies. They are all being acted out upon the stage of your sphere at this very moment.

Can you cry mercy, he asks. No. You must stand without sympathy and accept the totality of your being, and then pour love from the Creator into that world, into that merciless darkness, with every iota of your being. For only when you know total mercilessness in your estimation of yourself can you be truly a channel for love.

And then the closing image, which lands like a bell. Spirits are lovely, Latwii says, but the sturdy ones who stand astride the world of illusion, of pain, of limitations of all kinds, and against that illusion take up the sword of love, ah, there is the soldier that shall conquer in the name of love.

Monka's mirror and Latwii's sword belong together. See everything, refuse nothing, drink the shadow, and then pour the love. The embrace means nothing without the honesty that precedes it.

Thank you for listening.

title: Faith in Things Unseen
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: faith in things unseen.

This October session belongs to Laitos, the gentlest voice in the Confederation's circle, the one who works with new channels and with those learning to quiet their minds. Much of the session is about the work of channeling itself, about gaining confidence and learning to speak the thoughts that appear in the mind without analyzing them first. But near the end, Laitos turns from the mechanics to the meaning, and the tone changes entirely.

It is especially important, Laitos says, to establish good contacts at this particular time, and not only that, but to establish them in those who are grounded in themselves as seekers, who cannot be moved. For there will come times in which your faith will be shaken. It will seem that you have too great a task to accomplish, too many unanswerable questions to deal with. However, that which is needed will be provided. That which is to be, will be.

I want to pause on that sentence, because it is doing two things at once. It does not promise that the shaking will not come. It promises that the provision will come with it. The faith being asked for is not a guarantee against difficulty. It is a steadiness inside difficulty, a groundedness that cannot be moved because it does not depend on conditions.

Laitos is clear about what they will and will not protect. Although there will be miracles, he says, we shall not safeguard the physical lives and the artificial values of each of those who seek our information. Our concern is for the things of the spirit. You must have covering for your feet and protection against the cold and food to fill your bellies while you are in the physical, he says, practical as ever. But do not be overly concerned. Work upon yourselves, upon your desire, and upon your sense of will.

Then comes the teaching on mission, which I find startling in its plainness. It is not understood in your culture, Laitos says, that a person can be born with a mission. It is taken as a sign of mental aberration that such a belief could be held. Yet your higher self planned certain things for you to accomplish. To seek them. To know the Creator, the channel through which your higher self speaks to you, that you may know in each day the service and the action and the manifestation of that day, and in each experience the lesson and the import of that experience.

The idea is not that your life is scripted. It is that your deeper self set a direction before you arrived, and that each day carries some piece of it, if you are listening. The channel for hearing it is the Creator remembered as the center, as the giver, as the source, and as the identity of the self. Keep that center, and the day's work reveals itself.

And then the closing line, the one this episode is named for. If you cannot be shaken from the faith in things unseen, Laitos says, those things which you can see will never shake you.

It is a small sentence, and it inverts the whole usual order of belief. We tend to want the visible to confirm the invisible. Laitos says the traffic runs the other way. Hold the unseen steady, and the seen loses its power to unmake you. The shepherds he is speaking to, the ones who would carry this work, need exactly that kind of faith. Not faith that nothing will go wrong. Faith that cannot be moved when it does.

Laitos leaves the group the way he came, quietly, with thanks for their dedication, joining them with his whole heart. He is aware, he says, of questions still beneath the surface, and he is content to await their maturity. For the answers, after all, are within you.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Education of the Soul
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the education of the soul.

Latwii opens this October session by saying he has very little in words to share, because the group's understanding of the basic truths is already fairly strong, and their minds have been all too active. So instead of a lecture, he offers a journey. Come with us, he says, floating up from your physical vehicles as you would float in the water, light as a bubble. There are no more limitations. There is no more ugliness, for you are now seeing reality, and the light is very bright.

You may pass through many dimensions and colors, he says, and glimpse many universes being born and existing in ways far unlike your own. You may do this for infinity, but this is only a short trip, for in the end you will desire to arrive back in your physical vehicle, refreshed, and ready again to take up the task of loving and living consciously and well.

When the journey ends, the teaching begins, and it is about forgiveness, beginning with the hardest object of forgiveness. Be aware of each other as the Creator, Latwii says, and be aware of yourself as the Creator. Forgive others, but far more, forgive yourself. For though you may have many times heard and made mistakes, yet you have learned from these mistakes. And how else can you learn, when that is the entire reason for this experience you are now sharing? Education. The education of your soul.

And then the line I want to underline twice. Do not worry about your grade, as a spirit, he says, but simply enjoy what you can. And when there is not the simple enjoyment, take conscious enjoyment in the knowledge that you are learning. The whole cosmos as a school, and the only failing grade is refusing to enjoy the lessons.

A questioner asks about the fear of letting go in meditation, the pull toward something like astral travel, and the fear of being lost or harmed out there. Latwii's answer is disarmingly practical. You separate from your body every time you sleep, he says, so it is not an alien occurrence. The discomfort some feel comes from physiological reactions, sounds and vibrations as the bodies part unevenly, and this often causes fear. But there is no astral boogeyman waiting for you.

The places you wish to go, he says, are created by your desire, and you will go where your desire is to go, and visit whom or what your desire is to visit. Your desire shapes your experience. That is a law of the universe. If you are cautious, work with a group in meditation, so they act as batteries strengthening your desire for the truth, the good, and the beautiful. For in those realms, your thoughts are the only reality. As your thoughts are, so shall you go.

But he adds something important, and it steadies the whole discussion. It is not necessary to experience any unusual phenomenon in order to experience the release and freedom that the love and light of the infinite Creator can bring. This can be experienced in any condition. It requires only a state of mind capable of grasping love. Cultivate freedom in whatever state you find yourself, and choose freely what you wish to experience, according to your desires.

There will come a time, Latwii says, when you will not be burdened with the difficulties of this density, and you will be far more able to see the love and the light of the Creator at work in your lives. Meanwhile, there is an element of faith in living well, and he encourages them to refresh it by cleansing themselves in the waters of meditation.

So the session that began with floating like a bubble ends with both feet on the ground. Forgive yourself. Enjoy the schooling. Let desire shape the journey. And remember that freedom is a state of mind, available in any condition, to anyone willing to grasp love.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Mind Is Water
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the mind is water.

Latwii opens this late October session with an image of unusual delicacy. He says he can see the calm growing within the group's minds as they settle into meditation, as though it were the surface of a quiet pond which had been tossed by storms and blown by the wind, and now begins to calm under sunny skies, and to reflect more accurately the beauty of the foliage surrounding the pond.

The minds of your people are so often disturbed, he says, by the waves and storms of emotion, emotion developed by the sense of separateness of one being from another. If he could give them one concept, the waters of the mind would ever be calm, and the springs of inspiration would flow clear and sweet. That concept is one Thought. It is written in your holy works as one word. That word is love.

Love, manifesting in your world as light, is the source of all matter, all consciousness, and all energy, he says. All the beauty you see is a living embodiment of love. And the darkness that does not understand it, the separation, will always be so. The complex will never understand the simple.

Then comes the teaching this episode is named for. People find their minds to be like stone, Latwii says, their opinions and biases etched in the stony surface with great deliberation, and therefore people do not change. Yet in truth, all living things are in a constant state of change, and thus the mind is water, not stone. For water can adapt itself to any circumstance, and in the end is stronger than any rock. Look at your rivers and your canyons. Given time, water erodes that hard and unforgiving stone, absorbing life-giving minerals, flowing, always flowing, giving beauty and life, rain from the sky, waves along the shore.

That is the secret of your consciousness, he says. Your mind is much stronger than you may think. Not because of its firmness, but because of its incredible ability to learn, to change, to adapt, and to transform itself, just as water becomes part of the air and is then reformed as a life-giving substance watering the crops.

You can no more be separate from each other, he says, than one drop of water can be separate from the ocean. We are all one. And in this may we humbly rejoice.

The session closes with a parable I have been turning over ever since I read it. Suppose, Latwii says, that your neighbor had a very large garden, and yours was very small. But in your garden you planted with balance, with an understanding of sun and shade, of color and beauty and the needs of each plant. You weeded and fed and harvested, with flowers about its edges. And your neighbor's garden, large as it may be, was planted without regard to the needs of plants, allowed to grow wildly, weeds growing along with the food, no flowers, no eye for beauty. Which garden would be the beautiful garden? The small one.

It is not how great the deeds are that we do, he says, in our day-by-day existence. It is the grace and the understanding with which we do them. Keep your heart full of love and your mind acquainted with beauty. And no matter how great, how intellectual, how ambitious are the people with whom you deal, the quality will be judged only by the grace with which each of you meets the small requirements of the day, the tiny moments when you can be graceful and kind and appreciative.

Never, ever lose confidence, he says, in the beauty and the grace and the importance of yourself. For you are the Creator. You have, within you, all that anyone has. Perhaps your lot in life, this particular time, is not dramatic. But if you are graceful in the smallest thing, you are a better channel for love than the greatest individual who does not look to love for his actions.

The pond calms. The water wears down the stone. The small garden blooms. Be water, and be graceful in the smallest thing.

Thank you for listening.

title: The True Union
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the true union.

This November session takes up a question that was pressing on the group's minds, about relationships, about why so many partnerships were straining and breaking at once. Hatonn answers with an image from the mineral world. Picture the formation of crystals, he says. There is a great deal of rock that is not crystallized at all, and is therefore insensitive to delicate vibrations.

Most people, he says, feel the new vibrations of the dawning age only faintly, their crystallization of purpose so truncated that it hardly matters to them, and their relationships are governed almost entirely by needs for procreation, companionship, and financial aid. When those conditions are not met, this type of union will cease. It is not a judgment. It is a description of what holds such unions together, and what happens when the holding fails.

But seeded among your peoples, Hatonn says, are more crystallized souls, spirits oriented toward reflecting and refracting the light and love of the Creator, people of magnetism and illumination, each committed in their own way to the path. And here is the difficulty. It is the nature of most crystals to be flawed, and the delicate vibrations of the new age are such that each crystal will begin to disintegrate along the flawed line. It is within each entity's free will to rebuild in such a manner that the flaw no longer exists. But this is extremely painful.

And this, he says, is the great contributing cause of the relationship difficulties so many are observing and experiencing. Those undergoing personal purification, in order to become purely crystallized on the path to mastery, very often blame the pain of transformation upon those nearest them, interpreting the pain as having to do with a relationship, rather than recognizing that the problem is completely personal, and is no reflection upon any partner, child, or situation.

I find that both bracing and merciful. Bracing, because it relocates the work where it belongs. Merciful, because it reframes the pain. When the entity has vibratory difficulties, Hatonn says later, it is not failure. It is simply the pain of growing.

The session then turns to the deeper question underneath. What is spiritual union, truly? Hatonn speaks of the two poles of the love and light of the infinite Creator. One is love, the other wisdom. Love is a female vibration and wisdom male, he says, using those terms because they will be helpful. Neither will be of service in becoming a channel for the love and light of the Creator without some balancing agent of the other. To achieve mastery, the two must come into balance, so that each nature holds both in full.

And then the sentence I keep coming back to. Love without wisdom, he says, is wasted on foolish things. And wisdom without love is hollow, and foolish also. This is the true basis of spiritual union. This is the true yoga, for the female and the male to work out together the lessons of love and wisdom.

It is nearly impossible to achieve mastery alone, Hatonn says. Those who achieve it, for the most part, work with a partner. Yet there are those who must experience solitude until they are ready to open themselves. Then the opener, the partner, will appear, and they will be caught up without doubts or prejudice. For such is true union that it is impossible to ignore.

And what of the pain of the work itself? Initiation through purification exists for those ready to work upon themselves, Hatonn says, and the currency of this work is most often pain. It is in time balanced by joy. The nature of this illusion is polarity. Remember that you are a continuing soul, and that this particular incarnation is merely one small part of the circle of yourself. It does not always make sense day by day. Look at the greater cycles, knowing that that which you need will come to you, and be unmistakable.

The crystal reforms along the flaw. Love learns wisdom, wisdom learns love. And the pain, in time, is balanced by joy.

Thank you for listening.

title: Believe Your Heart
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: believe your heart.

This November session contains a confession I did not expect. Hatonn, the patient teacher of love and light, tells the group a story from his own people's past. At one time, he says, we of Hatonn were a warlike nation. Though united as one planet, we were divided into sects that strove to dominate and control it. We chose to combat one another. None could dominate, and all were weakened by the struggle.

Finally a point was reached, he says, in which they were destitute. They had destroyed all the resources the planet had to offer, and could not kill one another simply because they no longer possessed the raw materials for further weaponry. They had destroyed their food chain and were near starvation. In many ways, he says, we were at that time very similar to you as your planet is today, fixed upon oblivion.

What saved them was not a triumph but a surrender of priorities. They discovered that survival superseded all other priorities, and the requirements for survival became very obvious. Regard each man or woman as one's own brother, and share with that brother as you would with your wife or husband or child. Their decimation became, in this manner, their strength. In choosing to reduce the planet's ability to support life, they inadvertently chose a strenuously spiritual path, that of loving through forced sharing.

And then the line that stops me every time. Then we learned, Hatonn says, that sharing was more valuable than surviving. They obtained a vibration that enabled them to sustain their bodies and at the same time progress beyond physical needs. He shares this not in pride, he says, but in encouragement. Small though your numbers may be, those of you who have grown beyond your brothers in your desire to love and share will be able, in destitution and poverty and starvation, to mold and guide the growth of your race, but only if you keep faith with your feelings.

He adds a word about pain that belongs beside the story. Growing pains will occur, he says, that you may adapt yourselves to the experience of pain without taking the pain within and clinging to it as one would a valuable jewel or possession. All things pass, as will your pains. Do not let them worry you. They are merely tools with which the universe shapes the final product which you so desire to become.

Latwii takes the questions afterward, and his answers are among the bluntest in the archive. Asked how much to believe the various teachers and channeled sources, he answers the most important question first. You are not to believe any teacher, he says. You must believe your heart. There is no true teacher but yourself, for there is no one but yourself. All the information that comes your way does so for a purpose. Out of it you take what vibrates to you as proper. The rest you discard. This is true of all information, including, he adds with dry humor, the owner's manual of your car.

We do not consider ourselves a higher source, he says. We are your brothers. We have had experience. We share it. It may not help you. It is as simple as that. And then the image that gathers it all. You are like a web shining in the light, and you weave yourself moment by moment. Do not compare teachers. They are all lacking. Listen to the wind, and attentively weave your life from the strands of love and light the Creator has placed at your momentary disposal.

Asked about karma, Latwii gives the clearest definition in the archive. Karma is, very simply, action, he says. There is a law in your physics of equal and opposite reaction, and this holds true unless a higher law of creation is invoked. And that law is forgiveness. If you can forgive yourself, or forgive another, you have eliminated that much karma. You have nulled the action, and there will be no reaction. This is what the master known as Jesus was exemplifying. He stopped the wheel of karma. And so may you, without being quite so dramatic.

And his final counsel to the questioner tangled in worry about lessons and lifetimes is the simplest of all. Release the lessons, the worries, the distress, the confusion, and meditate. Enjoy yourself, my brother. That is the highest advice we can think of to give you. Laugh and love and be. What you came here to learn, you will only learn by embracing this life with love.

A warlike people learned that sharing outweighed surviving. The wheel of karma stops at forgiveness. And no teacher outranks your own heart.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Seed of Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the seed of love.

This late November session opens with a re-reading of one of the most familiar stories in the Western world, and Hatonn insists we have been misunderstanding it. It is said, he begins, that the one known as Jesus was incarnate by a virgin, and was made man, and dwelt among men, and by them was crucified. This, he says, is a much misunderstood story, a much misunderstood example, and a vastly underrated life. Around it has been built a great organization, all too lacking in the one thing that entity desired, and that is the experience of being one with the Creator.

Then he turns the story inward, and this is where the session becomes extraordinary. You yourselves, he says, are at some stage of holy conception by the inspirited self, that self who you really are. This self was not conceived by man, but came to this plane asleep in a body, the physical vehicle. The physical conception was, of course, not immaculate. But the spiritual conception which each of you who seek are attempting to further is totally immaculate, and takes place within what we may call your heart of hearts, within your deepest inner self.

And like an infant, he says, the spiritual self must be nurtured, loved, and nourished, through meditation and through as much right action as you can possibly interject into your daily lives. I love how tender and how demanding this is at once. Something holy is being born in you, and it needs tending the way a child needs tending. It cannot raise itself.

He knows it sounds impossibly difficult. But once an understanding of the love of the infinite Creator has been realized, he says, that which is difficult will become obvious, and that which is crooked will be made straight.

Take heed, he urges, for you have within you the most precious thing in the creation. Take heed to your spirits. Nourish them, and hearken to the faint music of the angelic choirs as they resound throughout the heavens. For each realized soul is a cause of great rejoicing among our peoples, for the harvest draws near and we grow closer to you.

Draw on us if you need us, Hatonn says, but more than any, draw upon the love within you, the truth that resides within you, the one original Thought that created you. All of these things you bear within yourself. Let them be born. And then the line that closes the passage like a benediction. Never let the limitation of your physical vehicle distract you from the perfect beauty of that which is born within you, the seed of creation, which is love.

Latwii takes the questions afterward, and one answer belongs with this theme so closely that I am placing it here. Asked about the feeling of being a finite being trying to understand the infinite, Latwii answers that the concept of yourself as finite is essentially incorrect. You are an infinite being able to experience an infinite Creator. In fact, you are the infinite Creator, as is each person into whose eyes you may gaze.

It is written in your holy works, he says, before the world was, I am. There is no past, there is no future. There is an infinite present, and I am. Your being is infinite and preceded the making of this galaxy, this solar system, this Earth. And to understand your being is to understand love, for it was the love of the Creator that generated awareness. I am. That is you, and that is infinite.

Your brain, with all its limitations, its overloads and confusions, is merely a tool, Latwii says, that you have sometimes used poorly. Never let it tell you what to do. Let your heart and your will express themselves, so that your mind performs the tasks given it by love, working as a servant to you, who work as a servant to the creation.

The infant in the heart of hearts. The seed of love waiting to be born. The mind as servant, the heart as master. Nourish what is growing in you, and let it be born.

Thank you for listening.

title: Prayer Is a Conversation
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: prayer is a conversation.

This December session, recorded on the anniversary of Pearl Harbor, takes up the darkest subjects in the archive, and handles them with a steadiness I admire. A questioner asks about Satan, whether such a being lives. Latwii answers carefully. There is an entity in people's hearts known as Satan to them, he says. But this entity is part of the illusion of your density. There is no being known as Satan on your physical plane, nor has there ever been.

What exists, he says, is a thought form. The vibration you live in is made of many pairs of opposites, and the interplay between them causes movement. The principle called Satan is something within consciousness which repels, and thus causes growth and movement. Those drawn to the negative principle have chosen a path of separation, a path of belief in the importance of the self, which leads them to desire power over others. Those polarized toward the good desire power over themselves, so that they may better serve others.

And then the turn that gives the darkness its proper size. The one known as Satan, Latwii says, is merely the shadow of evil thoughts. Given fear enough, evil thoughts can do harm, can cause fear and pain and anguish. This power is given to the Satanic principle only through the fear of the one who is feeling the difficulty. There is no reality to the fear, and thus it is said that love casteth out fear. The principle called Satan is a lonely and sad thought form. And we would say to you, accept this principle as part of yourself, as that within you which spurs you on to growth, to new understandings, to desire for truth. Love this entity, therefore, and take all strength from this mere shadow.

Asked whether there is a war between Latwii and this darkness, he answers that the battle is real but not physical. Whatever occurs upon your plane has already been joined, he says, and it is fought with the heart and the minds and the spirits of mankind, not with their physical bodies. The forces of darkness, he says, will always be scattered, for they do not trust one another, but wish only to have power over one another as well as over all else. Whereas those in the light have one Creator to guide them and one great truth to sustain them.

The session then turns to prayer, and Latwii's teaching on it is one of the warmest passages in the archive. How does prayer function, he is asked. And he answers with a question of his own. How does your question function to cause an answer from me as I listen to you? It is self-evident, is it not? Prayer is a conversation.

Sometimes you ask for things for yourself. Sometimes you ask intercession for others. Sometimes you only wish to say thanksgiving to the Creator and have no questions at all. Sometimes you merely say, what should I do today, and then you listen, that also being a prayer. It is a rather privileged conversation, held inwardly, between yourself and the one whose spirit will fill your life if you request it.

You cannot speak too softly for the Creator, he says, for the Creator is the entire creation, omnipresent, and therefore knowing everything. But one of the sad things about prayer is that the Creator often speaks more softly than the one who prays can hear. Then he who prays will say, my prayer was not answered. But prayer is always answered. Perhaps the answer is no, when you wished it to be yes. But always there is a contact that is infallible, the still, small voice.

And when the questioner is troubled by the paradox, by the promise that those who ask shall receive, Latwii does not resolve it so much as deepen it. You will find in your spiritual life, he says, that you are constantly running up against paradoxes. This is one of the signs of spiritual progress. If your basic desire is to know the truth, to know the will of the Creator in your life, that is what you will find. And what you thought you prayed for, you may find you did not pray for so much as you prayed for the understanding, love, and presence of the infinite Creator in your life.

Knock, and it shall be opened unto you, he says. But which door are you knocking upon? And then the warning, delivered with unmistakable affection. Be careful what you pray for, my brother, for sometimes the Creator in His wisdom will give it to you, just so that you will find out what to truly pray for.

A shadow with no substance but the fear we feed it. A battle fought with hearts, not bodies. And a conversation, held inwardly, with one who always answers, even when the answer is no.

Thank you for listening.

title: Anger at the Creator
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: anger at the creator.

Hatonn opens this December session with a subject he says has not often been dealt with in these meetings. He wishes to share some thoughts upon the anger that you may feel at times toward your Creator.

He begins by granting the anger its full weight. You live and breathe in a world full of seeming injustice and cruelty, he says. Things occur in your own lives which are quite simply unfair. There is nowhere you can look where this pattern is not repeated endlessly. The innocent deer fleeing the burning forest onto a road where men wait with guns. A friend unfairly taken from you, or hurt. Sadness for your planet, and the frustration that you can do nothing. It is only natural that you should become angry. But to whom should you direct your anger? You can only direct it at the Creator.

And we would suggest to you, Hatonn says, that at times it is healthy to do so. Express your anger and your frustration and your grief. Remove it from your system. Purge it as if it were an unhealthy substance. For the Creator is able to absorb this energy. As this instrument would say, He can take it. You cannot damage the Creator.

Then the teaching deepens. Who is the Creator? He is yourself, ourselves, your friends, those whom you prefer not to associate with, all who share consciousness in the creation. In short, yourself. The Creator is yourself. As you are angry at the Creator, so you become angry at yourself. And again we say to you, be angry at yourself. You can take it.

Face those things that make you angry straight on, he urges, never blinking. For this is your school. This is where you will learn compassion, balance, and understanding of love. This is where you will learn who you are. This is the only understanding that matters, and you cannot come to it by blinking at those things that make you frustrated or angry or fearful.

Before you condemn yourselves totally, he says, look with solemnity and joy upon the work of your hearts and your hands. So many beings have turned toward the light, toward love and service, and veritably shine, that much that could have been terrible upon your planet has been softened. Light groups such as this one have aided enormously. Catastrophes, including nuclear war, that seemed almost inevitable a year ago, seem less inevitable now. You think you do nothing through your meditations, through your smiles, through noticing the difficulties of others. But the planetary consciousness is changed by such acts of conscious positivity.

Then comes a passage of pure poetry, on the polar nature of creation. The perfect symbol of love, the rose, is surrounded with thorns, Hatonn says. The creation is a creation of polar opposites. The one without the other would not be complete. Cherish, then, the rose. Avoid the thorns, but recognize them and love them as part of the rose. Look at the pearl and cherish it, but respect also the terrible irritation of sand which a small animal had to bear in order to build up this beauteous substance. Bless the rain as it falls sweetly upon the dry land, but know also that in order for rain to fall, there must be a particle of dust.

The second half of the session turns to wonder. Hatonn asks the group to consider the miracle of the ordinary day. The physical vehicle itself, each muscle and tendon moving in obedience to your wishes. The food you ate this day. Whence came it? In what earth did it grow? What hands harvested it, shipped it, unpacked it, prepared it, and served it to you? What a miraculous chain of love and service exists that you may eat. And yet how many have said this day, what a rainy day, what a terrible day. Never lose sight of the fact that you are doing the impossible, he says. You are aware, in such a complex fashion, of so many things in such an infinite creation filled with such beauty that it simply seems impossible. And yet it is simple. It is love. And it is one.

And then Hatonn makes a confession that reframes everything the group thought they knew about him. We of Hatonn, he says, have never experienced many of the complex emotions you take for granted. We have recently learned that this is part of our lesson, that we are to grow from our contact with your race. For us it is equivalent, he says, to a person going from being color-blind to perceiving color. We are overjoyed at the depth of emotion we can now perceive. Even the painful ones, disheartenment, jealousy, envy, greed, each is merely a convolution, a defective form of love, and we are able to perceive the crystal teardrop of love within the experience, and rejoice in that feeling.

When we of Hatonn are able, through your hearts and eyes, through your tears and your touch, to experience that which you call love, he says, our joy is boundless. We love you. You are our brothers and sisters. Our world is enriched from the experience of knowing you.

So the evening that began with permission to be angry at the Creator ends with the Creator's messengers thanking us for teaching them how to feel. Be angry when you must. He can take it. Face the thorns, honor the sand, bless the dust. And know that your smallest kindnesses are changing the consciousness of the planet.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Seed Time
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the seed time.

This session was recorded three days after Christmas, and Latwii opens with the season itself. The light of this particular time of year, he says, is so bright that it is harsh to many of your peoples. There are many who will leave this incarnation in this season. There are others who are unhappy, or sick, or sick at heart, or uncertain. If you are among the fortunate who have been caught up in the joy of the celebration, he asks, give your especial meditation and your sending of light to those about you whom you may or may not know. Simply share the Creator with them by holding the love and the light of the Creator in your heart and releasing it to the world's use. This is all you need to do. You do not need to know details.

I love the modesty of that instruction. You do not need to know details. You do not need a plan for anyone's salvation. Hold the light in your heart and release it. That is the whole of the work.

Then Latwii turns to the deeper rhythm underneath the holiday, the rhythm of winter itself. We say to you, my friends, you are under the earth. This is your time of growing, of knowing and realizing who you are. This is, in your cycle of seasons, the winter, the quiet time. Therefore bring quiet to your souls as they rest in the darkness of the earth, gathering the strength to move and to blossom in season. This is the time to be patient with yourself. This is the time to feel the light within rather than looking for the light without. This is the seed time.

You may look at this earth time as a prison, he says, for indeed it is not a time wherein your being can make the transformations of color and harmony that it will make in its season. However, you have the key to that prison, and that key once used opens the door to more color and more harmony than you shall ever experience as manifestation. As you meditate in your seed time, as you discover the love that is your essence, realize the source of that love, the original Thought that created that love, and revel in the harmony and the beauty and the blooming of that reality.

Your manifestations, he says, can only occur in as much fullness as you prepare for at this time, by the strength and the solidarity with which you ground yourself in your own being. The blossom is decided underground, in the dark, in the quiet. What flowers in the spring was determined by the patience of the winter.

The rest of the session is fragmentary, much of it lost to inaudible passages on the tape, but two things survive intact. A voice speaking through the channel, calling the group his children, asks them to husband the creation in which they walk, and to wait the precious gift of their love as it wakes toward the kingdom of love. And Latwii, in a broken passage about desire, leaves a thought I want to preserve. Pray, he seems to say, not for ends but for growth. Not for sights but for lights. Not for ease but for strength. For of such is the road to the kingdom constructed.

Not for ends but for growth. That may be the whole teaching of the seed time in a single line. The seed does not pray to be a flower by morning. It prays, if seeds pray, for the strength to split its own husk when the season comes. Be patient with yourself. Feel the light within. Rest in the darkness of the earth, and gather your strength to blossom.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are a Star
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are a star.

This is the last session of the year, recorded on New Year's Eve, and Latwii arrives in a mood I can only call tender. He is amazed, he says, at the people in the room. We do not understand how you can overcome so much and love so much, he tells them, for we are beginning to understand the limitations of your sphere of illusion, and we are amazed that you are able to deal with it as well as you do, given the limitations of your senses.

Jim asks the question of the evening. How can he and his companions best serve the planet and fulfill their mission? Latwii's answer cuts through every grand plan they might have been forming. You have one mission above all others, he says, and that is, as you already know, to realize your true nature.

As it happens, he says, the three of them have arrived at a rare position. The mirror in which they look to determine their true character is a true mirror, given support by those who will not lie to them or give them a false image. This is true of each of them. And as they work together, that will be their chief work: the improvement of the understanding of their own personality, and the disciplines necessary to complete that understanding. Each will help the other. Each will learn. This is the most important task. The other tasks are within their free will, and of those he cannot speak.

Then a questioner brings a painful personal dilemma, torn between the group and her family, afraid that choosing will break harmony somewhere. Latwii's answer is one of the most liberating in the archive. You must realize, he says, that you are a completely free entity. You must detach yourself from all supposed entanglements, including those of your family and those of the group. You are a star. Your radiance lights many. Your decisions must be made on the basis of your ability to shine, and that which causes you to be able to function properly.

Center yourself, he says, without reference to those who would pull upon you and ask you to play roles. You do not play a role. You are an eternal spirit and you have your work. Determine what you can best do to help, in the most high sense that you know. You may be mistaken in practice, but it will matter less than you fear, because your intention was of the highest nature. When one's intention is consistently of the highest, the fruits will be known upon the planes that affect the thought forms of this planet, and eventually they will come back to you in such a way that these problems will disappear.

You cannot live in anyone else's understanding of life, he says. It must be your own. Whatever service you feel is the highest, do.

Toward the end of the evening, Latwii offers the group a wish for the new year, and I want to give it to you as he gave it to them. A wish that the love and the light of the infinite Creator might light the way that each of you travel as you journey homeward, and that that light might shine upon each you meet on this journey, and that the light of the recognition of the Creator in each face might remain where you have passed, to illuminate the way for others to travel that same path homeward.

And then his closing counsel, simple enough to carry into any year. Pay no attention to what others say. Remain simple. Remain humble. In whatever situation you find yourself, radiate the Creator, and know that you are doing your Father's work and not your own. That, he says, is the key to simplicity, contentment, and understanding.

So be it for the year ahead. But let it be the Creator's year. Remain simple, loving, charitable, kind, and above all humble, for that is the key to a pure channel. You are a star. Your radiance lights many. Shine, and let the rest take care of itself.

Thank you for listening.

title: You Are Seeing Love
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: you are seeing love.

This one opens with a large group gathered in meditation, and the voice that comes through first belongs to one called Laitos. He is almost surprised by the size of the crowd. He says it does them good to feel their work land somewhere. And then he gives them the whole of the teaching in a single word.

Love. Not as a feeling that visits now and then, but as the original Thought that made everything. He says it straight out: the original Thought that created all that there is, is love. And this simple and consuming fire is the fire of creation, the fire of change, of transformation, and of infinity. There is no end to love.

I love how plain he makes it. We do not have a complex story to tell, he says. We speak one word, and that is love.

He knows we hear that word and think we know it already. So he walks it around the room. You may think of love in many ways, he says. Many words in many languages have tried to express the fullness of the original Thought, because love is all that there is. Not mostly. Not nearly. All.

Then comes the line that became tonight's title, and I think it is one of the finest sentences in the whole archive. Look into the face of the one next to you, he says. You are seeing love. Maybe the mirror has been distorted. Maybe sometimes the face beside yours does not know it is a face of love. But there is no consciousness that is not love.

He does not stop there. You cannot flee from love, he says. You cannot be separated from love, because you are love. Love is closer to you than your body. Each breath is farther from your being than love is. Read that again slowly and let it land.

What I find most moving is his claim about who benefits when they come to speak. We would think the group is the lucky one, receiving this message. But Laitos says the gifts the seekers give them are infinitely precious, because helping others deepens their own understanding of love, and it is through that understanding that they themselves are trying to refine what they call wisdom. Love they have, he says. Wisdom they are seeking.

Later that same evening another voice, Latwii, takes questions. A woman asks about the Earth, and how the planet's people have abused it, and whether they have to deal with such abuse where they are. And Latwii answers with unusual tenderness. You are encased in a heavy chemical vehicle, he says. You cannot hear the flowers and the trees speak, nor understand the song of the wind. It is not apparent to many that each part of the creation dwells in service.

So what do you do, he asks back, when you can see the abuse and others cannot? His answer is small and practical, and I think it fits perfectly after Laitos. Do what you can. Feel what you can. Love as best you can. That is a great deal in the third density.

There is a promise near the end of Laitos that I want to leave you with. He says that all your questions, if you follow them far enough, dissolve. Not into answers, exactly. All questions dissolve, he says, into a dying fall, as they reach the ocean of infinite and all-encompassing love. That is where this evening ends. Not with a teaching to memorize, but with an ocean to fall into.

Thank you for listening.

title: Every Last Being
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: every last being.

This transcript is short and strange, and it comes from an advanced meeting where the channel was not even named in the record. The voice is Hatonn. And the message he brings that morning is, frankly, startling. He says they are preparing to speak to the whole planet through its own machines.

They call it a new mode, a new vehicle. In the near future, he says, they will be using your radio communication to influence, without infringing on free will, the thinking of those who listen. Messages will be substituted into the programming. Images will appear on television that have no other explainable source than their transmission. He admits this is a surprise to everyone, including the channel himself.

Now, before your mind runs to science fiction, listen to why. He gives the reason plainly. The time of listening and considering grows short. The time of the great changes that your cultures and religions and folk stories have long spoken of is close at hand. And they are pledged, he says, to provide this message of love to every last being upon your planet.

That is the heart of it, and that is tonight's title. Not to the wise. Not to the willing. To every last being. Each is of the fold of the Father, he says, and each must have the opportunity to finally decide whether to return to the fold or to continue on a path that takes them further from the unity that is the birthright of each within the creation.

I want to sit with that word, fold. It is not a courtroom. It is not an exam hall. It is where the sheep are kept warm at night. The image is not of judgment but of homecoming. And the choice, he insists, belongs entirely to each entity. They will shake the perceptions of those who view these signs only so far as to provoke internal questioning, followed by internal seeking. Nothing more. The seeking itself cannot be forced.

He is honest about the cost of this plan, too. He says it will be unavoidable, in such cases, to infringe on the rights of some who will witness these events. They have considered this carefully, and they are willing to take these actions in the hope that opening the hearts and minds and souls of the few who are still able to seek inwardly will give those entities the opportunities they so richly deserve.

What stays with me is the humility underneath the grandness of the claim. These are beings who say they can rearrange your radio stations, and yet they keep returning to the same small truth. Their message has never changed. It is the simple message of love and understanding. All the machinery, all the new modes, are only so that this one simple thing might reach one more ear.

And there is a line near the end that steadies the whole strange session. They wish, he says, to make the relationship between peoples such as yourselves and us more concrete, so that you may begin to share some of the more inner teachings: about your relationship to your own identity, your relationship to others, and both of your relationships to the Creator.

A strange transmission, then. But strip away the strangeness and it is the same vow you will hear across hundreds of these sessions. To every last being. The love will be offered. What is done with it is up to you.

Thank you for listening.

title: Fools for the Creator
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: fools for the creator.

The voice tonight is Laitos, and he opens with a story. He warns you first that he is going to call someone a fool, and then he tells you who.

Once, he says, in the past of your planet, a man came from a small town in a poor country, proclaiming that he could hear the words and the voice of a father who existed in another realm than his own physical, visible father. His neighbors knew he was crazy, because this was not the way the universe worked. Still the man persisted. He claimed that his father, of all things, was everyone's father, and that for this reason everyone was brothers and sisters.

You know what happened next. He was ridiculed, shamed, cursed, and eventually beaten. His friends abandoned him. His countrymen killed him. And then, Laitos says with what I can only hear as dry satisfaction, as if intent on making matters worse, he came back and continued his foolishness.

And then Laitos asks the question that turns the whole story inside out. Who but a fool, he says, could step out into oblivion and trust the truth to bear him up? Who but a fool would risk his earthly life in the belief that more existed than earthly life? And again, who but a fool would trust in an invisible father?

Listen to how he lands it. We of Laitos are thankful for your foolishness, he says, for the universe is desperately short of such fools. We would encourage you to trust in your foolishness, to step off the precipice into space and rely upon your foolish belief that what is real will bear you up and sustain you and maintain your real life.

This is not a call to be careless. A little later, through another channel, Laitos adds a tenderness that balances the dare. In the beginning of your seeking, he says, do not speak of your path in great detail to others. Seedlings are fragile until they have taken root. Keep your new understandings nurtured quietly and carefully, as a small plant in a hotbed, until each step becomes firm enough to push off from onto the next.

There is also a gift from Latwii that evening, in answer to a question about the value of humor. And his answer is one of my favorites in the archive. Laughter, he says, is one outward expression of the basic ecstasy or joy of the universe. The energy that is love. Laughter is available to all. Laughter is a healing, comforting, lovely energy, and indeed one of the most highly prized of all states of being. We find the universe to be full of the laughter, or the song, of joy.

So tonight's foolishness has two faces: the courage to step off the cliff, and the laughter that rings through the universe while you fall. Both, they say, are forms of the same trust. Both are ways of saying that what is real will catch you.

Thank you for listening.

title: Know Your Own Center
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: know your own center.

The evening of January eighteenth opens with a rare visitor. Oxal does not speak through this group often, and he uses his few minutes to give them a single image. He says: think of a spinning top, or a gyroscope. There is always a center that lets the whirling stay balanced. And then he gives the image its meaning. As you are light beings, he says, the energy which spins you is called love. So seek, in your meditation, always to know your own center.

It is a small message. It takes about two minutes to deliver. And then Latwii picks it up and spends the whole evening unfolding it, the way you might unfold a map.

Latwii starts with a confession that stops me every time I read it. It is interesting to us, he says, that so many of the events of your lives seem to revolve not around your own central axis of love, but around an avoidance of love. We find this difficult to understand, he says, both how you are able to accomplish it and why you are willing to attempt it.

Think about that as a description of an ordinary week. Not revolving around love. Revolving around the avoidance of it. The careful scheduling, the managed impressions, the things left unsaid. He is not scolding. He sounds genuinely puzzled, the way you might be puzzled watching someone drink salt water to quench their thirst.

And then the gyroscope returns, sharpened. How can a spinning top revolve around an axis outside its perimeter, he asks. It is impossible. Yet so many of your people continue to attempt this. If enough of them do it, he warns, the whole planet wobbles. Your planet, its people, are out of balance. And if they do not choose consciously to return to their given axis, then a new axis will be found.

There is a gentler thread in the same evening, and I want to give it room, because it answers the heaviness of the warning. Latwii speaks of the mystery that remains inside every experience, even the ones you think you have fully understood. That remaining mystery, he says, is not a defect. Those things which remain a mystery are equally as valuable as the things that can be known, for they teach seeking. And wisdom must always include seeking.

Listen to how he puts the relationship between love and mystery. Love, he says, grows more fully by its residence in the same experience with mystery. The unanswered part of your life is not proof that you have failed to learn. It is the part that draws you forward into the next adventure, the next learning.

So the teaching of the evening holds together like the gyroscope itself. Find your center, which is love. Let the mystery spin around it without frightening you. The wobble you feel is not a sign you are broken. It is a sign you are still learning how to spin true.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Unquenchable Spirit
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the unquenchable spirit.

Laitos speaks first on the evening of January twenty first, and he begins by reassuring the group about the nature of love itself. Because love, he says, can seem as fragile as a newborn rose in the snow. Beautiful, but transient. You hold it, you lose it, you grieve it. And he wants you to know that this fragility is an illusion.

The rose may wither, he says. The preserved odor may fade. But the memory and the knowledge of that beauty is as infinite as your being. You hold each perception within you, and you assign to it the value that seems proper. Look then to each moment, he says, for in even the most difficult or confused circumstance, love resides. And not as a fragile thing, but as the very heart of your experience.

He returns to this at the close, and the closing is even stronger. It may seem that love can be shattered, he says. It may seem that love can be damaged. It may seem that misunderstandings and confusions can cause harm. If this be so, my friends, then you must search more deeply in your understanding for the essence of love, for naught can undo its everlasting beauty and strength.

I love that old word, naught. Nothing can undo it. Not the argument. Not the distance. Not the years. The power of your being and the power of the universe are one thing, he says, and that thing is love.

There is a humility woven through this session that I do not want to skip. Laitos tells the group that the gifts they give him are infinitely precious. Love, he says, they have. Wisdom they are seeking. And it is through helping others deepen their understanding of love that they refine their own wisdom. The teacher is being taught by the teaching. I think there is something deeply honest about a voice from beyond that admits it is still a student.

Later, Latwii takes up a question that reaches the group by letter, from a woman in Denver, about ill health in her family. She cannot lift her loved ones' afflictions, and she wants to know what ill health means. Is it a chosen path, or a body failing to find balance?

Latwii answers carefully. Health, as your culture defines it, is a narrow idea, he says: every part working smoothly, complete vitality at all times. But catalyst is the purpose of this density, not comfort. Sometimes, he says, when the mind is unable or unwilling to face the lesson of the moment, the lesson is passed on to the body, where in its symbolic form it might be pondered and unraveled.

And sometimes the reason runs deeper than one lifetime. An entity who once gave love abundantly but never let love be given to it, he says, might choose before incarnation a body that needs care, so that it might finally learn to receive. These are great lessons, he says, lessons that could well take an entire incarnation to assimilate.

Put the two halves of the evening together and you get tonight's title. Love is the unquenchable spirit. It cannot be shattered, only misunderstood for a while. And the body, even in its breaking, may be carrying a lesson the soul chose on purpose. Nothing here is fragile. Nothing here is wasted.

Thank you for listening.

title: All Roads Lead to Rome
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: all roads lead to rome.

Two voices share the evening of January twenty fifth, and between them they answer one of the oldest questions a seeker can ask. What if I chose my path before I was born, and what if I am blowing it?

Hatonn speaks first, briefly, and his message is almost entirely about meditation. Not as a technique, he says, but as a different way of knowing. Avail yourself in meditation, he says, and begin to know without speaking. Begin to see without looking. Begin to hear without listening. That small voice that is all and ever present is not only without you, he says. It is within you. For it is all things, and you are all things.

I love that sequence. Know without speaking. See without looking. Hear without listening. It is the whole spiritual path compressed into three impossible instructions, and he means them literally.

Then Latwii takes the questions, and a man asks about something that has been troubling him since the week before. Someone he knew suffered terrible losses: a death on a wedding day, a child killed. How can suffering like that be part of any plan? Did this person program their own catastrophe?

Latwii answers with an image I have never forgotten. Consider yourself on the floor of a terminal building, he says. You are planning a trip. You look at the schedules and you decide your destination. You may go a short distance, conveniently. Or you may decide to go a very long distance, and the difficulty of getting there may be quite great. You choose your destination. And that destination, in spiritual terms, is the sum total of lessons you wish yourself to learn.

You plan it before you are born, he says. Then you incarnate and forget. And during the trip it is extremely unlikely you will remember picking such a destination, especially if it turns out to be difficult. So the problems, the losses, the limitations you meet are preprogrammed by yourselves, so that you may learn whatever lessons these difficulties cause you to face more squarely.

But here is the part that matters for the man asking, and for anyone who has watched someone suffer and felt helpless. You cannot miss your lesson permanently, he says. Many, many times you will decide not to learn a particular lesson, and the lesson immediately returns in another form. You are never hopelessly lost. And then he borrows a phrase from the channel's own mind: all roads lead to Rome. If you miss a turn, there is always another turning that will bring you back to the correct path.

And for the one whose suffering seems far out of proportion, he offers this startling image. You see a person who has chosen to go from New York to Tanganyika by ark. This is difficult, he says, but the lessons are rewarding. In the life of the soul, that is what is important, not the ease of the journey.

From New York to Tanganyika by ark. Not by plane. By ark. I think about that line whenever I am tempted to measure a life by how smooth it looks from the outside. The difficulty was the choice. The difficulty was the point.

Thank you for listening.

title: Seekers, Not Knowers
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: seekers, not knowers.

The evening of January twenty eighth opens with Hatonn speaking against what he calls a backdrop of unimaginable immensity and scale. He wants you to hold the size of it in your mind while he says the smallest thing. And the smallest thing is this: we do not ask you to believe.

Listen to how he puts it, because I think it is one of the most important passages in the early archive. We of the Confederation do not ask you to believe, he says. We ask you to question. We do not pretend to have the answers, although we do have information to share. We are not those who know. We are those who seek.

Seekers, not knowers. That is the whole of their authority, stated honestly. When they speak to you, he says, they ask you to join them in that seeking. Not against the backdrop of the limits your people have defined for seeking, but against the backdrop of the infinite creation. This one Creator, he says, is the very core of each and every thing that exists. Each ear that hears these words is part of the Creator. We are one being.

It is worth pausing on what this means for everything else you hear in this series. They will tell you extraordinary things across hundreds of sessions. And their own instruction, from the start, is to take what is useful and toss away the rest without a second thought. Belief was never the assignment. Seeking was.

Later that night, Latwii takes a question that fits the evening perfectly. Is meditation the best way to get in contact with the higher self, a woman asks, and does the higher self express itself through meditation?

Latwii answers with characteristic care. Meditation, he says, is the most accessible way for most of the people of your planet to obtain contact with their inner being, their higher self, and the many guides which wait upon the seeking of the seeker. Whether it is the best way cannot be said for certain. Many ways there are. But many steps of preparation are necessary for the other techniques, so meditation is the most accessible means at this time.

And how does the higher self speak, once you are listening? Intuition is one of the many means, he says. Intuition, dreams, meditation, hunches, sudden insights. These are the techniques utilized to make contact with those of you who, for the most part, are unable to receive a contact from the inner planes by any conscious means.

I love the ordinariness of that list. Not visions. Not voices from the sky. Hunches. The sudden insight in the shower. The dream you almost dismiss at breakfast. The higher self, it turns out, mostly whispers in the most familiar voice you own: your own.

So the evening comes full circle. Do not believe, they say. Question. Seek. And the seeking itself has a doorway, and the doorway is the quietest thing in your day. Sit down. Be still. Listen for the whisper. That is the whole method, and they have never pretended it was more complicated than that.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Hillside and the Marketplace
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the hillside and the marketplace.

On the fourth of February, Hatonn gives the group one of the most beautiful guided images in the early archive. It is about work. Not spiritual work, set apart and special. Ordinary work. The daily grind. And he begins with a claim that might sting a little.

It was intended by the Creator, he says, that you might experience your so-called work as a form of meditation, and as an experience of love. It has been said, to work is to pray. For those lucky enough to have found occupations that feed the spirit as well as the body, this is in the deepest sense true. But for so many, he says, the connection between daily life and love, between action and meditation, is not apparent.

So he offers a way back, and it starts not with the work but with the meditation. To move from one consciousness to another, he says, is like mounting a great hillside. At the bottom of the hillside is vanity, pollution, pettiness, and distraction. You climb in your spirit's garment, and you can feel that the garment is soiled from everything you have touched that you perceived as unclean.

And then the image opens up. You remove the garment, he says, and cleanse yourself in the waters falling down the hillside in a lovely waterfall, brilliant and iridescent as it sprays the rocks, the moss, and the grass. Leaning into the water, you begin to see the purity of your true being. You take up a fresh garment, a new washed linen, and you move onward until you sit at the top of the hillside.

The air about you is warm, he says, and redolent with the scent of wildflowers, pinks and roses and whites, all in profusion about you. And as you settle into meditation, this is your consciousness. This is who you are. All of creation breathes with you and desires to be of service to you, and you in turn offer up the rhythms of your body, your mind, and your spirit in service to this beautiful place, loving and delighting in its beauty, its purity, and its gentle ever-present strength.

But here is the turn that makes this more than a pleasant visualization. You do not stay on the hillside. Yes, my friends, he says, you come down again into the marketplace, where you live the illusion, where your lessons collect. But you bring with you an unsoiled garment, a cleanliness of soul, and a new vision that begins to see the top of the hillside beneath the soiled garment of all labor, all conditions, and all relationships.

The marketplace is where you live. The hillside is where you remember. And the practice is the daily commute between them.

He closes with a line for everyone who has ever come down from a beautiful meditation and failed, within the hour, to live up to it. We ask that you never be discouraged, he says, if you fail to manifest what you have learned in your meditations. For this is the work of your life: to find who you are. That is, to find the Creator. That one great original Thought which is love.

And his very last image of the night stays with me. I leave you on a hillside, he says, gazing forth into a world of illusion, a world in which each illusion has a central core of purity and love. Your mission is, impossible though it may seem, to find it.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Enchanted Forest
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the enchanted forest.

On the eighth of March, Hatonn tells the group a parable. He says it plainly: once again we shall tell you a parable, so that you may turn in your mind another facet of the understanding of love and its workings in your life as you live it at this time.

Imagine yourself, he says, as a young man at the dawn of adulthood, contemplating with some despair the difficulties and limitations of responsibility. Imagine then a guide coming to this young man and saying: come with me, and I shall show you the alternative to your difficulties and your limitations.

The young man wakes in an enchanted forest. He is cold, and wishes himself better clothed, and immediately he is garbed in a warm and comfortable garment. He wonders if there might be water, and a brook gurgles at his feet. Recklessly he thinks, well, I will just think myself a house, and there it is, a comfortable furnished cabin. Outside he finds beehives, gardens, everything as he would wish it to be.

And it is many days before this young man begins to realize that he is not happy in this tremendous freedom from limitation and from responsibility. It is not many more days than that before he recalls his guardian. Great being, he says, you have shown me what it is to be free of responsibility and limitation, and I now understand. I wish to go back.

And back he is, Hatonn says, in a world with responsibilities, sometimes of a crushing nature, of limitations of all kinds, and other people. I love the dryness of that ending. And other people. As if other people were the final, unavoidable item on the list of limitations.

Then Hatonn draws the moral, and it is not the one you might expect. Cherish each other, he says, and understand that in each entity you view the Creator. It is a responsibility to live in such a world, but it is an honor to be able to share woe and joy alike with your fellow beings, in a common understanding that you are one with the Creator, a Creator of infinite love.

A responsibility, yes. But an honor. The weight is the gift. That is the whole parable in four words.

So how do you keep this in mind, he asks, as your back bends under responsibilities you may not wish to bear? His answer is the one he gives in almost every session, and I never tire of hearing it. Time spent in meditation, he says, is time spent out of time, and in the kingdom of heaven. These moments are with you through the days. As you need them, you may call upon them, if you but will.

Later in the evening he gives the practice its image. Think of your daily meditation as a fire, he says, a light which burns within your being and illuminates it, burning brighter as you feed it the fuel of your attention. Burning brighter, he says, until those around you notice a change in your very being, and are inspired by the light that shines from your words, your thoughts, your actions.

The forest was enchanted, but it was empty. The world of responsibility is heavy, but it is full: full of other people, full of the Creator wearing their faces. Tonight's teaching is simple. Go back. It is an honor to be here.

Thank you for listening.

title: The Runaway Freight Train
transcript:
Voices from the Archive. Tonight: the runaway freight train.

Hatonn opens the session of March twenty second with an image borrowed, he admits, from the channel's own mind. Many of you, he says, feel as though you are on a runaway freight train.
